5. Geodesics on a submanifold

This chapter builds the geometry of \(N \subseteq V\) used in Chapters 6–10: geodesics, the exponential map, Theorem 10.4, Corollary 10.7, the distance \(\rho\) and Theorem 10.9 at one point. \(N\) need not be closed, compact or connected; everything is computed in \(V\). Abstract connections, parallel transport and Lemmas 8.1–8.7, the symmetries and sectional curvature of §9, metric completeness, Corollary 10.10 and the Hopf–Rinow equivalence are not needed.

5.1 The second fundamental form

Recall [V6.1, §1.4]: \(P_q\) is the orthogonal projection onto \(T_qN\), and for \(F : N \to E\), \(dF_q = dG_q\) on \(T_qN\) whenever \(G : V \to E\) is differentiable at \(q\) and equals \(F\) on \(N\) near \(q\). A slice chart \(\sigma\) has the parametrization \(x(u) = \sigma^{-1}(u, 0)\), and \(T_{x(u)}N = \operatorname{ran} dx_u\) [V1.6, §1.4].

Proposition (the projection is smooth) [V6.2]. For injective linear \(A\) from a finite-dimensional space to \(V\), \(\Pi(A) = A(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is the orthogonal projection onto \(\operatorname{ran} A\), smooth in \(A\) Chapter6/ProjectioncontDiffAt_gramProj. So \(Q_\sigma(y) = \Pi(dx_{(\sigma y)_1})\) is smooth near \(N \cap \operatorname{dom}\sigma\) and equals \(P_y\) on \(N\), and \(q \mapsto P_q\) is smooth Chapter6/ProjectionprojRep Chapter6/ProjectioncontMDiff_tanProj. (\(A^{\mathsf T}A\) is invertible; \(dx_u\) is injective as \(\sigma \circ x = (\,\cdot\,, 0)\).)

Let \(D_v = dP_q(v)\); for tangent \(v\), \(D_v = dQ_\sigma(v)\).

Proposition (the second fundamental form) [V6.12]. Put \(\mathrm{II}_q(v, w) = D_vw\) Chapter6/SubmanifoldsecondFundForm. Each \(D_v\) is self-adjoint; for \(v \in T_qN\), \(D_v\) maps \(T_qN\) into \(T_qN^\perp\) and \(T_qN^\perp\) into \(T_qN\); and \(\mathrm{II}_q\) is symmetric on \(T_qN\) Chapter6/Submanifoldinner_secondFundForm_comm Chapter6/SubmanifoldsecondFundForm_comm.

Proof. Differentiate \(P^* = P\) and \(P^2 = P\): \(D_vP_q + P_qD_v = D_v\), so \(P_qD_vP_q = 0\) and \(P_qD_v\nu = D_v\nu\) for normal \(\nu\). Symmetry: with \(g = (\sigma\,\cdot)_2\), \(T_xN = \ker dg_x\) on \(N\), so \(dg_y \circ Q_\sigma(y) = 0\) on \(N\) near \(q\); differentiating along tangent \(a\) and applying to tangent \(b\), \(d^2g_q(a, b) + dg_q\,\mathrm{II}_q(a, b) = 0\). So \(\mathrm{II}_q(a, b) - \mathrm{II}_q(b, a)\) lies in \(\ker dg_q = T_qN\), and is normal. \(\square\)

Definition (curvature) [V6.17]. \(R_q(x, y) = D_yD_x - D_xD_y\), i.e. \(R_q(x, y)z = \mathrm{II}_q(y, \mathrm{II}_q(x, z)) - \mathrm{II}_q(x, \mathrm{II}_q(y, z))\) Chapter6/SubmanifoldcurvOp, Milnor’s \(R\) with his sign. It is tangent for tangent arguments, \(D_y\) mapping the normal \(\mathrm{II}_q(x, z)\) to \(T_qN\) Chapter6/SubmanifoldcurvOp_mem.

Proposition (the Gauss equation) [V6.18]. \(\langle R_q(x, y)z, w\rangle = \langle\mathrm{II}_q(x, z), \mathrm{II}_q(y, w)\rangle - \langle\mathrm{II}_q(x, w), \mathrm{II}_q(y, z)\rangle\) for \(x, y, z, w \in V\), by self-adjointness Chapter6/Submanifoldinner_curvOp.

5.2 Differential equations

Fact (Theorem 10.1) [V7.4] (standard). (a) Continuous maps into a Hausdorff space that agree at a point of an open interval \(s\), and near each point of \(s\) where they agree, agree on \(s\) Chapter7/ODEeqOn_of_eventuallyEq. (b) Solutions of \(x' = G(x)\) that agree at \(t_0\) agree near \(t_0\) if \(G\) is \(C^1\) at their value, and on a whole interval if they stay in an open set where \(G\) is \(C^1\) Chapter7/ODEode_eventuallyEq Chapter7/ODEode_eqOn. (c) If \(G\) is smooth on an open \(U \ni x_1\) of a finite-dimensional space, a smooth \(\varphi\) and \(r, \tau > 0\) satisfy \(\varphi(0, x) = x\), \(\varphi(t, x) \in U\), \(\partial_t\varphi(t, x) = G(\varphi(t, x))\) for \(\|x - x_1\| < r\), \(|t| < \tau\) Chapter7/ODEexists_localFlow. Proof idea. (b): Grönwall, then (a). (c): the flow [V1.14, §2.2] of \(G\) times a bump function.

Fact (linear equations) [V6.7] (standard). For continuous \(A : \mathbb R \to \operatorname{End}(E)\), solutions of \(x' = A(t)x\) on an open interval, or on \(\mathbb R\), that agree once agree everywhere Chapter6/LinearODElinearODE_eqOn Chapter6/LinearODElinearODE_eq. (Grönwall, \(A\) being bounded on compact intervals.)

5.3 Geodesics

Definition (geodesics) [V7.1]. For open \(s \subseteq \mathbb R\), \(\gamma : \mathbb R \to V\) is a geodesic on \(s\) if it is \(C^\infty\) on \(s\), \(\gamma(s) \subseteq N\), and \(\gamma''(t) \perp T_{\gamma(t)}N\) on \(s\) Chapter7/GeodesicIsGeodesicOn; constants in \(N\) are geodesics. A curve in \(N\) near \(t\) has \(c'(t) \in T_{c(t)}N\) if differentiable at \(t\), since \((\sigma \circ c)_2 = 0\) near \(t\) Chapter7/GeodesichasDerivAt_mem_tangentSubspace. So \(\gamma' \in T_\gamma N\) and \(P_\gamma\gamma'' = 0\): Milnor’s \(\frac{D}{dt}\frac{d\gamma}{dt} = 0\) Chapter7/GeodesicIsGeodesicOn.tanProj_deriv_deriv. Being a geodesic is local Chapter7/MinimalisGeodesicOn_of_locally.

Proposition (the geodesic equation) [V7.3]. (i) A geodesic satisfies \(\gamma'' = \mathrm{II}_\gamma(\gamma', \gamma')\) Chapter7/GeodesicIsGeodesicOn.deriv_deriv_eq. (ii) For a slice chart with parametrization \(x\) on \(T_\sigma \subseteq Z\), let \(A^+ = (A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\Gamma(u)(w) = (dx_u)^+d^2x_u(w, w)\). The field \((u, w) \mapsto (w, -\Gamma(u)(w))\) is smooth on \(T_\sigma \times Z\), and if \((u, w)\) is a \(C^\infty\) solution on an open \(s\) with \(u(s) \subseteq T_\sigma\), then \(x \circ u\) is a geodesic on \(s\) Chapter7/GeodesicLocalcontDiffOn_chartSpray Chapter7/GeodesicLocalisGeodesicOn_chart.

Proof. (i) Differentiate \(Q_\sigma(\gamma)\gamma' = \gamma'\): \(D_{\gamma'}\gamma' + P\gamma'' = \gamma''\). (ii) \((x \circ u)'' = (1 - \Pi(dx_u))\,d^2x_u(w, w)\) is normal. \(\square\)

Theorem (uniqueness) [V7.5]. Geodesics on open sets containing \(t_0\) with equal position and velocity at \(t_0\) agree near \(t_0\), and on all of a common open interval Chapter7/GeodesicIsGeodesicOn.eventuallyEq Chapter7/GeodesicIsGeodesicOn.eqOn.

Proof. With \(Q = Q_\sigma\) at \(\gamma_1(t_0)\), \(G(x, v) = (v, dQ_x(v)v)\) is smooth, and since \(D_v = dQ(v)\) along \(N\), both lifts \((\gamma_i, \gamma_i')\) solve \(z' = G(z)\) near \(t_0\) by [V7.3, §5.3]; apply [V7.4, §5.2] (b), then (a). \(\square\)

Proposition (constant speed, homogeneity) [V7.2]. For a geodesic on \(s\), \(\frac{d}{dt}\|\gamma'\|^2 = 2\langle\gamma'', \gamma'\rangle = 0\), so the speed is constant on intervals Chapter7/GeodesicIsGeodesicOn.norm_deriv_eq; and \(t \mapsto \gamma(at + b)\) is a geodesic on \(\{t : at + b \in s\}\) for all \(a, b \in \mathbb R\) Chapter7/GeodesicIsGeodesicOn.comp_mul_add.

Lemma 10.2 [V7.6]. For \(q_0 \in N\) there are an open \(U \ni q_0\), \(\varepsilon > 0\) and \(\Theta\) smooth on \(U \times B(0, \varepsilon) \times (-2, 2)\) such that for \(p \in N \cap U\) and \(v \in T_pN\), \(\|v\| < \varepsilon\), \(\Theta(p, v, \cdot)\) is the geodesic on \((-2, 2)\) with value \(p\) and velocity \(v\) at \(0\) (unique there) Chapter7/GeodesicLocallemma_10_2.

Proof. [V7.4, §5.2] (c) for the chart field at \((u_0, 0)\), \(u_0 = (\sigma q_0)_1\), gives a flow \(\varphi\) with \(r, \tau\). By quadratic homogeneity of \(\Gamma\) (Milnor’s rescaling), \(\mathrm{geo}(u, w)(t) = x\big((\varphi(ct, (u, w/c)))_1\big)\), \(c = \tau/2\), is for \((u, w) \in B(u_0, r) \times B(0, cr)\) a geodesic on \((-2, 2)\) with initial data \((x(u), dx_uw)\), smooth in \((u, w, t)\) Chapter7/GeodesicLocalLocalSpray.contDiffOn_geo. Put \(\Theta(p, v, t) = \mathrm{geo}((\sigma p)_1, (d\sigma_pv)_1)(t)\) on \(U = \{p : (\sigma p)_1 \in B(u_0, r),\ \|d\sigma_p\| < C\}\), \(C = \|d\sigma_{q_0}\| + 1\), \(\varepsilon = cr/C\). Uniqueness is [V7.5, §5.3]. \(\square\)

5.4 The exponential map

Definition (the exponential map) [V7.7]. \(\gamma\) is a geodesic from \(q\) with velocity \(v\) if it is a geodesic on some \((-\delta, 1 + \delta)\) with \(\gamma(0) = q\), \(\gamma'(0) = v\) Chapter7/ExpIsGeodesicFrom; then \(q \in N\). The domain of \(\exp\) is the set of such \((q, v)\) Chapter7/ExpexpDom, and \(\exp_q(v) = \gamma(1)\) for a chosen such \(\gamma\), \(= q\) off the domain Chapter7/Expexp. By [V7.5, §5.3] and [V7.2, §5.3]: \(\exp_q(v) = \gamma(1)\) for every such \(\gamma\) Chapter7/ExpIsGeodesicFrom.exp_eq; \(\exp_q(0) = q\) for \(q \in N\); and \(t \mapsto \exp_q(tv)\) equals \(\gamma\), hence is a geodesic, on some \((-\delta, 1 + \delta)\) Chapter7/ExpIsGeodesicFrom.isGeodesicOn_exp_smul. Any geodesic on an open interval containing \(0\) and \(1\) is one from \(\gamma(0)\).

Proposition (\(\exp\) near the zero section) [V7.8]. Let \(TN = \{(q, v) : q \in N,\ v \in T_qN\}\) Milnor/Chapter8/TangentBundleProblems.tangentBundleSet. (i) For \(q_0 \in N\) there are an open \(U \ni q_0\), \(\varepsilon > 0\) and \(F\) smooth on \(U \times B(0, \varepsilon)\) with \(\exp_p(v) = F(p, v)\) (and \((p, v)\) in the domain) for \((p, v) \in TN\), \(p \in U\), \(\|v\| < \varepsilon\) Chapter7/Expexists_exp_eq. (ii) An open \(O \subseteq V \times V\) contains every \((q, 0)\), and near each point of \(TN \cap O\), which is in the domain, \(\exp\) is the restriction to \(TN\) of a smooth map Chapter7/Expexists_isOpen_exp. (iii) \(\exp_q : T_qN \to V\) has derivative the inclusion at \(0\) Chapter7/ExphasFDerivAt_exp_zero. Proof. \(F(p, v) = \Theta(p, v, 1)\); \(O = \bigcup U \times B(0, \varepsilon)\); for small \(v\), \(t \mapsto F(q, tv) = \exp_q(tv)\) has velocity \(v\) at \(0\). \(\square\)

Definition (normal coordinates) [V7.9]. Let \(B_\varepsilon(q) = \{v \in T_qN : \|v\| < \varepsilon\}\). Normal coordinates of radius \(\varepsilon\) at \(q\) are open \(O, U \subseteq V\), \(F\) smooth on \(O\) and \(G\) smooth on \(U\), such that each \(v \in B_\varepsilon(q)\) is in \(O\), \((q, v)\) in the domain, \(F(v) = \exp_q(v) \in U\), \(G(\exp_qv) = v\); and each \(y \in N \cap U\) has \(G(y) \in B_\varepsilon(q)\), \(\exp_q(G(y)) = y\) Chapter7/NormalNbhdNormalCoord. \(\varepsilon\) is then a normal radius at \(q\) Chapter7/NormalNbhdIsNormalRadius.

Lemma 10.3 [V7.10]. Each \(p \in N\) has an open \(O \ni p\) and \(\varepsilon > 0\) such that: (1) for \(q_1, q_2 \in N \cap O\), exactly one \(v \in B_\varepsilon(q_1)\) has \(\exp_{q_1}(v) = q_2\); (2) \(v = G(q_1, q_2)\) for a \(G\) smooth on an open \(O_2 \supseteq (N \cap O)^2\); (3) \(\varepsilon\) is a normal radius at every \(q \in N \cap O\) Chapter7/NormalNbhdlemma_10_3. In particular every point has a normal radius Chapter7/NormalNbhdexists_isNormalRadius.

Proof. In the chart at \(p\), \(\exp(x(u), dx_uw) = x(E(u, w))\) with \(E(u, w) = (\varphi(c, (u, w/c)))_1\). Milnor’s \(\Phi(u, w) = (u, E(u, w))\) has derivative \((a, b) \mapsto (a, a + b)\) at \((u_0, 0)\) Chapter7/NormalNbhdLocalSpray.hasFDerivAt_chartF, as \(E(u, 0) = u\) and \(t \mapsto E(u_0, tb)\) has velocity \(b\); by the inverse function theorem Milnor/Chapter1/InverseFunctionContMDiff.isLocalDiffeomorphAt_of_isInvertible_mfderiv it is invertible on a small set \(S \ni (u_0, 0)\), chosen of the form \(\|dx_{z_1}z_2\| < \varepsilon\) near \((u_0, 0)\). Take \(O\) so small that \(((\sigma y)_1, (\sigma y')_1) \in \Phi(S)\) for \(y, y' \in O\). Then \(v = dx\,w\) with \(((\sigma q_1)_1, w) = \Phi^{-1}((\sigma q_1)_1, (\sigma q_2)_1)\) gives (1) and (2), and \(v \mapsto x(E((\sigma q)_1, (d\sigma_qv)_1))\), \(G(q, \cdot)\) are normal coordinates at \(q\). \(\square\)

5.5 Paths, the Gauss lemma, and leaving a normal ball

Definitions (paths, length) [V7.11]. For \(c : \mathbb R \to V\) and \(a \le b\), \(L(c|[a, b]) = \int_a^b\|c'\|\), with \(c' = 0\) where \(c\) is not differentiable Chapter7/PathpathLength. \(c\) is piecewise smooth on \([a, b]\) if continuous there and, for a finite \(B\), \(C^\infty\) on each \([s, t] \subseteq [a, b]\), \(s < t\), with \(B \cap (s, t) = \emptyset\) Chapter7/PathIsPiecewiseSmooth; admissible if continuous on \([a, b]\), differentiable off a countable set, with \(\|c'\|\) integrable Chapter7/PathIsAdmissible; in \(N\) if \(c([a, b]) \subseteq N\). Piecewise smooth paths are admissible Chapter7/PathIsPiecewiseSmooth.isAdmissible. For admissible \(c\): \(\|c(b) - c(a)\| \le L\) (fundamental theorem of calculus off a countable set); \(L\) is additive; \(L = 0\) forces \(c\) constant; \(\|c'\| = k\) wherever defined gives \(L = k(b - a)\) Chapter7/PathpathLength_eq_of_norm_deriv. Restriction, concatenation, reversal and translation preserve piecewise smoothness, and lengths behave as expected Chapter7/PathpathLength_concat.

By [V7.2, §5.3], a geodesic on an interval \(s \supseteq [a, b]\) has length \(\|\gamma'(t_0)\|(b - a)\), \(t_0 \in s\). Fix normal coordinates \((O, U, F, G)\) of radius \(\varepsilon\) at \(q\); write \(D_w = dF_w\).

Lemma 10.5, the Gauss lemma [V7.12]. For \(w, x \in T_qN\), \(\|w\| < \varepsilon\): \(\langle D_ww, D_wx\rangle = \langle w, x\rangle\); \(\|D_{rw}w\| = \|w\|\) for \(0 \le r \le 1\); and \(dG(D_wx) = x\), so \(D_w\) is injective on \(T_qN\) Chapter7/GaussLemmaNormalCoord.inner_fderiv_F Chapter7/GaussLemmaNormalCoord.injective_fderiv_F.

Proof. \(F(tw) = \exp_q(tw)\) has speed \(\|w\|\); differentiate \(G(F(w + sx)) = w + sx\). Let \(g(r) = \langle D_{rw}w, D_{rw}(rx)\rangle\); then \(g(0) = 0\) and \(g'(r) = \langle d^2F_{rw}(w, w), D_{rw}(rx)\rangle + \langle D_{rw}w, d^2F_{rw}(w, rx) + D_{rw}x\rangle\). The first term vanishes: a normal acceleration against the tangent velocity of \(s \mapsto F(rw + srx)\). The second is \(\langle w, x\rangle\): differentiate \(\|D_{r(w + sx)}(w + sx)\|^2 = \|w + sx\|^2\) at \(s = 0\), using the symmetry of \(d^2F\). So \(g(1) = \langle w, x\rangle\). \(\square\)

Lemma 10.6 [V7.13]. Let \(c\) lie in \(N\) near \(t\), be differentiable at \(t\), with \(c(t) \in U \setminus \{q\}\). Then \(r = \|G \circ c\|\) is differentiable at \(t\) with \(|r'(t)| \le \|c'(t)\|\), and if \(r'(t) = \|c'(t)\|\) the direction \(G(c)/r\) is stationary at \(t\) Chapter7/GaussLemmaNormalCoord.hasDerivAt_radius. For \(c\) admissible on \([a, b]\) with values in \((N \cap U) \setminus \{q\}\), \(L(c|[a, b]) \ge r(b) - r(a)\), and with equality the direction is constant Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.radius_sub_le_pathLength Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.direction_eq_of_pathLength_eq.

Proof. With \(w = G(c(t))\) and \(w' = dG(c'(t)) \in T_qN\), \(D_ww' = c'(t)\) and \(r' = \langle w, w'\rangle/\|w\| = \langle D_ww, c'\rangle/\|D_ww\|\) by the Gauss lemma; Cauchy–Schwarz. Equality makes \(c'\) a multiple of \(D_ww\), so \(w'\) of \(w\) by injectivity. Integrate off a countable set. \(\square\)

Lemma (leaving a normal ball) [V7.14]. For \(s > 0\) let \(\mathrm{ball}_s = U \cap G^{-1}B(0, s)\) Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.ballSet; for \(s < \varepsilon\), \(F(\bar B(0, s) \cap T_qN) = \{y \in N \cap U : \|G(y)\| \le s\}\) is compact Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.isCompact_closedBallSet. If \(0 < s < \varepsilon\) and \(c\) is admissible on \([a, b]\), in \(N\), with \(c(a) = q\), \(c(b) \notin \mathrm{ball}_s\), there are \(a \le t_1 < t_2 \le b\) with \(c(t_1) = q\), \(c((t_1, t_2]) \subseteq U \setminus \{q\}\), \(\|G(c(t))\| < s\) on \([t_1, t_2)\), \(\|G(c(t_2))\| = s\) and \(L(c|[t_1, t_2]) \ge s\) Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.exists_crossing.

Proof. Let \(t_2\) be the first exit from \(\mathrm{ball}_s\); since the closed normal ball is closed in \(V\), \(\|G(c(t_2))\| = s\). Let \(t_1\) be the last visit of \(q\) before \(t_2\). Lemma 10.6 on \([t', t_2]\), with \(\|G(c(t'))\|\) small, gives the length bound. \(\square\) Milnor’s proof of Theorem 10.4 omits this lemma: a competing path may leave \(U\).

5.6 Short geodesics are shortest

Theorem 10.4 [V7.15]. Let \(\varepsilon\) be a normal radius at \(q\) and \(v \in B_\varepsilon(q)\). Then \(t \mapsto \exp_q(tv)\) is a geodesic near \([0, 1]\) with velocity \(v\) at \(0\) and length \(\|v\|\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.radial, and every admissible path in \(N\) from \(q\) to \(\exp_q(v)\) has length \(\ge \|v\|\) Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.norm_le_pathLength. (Apply [V7.14, §5.5] with \(s = \|v\| = \|G(\exp_qv)\|\).)

Theorem 10.4, sharp equality case [V7.16]. If moreover \(v \ne 0\) and \(L(c|[a, b]) = \|v\|\), then \(c(t) = \exp_q\big(\|v\|^{-1}L(c|[a, t])\,v\big)\) on \([a, b]\) Chapter7/ShortestNormalCoord.eq_exp_of_pathLength_eq. Proof. With \(t_1, t_2\) of [V7.14, §5.5], \(c\) has length \(0\), hence is constant, on \([a, t_1]\) and \([t_2, b]\). For \(t \in (t_1, t_2]\), [V7.15, §5.6] on \([t_1, t]\) and Lemma 10.6 on \([t, t_2]\) give bounds \(\|G(c(t))\|\) and \(\|v\| - \|G(c(t))\|\) adding up to the total; both are equalities, so \(G(c(t))\) points along \(v\). \(\square\) Milnor’s equal images do not suffice for Corollary 10.7.

Corollary 10.7 [V7.17]. Let \(c\) be piecewise smooth on \([0, \ell]\), in \(N\), with \(\|c'\| = 1\) wherever \(c\) is differentiable in \((0, \ell)\), and no longer than any piecewise smooth path in \(N\), on any interval, from \(c(0)\) to \(c(\ell)\). Then \(c\) is a geodesic on \((0, \ell)\) Chapter7/Minimalcorollary_10_7. Proof. If \(c([\alpha, \beta]) \subseteq O\) for \(O, \varepsilon\) as in Lemma 10.3, let \(v\) join \(c(\alpha)\) to \(c(\beta)\) by (1) and \(\tilde\gamma(t) = \exp_{c(\alpha)}(\frac{t - \alpha}{\beta - \alpha}v)\). Replacing \(c|[\alpha, \beta]\) by \(\tilde\gamma\) gives a competitor, so \(L(c|[\alpha, \beta]) = \|v\| = \beta - \alpha\) by [V7.15, §5.6], and [V7.16, §5.6] with unit speed gives \(c = \tilde\gamma\) on \([\alpha, \beta]\) Chapter7/Minimalminimal_segment. Apply this around each \(t_0 \in (0, \ell)\); locality. \(\square\)

5.7 The distance

Definition (the distance) [V7.18]. \(\rho(p, q) \in [0, \infty]\) is the infimum of the lengths of the piecewise smooth paths in \(N\), on any interval, from \(p\) to \(q\) Chapter7/DistanceriemDist (\(\infty\) if \(q \notin N\) Chapter7/DistanceriemDist_eq_top_of_notMem). It is at most the length of each such path, \(\rho(p, p) = 0\) on \(N\), and \(\rho\) is symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality (reversal, translation, concatenation) Chapter7/DistanceriemDist_triangle. If \(\varepsilon\) is a normal radius at \(p\), \(0 < s < \varepsilon\) and \(y \notin \mathrm{ball}_s\), then \(\rho(p, y) \ge s\) by [V7.14, §5.5] Chapter7/DistanceNormalCoord.ofReal_le_riemDist; so \(\rho(p, q) = 0\) implies \(p = q\) on \(N\) Chapter7/Distanceeq_of_riemDist_eq_zero.

Proposition (metric balls) [V7.19]. If \(\varepsilon\) is a normal radius at \(p\): \(\rho(p, \exp_pv) = \|v\|\) for \(v \in B_\varepsilon(p)\); for \(0 < r \le \varepsilon\), \(\rho(p, y) < r\) iff \(y \in N \cap \mathrm{ball}_r\) Chapter7/DistanceNormalCoord.riemDist_lt_iff. Hence the \(\rho\)-balls about \(p\) form a neighbourhood basis of \(p\) in \(N\) Chapter7/DistancehasBasis_nhdsWithin_riemDist. (The radial geodesic and [V7.18, §5.7]; continuity of \(F\) at \(0\).)

Lemma (Corollary 10.8, local form) [V7.20]. Call \(y, z \in N\) \(\delta\)-joined if exactly one \(v \in T_yN\) has \(\|v\| < \delta\) and \(\exp_y(v) = z\), \(\rho(y, z) = \|v\|\), and \(v = G(y, z)\) for some \(G\) smooth on an open \(O_2 \ni (y, z)\) that likewise gives such vectors \(G(y', z')\) for all \(y', z' \in N\) with \((y', z') \in O_2\), \(\rho(y', z') < \delta\) Chapter7/DistanceIsShortJoin. Each \(p \in N\) has \(s > 0\) and an open \(\Omega \ni p\), with \(\rho(p, \cdot) < s\) on \(N \cap \Omega\), such that \(y \in N \cap \Omega\) and \(z\) with \(\rho(y, z) < \delta \le s\) are \(\delta\)-joined Chapter7/Distanceexists_isShortJoin. Proof. Take \(O, \varepsilon\) from Lemma 10.3, the \(\rho\)-ball of radius \(r\) in \(O\), \(s = \min(r, \varepsilon)/2\), \(\Omega = \mathrm{ball}_s\); then \(y, z \in O\), and (1)–(3) with [V7.19, §5.7] apply. \(\square\)

Proposition (continuity of \(\rho\)) [V7.21]. \(\|q - p\| \le \rho(p, q)\) Chapter7/MetricofReal_norm_sub_le_riemDist; points of \(N\) near \(p \in N\) are \(\rho\)-near \(p\) Chapter7/Metriceventually_riemDist_lt; \(\rho\) is continuous on \(N \times N\), in particular \(y \mapsto \rho(y, q)\) on \(N\) Chapter7/MetriccontinuousOn_riemDist (triangle inequality and [V7.19, §5.7]).

Proposition (convergence) [V7.30]. If \(x_n \to y \in N\) within \(N\), then \(\rho(x_n, y) \to 0\) Chapter7/Metrictendsto_riemDist_of_tendsto, by [V7.19, §5.7].

5.8 Continuing geodesics; Theorem 10.9

Proposition (the geodesic flow) [V7.23]. (i) A geodesic on an open interval \(s \ni 0\) is \(\gamma(t) = \exp_{\gamma(0)}(t\gamma'(0))\) on \(s\) Chapter7/GeodesicFlowIsGeodesicOn.exp_smul_eq. Let \(\Psi_t(y, w) = \big(\exp_y(tw), \frac{d}{dt}\exp_y(tw)\big)\) Chapter7/GeodesicFlowgeoFlow. (ii) For \(x_0 \in N\), \(R > 0\) there are an open \(U \ni x_0\), \(\tau > 0\) and \(\Phi\) continuous on \(U \times B(0, R) \times (-\tau, \tau)\) such that for \((y, w) \in TN\) with \(y \in U\), \(\|w\| < R\), the ray \(t \mapsto \exp_y(tw)\) is a geodesic on \((-\tau, \tau)\) with velocity \(w\) at \(0\) and \(\Psi_t(y, w) = \Phi(y, w, t)\) Chapter7/GeodesicFlowexists_localFlow_exp. (iii) If the ray of \((y, w) \in TN\) is a geodesic on an open interval \(I \ni 0\), and that of \(\Psi_s(y, w)\), \(s \in I\), on an open interval \(J \ni 0\), the former is one on \(I \cup (s + J)\), and \(\Psi_{s + t}(y, w) = \Psi_t(\Psi_s(y, w))\) for \(t \in J\) Chapter7/GeodesicFlowisGeodesicOn_exp_smul_union. (iv) If \((p, v)\) is in the domain, so is every point of \(TN\) near it, and \(\exp|_{TN}\) is continuous at \((p, v)\) Chapter7/GeodesicFloweventually_mem_expDom_and_continuousWithinAt_exp.

Proof. (i) \(\sigma \mapsto \gamma(t\sigma)\) is a geodesic from \(\gamma(0)\) with velocity \(t\gamma'(0)\). (ii) Lemma 10.2 rescaled. (iii) [V7.5, §5.3] on \(I \cap (s + J)\); glue. (iv) Cover the arc from \(p\) by finitely many sets of (ii), \(R = \|v\| + 1\), of least time \(2\tau_0\). By induction on \(k\), for \((y, w) \in TN\) near \((p, v)\) the ray is a geodesic near \([0, \min(k\tau_0, 1)]\) and \(\Psi_{\min(k\tau_0, 1)}\) is continuous at \((p, v)\), as \(\Psi_{s + h} = \Phi(\Psi_s, h)\) by (iii) and constant speed. \(\square\)

Definition (geodesic completeness) [V7.22]. \(N\) is geodesically complete if \(TN\) lies in the domain of \(\exp\) Chapter7/GeodesicFlowIsGeodesicallyComplete. If \(\{q\} \times T_qN\) lies in the domain, each \(t \mapsto \exp_q(tv)\) is a geodesic on \(\mathbb R\) Chapter7/GeodesicFlowisGeodesicOn_univ_exp_smul (rescale the geodesics with velocities \(\pm Tv\)).

Definition (minimal geodesics) [V7.24]. \(\gamma\) is a minimal geodesic on \([a, b]\) if it is a geodesic on an open set containing \([a, b]\) and no piecewise smooth path in \(N\) from \(\gamma(a)\) to \(\gamma(b)\) is shorter Chapter7/HopfRinowIsMinimalGeodesic. On the domain, \(\exp_p(v) \in N\) Chapter7/HopfRinowexp_mem_of_mem_expDom. If \(t \mapsto \exp_p(tv)\) is a geodesic on \(\mathbb R\) and \(\rho(p, \exp_pv) = \|v\|\), it is minimal on \([0, 1]\), of length \(\|v\|\) Chapter7/HopfRinowisMinimalGeodesic_exp_smul.

Lemma (two steps of Theorem 10.9) [V7.25]. (i) If \(\varepsilon\) is a normal radius at \(p\) and \(0 < \delta < \varepsilon\), \(\delta < \rho(p, q) < \infty\), some \(w \in T_pN\) with \(\|w\| = \delta\) has \(\rho(p, q) = \delta + \rho(\exp_pw, q)\) Chapter7/HopfRinowNormalCoord.exists_riemDist_eq_add. (ii) Let \(\gamma\) be a geodesic on \(\mathbb R\) with \(\|\gamma'(0)\| = 1\), \(0 < t_0 < t_1\), and \(\sigma\) a geodesic on an open interval containing \([t_0, t_1]\) with \(\|\sigma'(t_0)\| = 1\), \(\sigma(t_0) = \gamma(t_0)\). If \(\rho(\gamma(0), \sigma(t_1)) \ge t_1\), then \(\sigma(t_1) = \gamma(t_1)\) Chapter7/HopfRinowbroken_geodesic_eq. Proof. (i) As \(q \notin \mathrm{ball}_\delta\) [V7.19, §5.7], by [V7.14, §5.5] every path from \(p\) to \(q\) has length at least \(\delta + \rho(y, q)\) for some \(y\) on the compact sphere \(S = \exp_p\{\|w\| = \delta\}\). Minimize the continuous \(\rho(\cdot, q)\) [V7.21, §5.7] on \(S\), and use the triangle inequality. (ii) The broken path, \(\gamma\) then \(\sigma\), has unit speed (also at \(t_0\), one-sided derivatives being unique), so its length \(t_1\) is at most \(\rho\): it is minimal, a geodesic by Corollary 10.7, equal to \(\gamma\) by [V7.5, §5.3]. \(\square\)

Theorem 10.9 at one point [V7.26]. If \(\{p\} \times T_pN\) lies in the domain of \(\exp\) and \(q \in N\) has \(\rho(p, q) < \infty\), some \(v \in T_pN\) has \(\exp_p(v) = q\), \(\rho(p, q) = \|v\|\), and \(t \mapsto \exp_p(tv)\) minimal on \([0, 1]\) Chapter7/HopfRinowtheorem_10_9. Proof. Let \(r = \rho(p, q) > 0\) (else \(v = 0\)), \(\delta < \min(\varepsilon, r)\), \(w_0\) from [V7.25, §5.8] (i), and \(\gamma(t) = \exp_p(tw_0/\delta)\), a unit-speed geodesic on \(\mathbb R\) [V7.22, §5.8]. \(A = \{t : \rho(\gamma(t), q) = r - t\}\) is closed [V7.21, §5.7] and contains \(\delta\). For \(t_0 \in A \cap [\delta, r)\) and \(y > t_0\), (i) at \(\gamma(t_0)\), with radius \(\delta' < \min(\varepsilon', r - t_0, y - t_0)\), and (ii) put \(t_0 + \delta' \in A\). By continuous induction \(r \in A\) Mathlib/Topology/Order/IntermediateValueIsClosed.Icc_subset_of_forall_exists_gt, so \(\gamma(r) = q\); take \(v = rw_0/\delta\) and [V7.24, §5.8]. \(\square\)

Completeness is used at \(p\) only.

← 4. Homology and the Morse inequalities6. Energy, Jacobi fields and the index theorem →

6. Energy, Jacobi fields and the index theorem

This chapter proves the index theorem 15.1, with the variational tools that Chapters 7–10 also use: Lemma 11.A, the variation formulas, Corollary 12.3, \(E_{**}\), Theorem 14.1, Lemma 14.3, smooth dependence of geodesics on initial data, and Remark 14.5. \(\Omega\) carries no topology; \(T\Omega_\omega\) is a space of fields, tied to \(\Omega\) by variations. \(E_{**}\) is defined by the second variation formula, the Jacobi theory is developed along any smooth curve, and no completeness is assumed. Lemmas 12.1 and 13.6, Remarks 14.2 and 14.6, Corollary 15.2 and Lemma 14.4 itself are not needed.

6.1 Paths, variations, energy

\(P_x\) is the projection onto \(T_xN\) for \(x \in N\), \(0\) otherwise; \(c'\) is the derivative where it exists, \(0\) elsewhere.

Definition (the path space) [V8.1]. \(\Omega(N; p, q)\) is the set of \(c : \mathbb R \to V\), piecewise smooth on \([0, 1]\) [V7.11, §5.5], with \(c([0, 1]) \subseteq N\), \(c(0) = p\), \(c(1) = q\) Chapter8/EnergypathSpace. \(T\Omega_\omega\) is the vector space of fields \(X : \mathbb R \to V\), piecewise smooth on \([0, 1]\), with \(P_{\omega(t)}X(t) = X(t)\) on \([0, 1]\) and \(X(0) = X(1) = 0\) Chapter8/EnergypathTangent; it depends only on \(\omega|[0, 1]\) Chapter8/FirstVariationmem_pathTangent_congr.

Fact (calculus on closed strips) [V8.8] (standard). On a closed strip \(S = U \times [a, b]\), \(U \subseteq \mathbb R\) open, let \(\partial_u\), \(\partial_t\) be partial derivatives within \(S\). For \(F\) smooth on \(S\), \(\partial_u\partial_tF = \partial_t\partial_uF\) on all of \(S\), edges included Chapter8/PiecewisepdU_pdT. If \(F\), \(F'\) are continuous on \(S\) and \(F'\) is the \(u\)-derivative of \(F\) for \(t \in (a, b)\), then \(\frac{d}{du}\int_a^bF\,dt = \int_a^bF'\,dt\); likewise if on each piece of a finite subdivision the integrand agrees inside with a function \(C^1\) on the closed strip Chapter8/PiecewisehasDerivAt_integral_of_piecewise. If \(g\) is integrable and \(\int_s^tg = F^-(t) - F^+(s)\) on every piece \([s, t]\) for break points \(B\), then \(\int_a^bg = F^-(b) - F^+(a) - \sum_{x \in B \cap (a, b)}(F^+(x) - F^-(x))\) Chapter8/Piecewiseintegral_eq_of_piecewise, by induction over the pieces. Proof idea. Mathlib’s symmetry of second derivatives within a set; domination by compactness.

Definition (variations) [V8.2]. For a normed space \(\mathcal P\), an open \(U \ni 0\) in \(\mathcal P\) and a finite \(B\), \(\alpha : \mathcal P \to (\mathbb R \to V)\) is a variation with break points \(B\) if \(\alpha(u, t) \in N\) for \(u \in U\), \(t \in [0, 1]\), \(\alpha(u, 0)\), \(\alpha(u, 1)\) do not depend on \(u\), and \((u, t) \mapsto \alpha(u, t)\) is \(C^\infty\) on each \(U \times [s, t]\), \(0 \le s < t \le 1\), \(B \cap (s, t) = \emptyset\) Chapter8/EnergyIsVariation. Then \(\alpha(u) \in \Omega(N; \alpha(0, 0), \alpha(0, 1))\), \(\alpha \circ \varphi\) is a variation for smooth \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi(0) \in U\), and \(\partial_u\alpha\) is tangent Chapter8/EnergyhasFDerivWithinAt_mem_tangentSubspace. For \(\mathcal P = \mathbb R\) the variation field \(W_t = \partial_u\alpha(0, t)\) Chapter8/EnergyvarField lies in \(T\Omega_{\alpha(0)}\) Chapter8/EnergyIsVariation.varField_mem: on each piece it is \(\partial_u\alpha\) on the strip, and adjacent strips agree at break points.

Lemma 11.A [V8.3]. Let \(\omega \in \Omega(N; p, q)\) and \(\Lambda : \mathbb R \to L(\mathcal P, V)\) be piecewise smooth on \([0, 1]\), with values in \(T_{\omega(t)}N\) and \(\Lambda(0) = \Lambda(1) = 0\). For some \(\varepsilon > 0\) and finite \(B\), \(\alpha(u, t) = \exp_{\omega(t)}(\Lambda(t)u)\), \(\|u\| < \varepsilon\), is a variation with break points \(B\), with \(\alpha(0, t) = \omega(t)\) and \(\partial_u\alpha(0, t) = \Lambda(t)\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter8/FirstVariationexists_variation. In particular each \(X \in T\Omega_\omega\) is the field of \(\exp_{\omega(t)}(uX(t))\) Chapter8/FirstVariationexists_variation_one. Proof. The compact set \(\{(\omega(t), 0)\}\) lies in the open set \(O\) of [V7.8, §5.4], hence so does \(\{(\omega(t), v) : \|v\| < \delta\}\) for some \(\delta\); take \(\varepsilon = \delta/(\sup\|\Lambda\| + 1)\). Smoothness on strips by [V7.8, §5.4] (ii), values in \(N\) by [V7.24, §5.8], the field by \(d(\exp_q)_0 = \mathrm{id}\). \(\square\)

Lemma 12.A [V8.5]. Let \(E_a^b(c) = \int_a^b\|c'\|^2\), \(E = E_0^1\) Chapter8/Energyenergy. For piecewise smooth \(c\), \(L(c|[a, b])^2 \le (b - a)E_a^b(c)\) (expand \(\int(\|c'\| - \frac{L}{b - a})^2 \ge 0\)); for admissible \(c\) with \(\|c'\| = k\) wherever differentiable, \(E_a^b(c) = k^2(b - a)\) Chapter8/EnergypathLength_sq_le_energy Chapter8/Energyenergy_eq_of_norm_deriv.

6.2 The first variation and critical paths

Definitions (the first variation) [V8.7]. \(\Delta_tf = f'(t^+) - f'(t^-)\) is the jump of the derivative, \(0\) where \(f\) is differentiable Chapter8/Energyjump. Along \(c\), \(\frac{DX}{dt} = P_cX'\) Chapter8/FirstVariationcovD, \(A = \frac{D}{dt}c'\), and \[\mathrm{FV}(c, X) = -\sum_{0 < t < 1}\langle X(t), \Delta_tc\rangle - \int_0^1\langle X, A\rangle\,dt\] Chapter8/FirstVariationfirstVariation, a finite sum over the break points of \(c\) Chapter8/FirstVariationfinsum_jump_eq_sum, depending only on \(X|[0, 1]\).

Theorem 12.2, at every \(u\) [V8.9]. For a variation \(\alpha\) with \(U \subseteq \mathbb R\) and every \(u_0 \in U\), \(u \mapsto E(\alpha(u))\) has derivative \(2\,\mathrm{FV}(\alpha(u_0), \partial_u\alpha(u_0, \cdot))\) at \(u_0\) Chapter8/FirstVariationIsVariation.hasDerivAt_energy; at \(0\) it is \(2\,\mathrm{FV}(\omega, W)\) for any \(\omega = \alpha(0)\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter8/FirstVariationfirst_variation. Proof. Differentiate under the integral [V8.8, §6.1], with integrand \(2\langle\partial_t\partial_u\alpha, \partial_t\alpha\rangle\) by symmetry of mixed partials; integrate by parts on each piece and telescope; \(Y = \partial_u\alpha\) vanishes at \(t = 0, 1\) and is tangent, so \(\langle Y, c''\rangle = \langle Y, A\rangle\). \(\square\)

Definitions (critical paths, geodesics) [V8.4] [V8.10]. \(c\) is a critical path if \(\frac{d}{du}E(\alpha(u))|_0 = 0\) for every variation \(\alpha\) (\(U \subseteq \mathbb R\)) with \(\alpha(0) = c\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter8/CriticalIsCriticalPath; an unbroken geodesic if it is \(C^\infty\) on \([0, 1]\) and a geodesic on \((0, 1)\) Chapter8/CriticalIsUnbrokenGeodesic. For \(c \in \Omega\), \(c\) is critical iff \(\mathrm{FV}(c, \cdot) = 0\) on \(T\Omega_c\), by [V8.9, §6.2] and Lemma 11.A Chapter8/CriticalisCriticalPath_iff; an unbroken geodesic has \(\mathrm{FV}(c, \cdot) = 0\) (no jumps, \(A = 0\)) Chapter8/CriticalIsUnbrokenGeodesic.firstVariation_eq_zero.

Corollary 12.3 [V8.11]. \(c \in \Omega(N; p, q)\) is critical iff it is an unbroken geodesic Chapter8/Criticalcorollary_12_3. Proof. Let \(c\) be critical, with break points \(B\). (1) For \(x \notin B\), the test field \(\varphi A\), \(\varphi\) a bump inside the piece at \(x\), gives \(\int\varphi\|A\|^2 = 0\), so \(A(x) = 0\) Chapter8/Criticalaccel_eq_zero_of_critical. (2) At \(x \in B\), \(\Delta = \Delta_xc\) is tangent, and \(\varphi P_c\Delta\) gives \(\|\Delta\|^2 = 0\). (3) A path smooth on both sides of \(x\), a geodesic there and differentiable at \(x\), is a geodesic near \(x\) Chapter8/CriticalisGeodesicOn_of_glue: its lift solves the \(C^1\) system of [V7.5, §5.3] off \(x\), hence at \(x\) by a derivative-extension theorem, and so equals the geodesic with its data at \(x\) [V7.4, §5.2]. Locality [V7.1, §5.3]. \(\square\)

6.3 The second variation and \(E_{**}\)

Write \(R(a, b)c\) for \(R_x(a, b)c\) [V6.17, §5.1] at the relevant point \(x\) (\(0\) if \(x \notin N\)) Chapter8/SecondVariationcurvR.

Proposition (curvature identity) [V8.12]. (i) For \(F\) smooth on an open \(O \subseteq \mathbb R^2\) with values in \(N\), at every point, \[P\,\partial_u\big(P\,\partial_t\partial_tF\big) = P\,\partial_t\big(P\,\partial_t\partial_uF\big) + R(\partial_tF, \partial_uF)\partial_tF\] Chapter8/SecondVariationcurvature_identity. (ii) For a variation \(\alpha\) (\(U \subseteq \mathbb R\)) and \(0 < x < 1\), \(u \mapsto \Delta_x\alpha(u)\) has derivative \(\Delta_x\partial_u\alpha(u_0, \cdot)\) at \(u_0\) Chapter8/SecondVariationIsVariation.hasDerivAt_jump. Proof. (i) With \(a = \partial_tF\), \(b = \partial_uF\) tangent and \(D_v = \mathrm{II}(v, \cdot)\) at the point: \(\partial_ta = D_aa + P\partial_ta\), \(\partial_tb = D_ab + P\partial_tb\), \(\partial_u\partial_ta = \partial_t\partial_tb\), \(PD_bP = 0\), and \(D_b\) maps normal to tangent. The two sides differ by \(D_bD_aa - D_aD_ab = R(a, b)a\), as \(D_ab = D_ba\) [V6.12, §5.1]. (ii) Symmetry of mixed partials on the edges of the strips at \(x\) [V8.8, §6.1]. \(\square\)

Theorem 13.1 [V8.13]. With \(V = \gamma'\) put \[\Phi(X_1, X_2) = -\sum_{0 < t < 1}\langle X_2, P\Delta_tX_1\rangle - \int_0^1\Big\langle X_2, \frac{D^2X_1}{dt^2} + R(V, X_1)V\Big\rangle dt\] Chapter8/SecondVariationsecondVariation. If \(\gamma\) is an unbroken geodesic and \(\alpha\) a variation with \(U \subseteq \mathbb R^2\) and \(\alpha(0) = \gamma\) on \([0, 1]\), then \(u_1 \mapsto \partial_{u_2}E(\alpha(u_1, u_2))|_{u_2 = 0}\) has derivative \(2\Phi(W_1, W_2)\) at \(0\), \(W_i\) the variation fields Chapter8/SecondVariationsecond_variation. Proof. By [V8.9, §6.2] at every \(u_1\), differentiate \(\mathrm{FV}(\alpha(u_1, 0), \partial_{u_2}\alpha(u_1, 0))\) at \(0\). Jump terms: [V8.12, §6.3] (ii), \(\gamma\) having no jumps. Integral: differentiate under the integral [V8.8, §6.1]; as \(A = 0\) along \(\gamma\), the integrand is \(\langle W_2, P\partial_{u_1}A\rangle\), which (i) turns into \(\langle W_2, \frac{D^2W_1}{dt^2} + R(V, W_1)V\rangle\). \(\square\)

Proposition 13.A [V8.15]. For \(\gamma \in \Omega\) and \(X_1, X_2 \in T\Omega_\gamma\), \(\Phi(X_1, X_2) = \int_0^1\big(\langle\frac{DX_1}{dt}, \frac{DX_2}{dt}\rangle - \langle R(V, X_1)V, X_2\rangle\big)dt\) Chapter8/HessianhessForm Chapter8/HessiansecondVariation_eq_hessForm. Proof. On each piece \(\int(\langle DX_2, DX_1\rangle + \langle X_2, D^2X_1\rangle) = \big[\langle X_2, PX_1'\rangle\big]\), \(X_2\) being tangent; telescope [V8.8, §6.1]. \(\square\)

Corollary 13.4 [V8.16]. \(\langle R(v, w_1)v, w_2\rangle = \langle R(v, w_2)v, w_1\rangle\) for tangent \(v, w_i\), by [V6.18, §5.1] and the symmetry of \(\mathrm{II}\) Chapter8/Hessianinner_curvR_comm. So the integral form is symmetric and linear on \(T\Omega_\gamma\) Chapter8/HessianhessForm_comm Chapter8/HessianhessForm_add_right, and so is \(E_{**}\) Chapter8/HessianenergyHessian_isSymm.

Definition (\(E_{**}\)) [V8.14]. For \(\gamma \in \Omega(N; p, q)\), \(E_{**} = 2\Phi\), a symmetric bilinear form on \(T\Omega_\gamma\) Chapter8/HessianenergyHessian, depending only on the fields on \([0, 1]\) Chapter8/HessiansecondVariation_congr. By Theorem 13.1 and Lemma 11.A it is Milnor’s Hessian at a geodesic.

Remark 13.5 [V8.17]. For an unbroken geodesic \(\gamma \in \Omega\) and a variation \(\alpha\) (\(U \subseteq \mathbb R\)) of \(\gamma\) with field \(W\), \(\frac{d}{du}E(\alpha(u))\) has derivative \(2\Phi(W, W) = E_{**}(W, W)\) at \(0\) Chapter8/SecondVariationremark_13_5 Chapter8/HessianhasDerivAt_deriv_energy: Theorem 13.1 for \((u_1, u_2) \mapsto \alpha(u_1 + u_2)\).

6.4 Jacobi fields

Fact (linear equations) [V9.1] (standard). Let \(E\) be complete and \(A : \mathbb R \to \operatorname{End}(E)\) continuous. Each \((t_0, x_0)\) has a solution of \(x' = A(t)x\) on \(\mathbb R\) Chapter9/JacobiODEexists_linearODE; the chosen one \(\mathrm{sol}_s(\xi)\) with value \(\xi\) at \(s\) is linear in \(\xi\) Chapter9/JacobiODElinSol; a function continuous on \([a, b]\) solving the equation on \((a, b)\) equals \(\mathrm{sol}_s(f(s))\) on \([a, b]\), \(s \in [a, b]\) Chapter9/JacobiODEeqOn_Icc_linSol; and if \(A\) is smooth on \([a, b]\) and \(f' = Af\) there, \(f\) is smooth on \([a, b]\) Chapter9/JacobiSystemcontDiffOn_Icc_of_hasDerivAt. Proof idea. Picard–Lindelöf for a radially truncated field, the truncation never acting (Grönwall); glue by [V6.7, §5.2].

A smooth curve in \(N\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0, 1]\) with \(\gamma([0, 1]) \subseteq N\); unbroken geodesics in \(\Omega\) are such, and such \(\gamma\) lie in \(\Omega(N; \gamma(0), \gamma(1))\). Along \(\gamma\), \(V\), \(P' = \frac{d}{dt}P_{\gamma(t)}\) and \(\frac{D}{dt}\) are taken within \([0, 1]\).

Proposition (Jacobi fields) [V9.2]. \(J\) is a Jacobi field along \(\gamma\) if it is \(C^\infty\) on \([0, 1]\), tangent there, and \(\frac{D^2J}{dt^2} + R(V, J)V = 0\) on \((0, 1)\) Chapter8/JacobiIsJacobiField. Let \(S = P'P - PP'\), \(K(t)v = R(V, Pv)V\). The Jacobi system \(J' = SJ + Y\), \(Y' = SY - KJ\) on \(V \times V\) Chapter9/JacobiSystemjacSys has coefficients smooth on \([0, 1]\), extended constantly to a continuous family on \(\mathbb R\); let \(\mathrm{jac}_s(\zeta)\) be its solution with value \(\zeta\) at \(s\) Chapter9/JacobiSystemjacSol. For \(s \in [0, 1]\) and tangent \(\zeta = (x, y)\) at \(\gamma(s)\), both components of \(\mathrm{jac}_s(\zeta)\) are tangent on \([0, 1]\), and the first is a Jacobi field \(J\) with \(\frac{DJ}{dt}\) the second Chapter9/JacobiSystemjacSol_mem_tanAt Chapter9/JacobiSystemisJacobiField_jacSol. Every Jacobi field has \((J, \frac{DJ}{dt}) = \mathrm{jac}_s(J(s), \frac{DJ}{dt}(s))\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter9/JacobiSystemIsJacobiField.eqOn_jacSol; so \(J(s) = \frac{DJ}{dt}(s) = 0\) forces \(J = 0\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter9/JacobiSystemIsJacobiField.eqOn_zero. Proof. As \(PP'P = 0\), the normal parts \(a = (1 - P)J\), \(b = (1 - P)Y\) solve \(a' = -P'a + b\), \(b' = -P'b\) and vanish at \(s\), hence on \([0, 1]\) [V9.1, §6.4]. Then \(\frac{DJ}{dt} = P(SJ + Y) = Y\) and \(\frac{D^2J}{dt^2} = P(SY - KJ) = -KJ\). Conversely \(J = PJ\) gives \(J' = SJ + \frac{DJ}{dt}\), and the Jacobi equation the second equation; uniqueness on \([0, 1]\). \(\square\)

No parallel frame is used; \(S\) keeps tangent data tangent.

Corollary 14.B [V9.3]. Let \(\mathcal J(\gamma)\) be the space of Jacobi fields with \(J = J \circ \pi\), \(\pi\) the nearest-point map onto \([0, 1]\) Chapter9/JacobiSpacejacobiSpace; every Jacobi field agrees on \([0, 1]\) with one in \(\mathcal J(\gamma)\), and one vanishing on \([0, 1]\) is \(0\) Chapter9/JacobiSpacejacobiSpace_eq_zero. For \(s \in [0, 1]\), \(J \mapsto (J(s), \frac{DJ}{dt}(s))\) is an isomorphism onto \(T_{\gamma(s)}N \times T_{\gamma(s)}N\), so \(\dim\mathcal J(\gamma) = 2n\) Chapter9/JacobiSpacejacEval_bijective Chapter9/JacobiSpacefinrank_jacobiSpace. (By [V9.2, §6.4].)

Definition (conjugate points) [V9.4]. \(a \ne b\) in \([0, 1]\) are conjugate along \(\gamma\) if a Jacobi field vanishes at \(a\) and \(b\) but not on all of \([0, 1]\) Chapter9/JacobiSpaceIsConjugate. The multiplicity \(\nu(a, b)\) is \(\dim\{J \in \mathcal J(\gamma) : J(a) = J(b) = 0\}\) Chapter9/JacobiSpaceconjMultiplicity; for \(a \ne b\) in \([0, 1]\), conjugacy is \(\nu(a, b) > 0\) Chapter9/JacobiSpaceisConjugate_iff. Write \(\nu(t) = \nu(0, t)\).

Theorem 14.1 [V9.5]. Let \(\gamma \in \Omega(N; p, q)\) be an unbroken geodesic and \(X \in T\Omega_\gamma\). Then \(E_{**}(X, \cdot) = 0\) on \(T\Omega_\gamma\) iff \(X\) is a Jacobi field Chapter8/Jacobitheorem_14_1. Proof. For a Jacobi field, \(\Phi(J, \cdot) = 0\) termwise. Conversely, as in Corollary 12.3, test fields give the Jacobi equation off the break points Chapter8/JacobijacobiExpr_eq_zero_of_null and \(P\Delta_xX = 0\); the normal part of \(\Delta_xX\) vanishes since \(X = PX\), so \(X\) is \(C^1\). Writing the Jacobi equation as \(X'' = -PP'X' - R(V, X)V + (1 - P)(P''X + 2P'X')\), a derivative-extension lemma and bootstrapping make \(X\) smooth across each break point Chapter8/Jacobismooth_near_of_null. \(\square\)

Theorem 14.1, nullity [V9.6]. The null space of \(E_{**}\) is read on \([0, 1]\), as the image of its kernel under \(X \mapsto X \circ \pi\) Chapter9/JacobiSpacehessNullSpace, and the nullity is its dimension. For an unbroken geodesic \(\gamma \in \Omega\) the null space is \(\{J \in \mathcal J(\gamma) : J(0) = J(1) = 0\}\), and the nullity is \(\nu(1)\) Chapter9/JacobiSpacehessNullSpace_eq Chapter9/JacobiSpacetheorem_14_1_nullity.

Lemma 14.3 [V9.8]. If \(\alpha\) is \(C^\infty\) on \((-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \times [0, 1]\) with values in \(N\) and each \(\alpha(u)\) is a geodesic on \((0, 1)\), then \(\partial_u\alpha(0, \cdot)\) is a Jacobi field along \(\alpha(0)\) Chapter9/JacobiVariationlemma_14_3; being a Jacobi field depends only on \(\gamma|[0, 1]\) Chapter9/JacobiVariationIsJacobiField.congr_curve. (Apply [V8.12, §6.3] (i) on the open strip, where \(P\partial_t\partial_t\alpha = 0\).)

Lemma (the tools of Lemma 14.4) [V9.9]. (i) For \(x_1 \in N\), \(R > 0\) there are an open \(U \ni x_1\), \(h > 0\) and \(\Phi\) smooth on \(U \times B(0, R) \times (-h, h)\) with \(\exp_y(tw) = \Phi(y, w, t)\), a geodesic on \((-h, h)\), for \((y, w) \in TN\), \(y \in U\), \(\|w\| < R\) Chapter9/GeodesicVariationexists_smooth_ray. (ii) A smooth curve \(\gamma\) in \(N\), geodesic on \((0, 1)\), equals \(t \mapsto \exp_{\gamma(0)}(tV(0))\) on \([0, 1]\), a geodesic on some \((-\eta, 1 + \eta)\) Chapter9/GeodesicVariationexists_initial_ray. (iii) Let \(c, w\) be smooth on an open \(U_0 \ni 0\) of \(\mathbb R\), \(c(u) \in N\), \(w(u) \in T_{c(u)}N\). If \(t \mapsto \exp_{c(0)}(tw(0))\) is a geodesic on \((-\delta, b + \delta)\), \(b \ge 0\), then for some \(\varepsilon, \eta > 0\), \((u, t) \mapsto \exp_{c(u)}(tw(u))\) is smooth on \((-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \times (-\eta, b + \eta)\) and each \(t \mapsto \exp_{c(u)}(tw(u))\) is a geodesic there Chapter9/GeodesicVariationRaysGood Chapter9/GeodesicVariationraysGood_of_isGeodesicOn. Proof. (i) Lemma 10.2 [V7.6, §5.3] rescaled, with [V7.23, §5.8] (i). (ii) Start at \(t = 1/2\) [V7.23, §5.8] (i); continue past both ends by (i) and the gluing [V7.23, §5.8] (iii). (iii) Let \(b_0\) be the supremum of the good \(b' \in [0, b]\) (\(0\) is good by (i)). With a flow (i) near the base ray at \(b_0\), for good \(s\) near \(b_0\) the rays continue from their position and velocity \((F(u), G(u))\) at time \(s\), smooth in \(u\), as \(\Phi(F(u), G(u), t - s)\) [V7.23, §5.8] (iii); so \(\min(s + h/2, b) > b_0\) is good unless it is \(b\). \(\square\)

Proposition (several parameters) [V11.1]. (iii) holds with \(u\) in an open subset \(U_0\) of any real normed space, about any \(u_0 \in U_0\), with \(B(u_0, \varepsilon)\) for \((-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)\) Chapter11/ExpSmoothRaysGoodE Chapter11/ExpSmoothraysGoodE_of_isGeodesicOn, by the same proof. Every \(p \in N\) has an open \(U \ni p\) and \(r\) smooth on \(U\) with \(r(U) \subseteq N\) and \(r = \mathrm{id}\) on \(N \cap U\), namely \(r(y) = x((\sigma y)_1)\) Chapter11/ExpSmoothexists_retraction.

Proposition (non-conjugate ends) [V9.10]. If \(a \ne b\) in \([0, 1]\) are not conjugate, \(J \mapsto (J(a), J(b))\) is an isomorphism \(\mathcal J(\gamma) \to T_{\gamma(a)}N \times T_{\gamma(b)}N\) Chapter9/GeodesicVariationjacEvalEnds_bijective_of_not_isConjugate: injective by definition, onto as \(2n = n + n\).

Remark 14.5 [V9.11]. If \(\varepsilon\) is a normal radius at \(q\) and \(v \in B_\varepsilon(q)\), then \(\sigma(t) = \exp_q(tv)\) is a smooth curve in \(N\), a Jacobi field along \(\sigma\) vanishing at \(0\) and \(1\) vanishes on \([0, 1]\), and \(J \mapsto (J(0), J(1))\) is an isomorphism Chapter9/JacobiVariationIsNormalRadius.isSmoothCurveIn_ray Chapter9/JacobiVariationremark_14_5_of_isNormalRadius Chapter9/JacobiVariationremark_14_5_bijective. Proof. With \(w = \frac{DJ}{dt}(0)\), \(F(t(v + uw))\) is a variation through geodesics [V7.9, §5.4] whose field \(t\,dF_{tv}(w)\) is a Jacobi field (Lemma 14.3) with data \((0, w)\) at \(0\), hence is \(J\) [V9.2, §6.4]. \(J(1) = 0\) gives \(dF_v(w) = 0\), so \(w = dG(dF_v(w)) = 0\) [V7.12, §5.5]. \(\square\)

6.5 The index theorem

Definition (index of a form) [V9.13]. For a bilinear form \(B\) on a real vector space, negative (positive) definite on \(S\) means \(B(x, x) < 0\) (\(> 0\)) for \(x \in S \setminus 0\) Chapter9/FormIndexIsNegDefOn; the index is the supremum in \(\mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}\) of the dimensions of finite-dimensional negative definite subspaces Chapter9/FormIndexformIndex. A finite index is attained Chapter9/FormIndexexists_isNegDefOn_of_formIndex_eq. If \(B'(Lx, Ly) = B(x, y)\), \(\operatorname{index}B \le \operatorname{index}B'\), \(L\) being injective on negative definite subspaces Chapter9/FormIndexformIndex_le_of_map; isomorphisms preserve the index. In finite dimension it is Mathlib’s negative index of inertia Chapter9/FormIndexformIndex_eq_sigNeg.

Lemmas 15.A and 15.B [V9.14]. (1) In dimension \(m\), a negative and a positive definite subspace have dimensions adding to at most \(m\) Chapter9/FormIndexfinrank_add_finrank_le, and a symmetric \(B\) is positive definite on a subspace of dimension \(m - \operatorname{index} - \operatorname{nullity}\) (Sylvester) Chapter9/FormIndexexists_isPosDefOn_add. (2) If \(\tau \mapsto H_\tau(x, y)\) is continuous at \(\tau_0\) for \(x, y\) in a finite-dimensional \(S\) on which \(H_{\tau_0}\) is negative (positive) definite, so is \(H_\tau\) for \(\tau\) near \(\tau_0\) Chapter9/FormIndexeventually_isNegDefOn Chapter9/FormIndexeventually_isPosDefOn (by compactness). (3) If \(X = A \oplus C\), \(B(A, C) = B(C, A) = 0\) and \(B\) is positive definite on \(C\), then \(\operatorname{index}B = \operatorname{index}B|_A\) Chapter9/FormIndexformIndex_eq_restrict_of_isCompl (project along \(C\)). (4) Let \(B\) be symmetric, \(U : \mathbb R^k \to X\) with \(B(Ua, Ua) < 0\) for \(a \ne 0\), and \(J, Y : \mathbb R^\nu \to X\) with \(B(Jb, Ua) = B(Jb, Jb') = 0\) and \(B(Jb, Yb') = 2\langle b, b'\rangle\). Then \(\operatorname{index}B \ge k + \nu\) Chapter9/IndexAssertionsle_formIndex_of_compound. Proof of (4). \((a, b) \mapsto Ua + c^{-1}Jb - cYb\) carries to \(B\) a form \(G_c\) polynomial in \(c\), with \(G_0 = B(Ua, Ua') - 4\langle b, b'\rangle\) negative definite; apply (2) and [V9.13, §6.5]. \(\square\)

Fix a smooth curve \(\gamma\) in \(N\), its form \(E_{**}\) [V8.14, §6.3], and \(\mathcal J = \mathcal J(\gamma)\).

Proposition (the jump formula) [V9.15]. If \(X, Y \in T\Omega_\gamma\) and near each \(t \in (0, 1) \setminus B\), \(B\) finite, \(X\) agrees with a Jacobi field, then \(E_{**}(X, Y) = -2\sum_{b \in B \cap (0, 1)}\langle Y(b), P\Delta_bX\rangle\) Chapter9/IndexFormenergyHessian_eq_jumps. (The Jacobi operator is local Chapter9/IndexFormjacobiExpr_congr, and \(0\) is a Jacobi field.)

Proposition (the mesh \(h_0\)) [V9.16]. Let \(C \ge 0\) bound \(\|P'\|^2 + \|K\|\) on \([0, 1]\) and \(h_0 = 1/(C + 1) > 0\) Chapter9/IndexFormfineMesh. (i) If \(X \in T\Omega_\gamma\) and each \(t \in [0, 1]\) has a zero \(s \in [0, t]\) of \(X\) with \(t - s \le h_0\), then \(\int_0^1\|X\|^2 \le \frac12E_{**}(X, X)\), so \(E_{**}(X, X) \le 0\) forces \(X = 0\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter9/IndexFormhessForm_ge Chapter9/IndexFormeqOn_zero_of_hessForm. (ii) \(J \in \mathcal J\) vanishing at \(a < b\), \(b - a \le h_0\), is \(0\), and for such \(a, b\), \(J \mapsto (J(a), J(b))\) is an isomorphism Chapter9/IndexFormeq_zero_of_short Chapter9/IndexFormjacEvalEnds_bijective. (iii) \(B \subseteq (0, \tau)\) is fine for \([0, \tau]\) if consecutive points of \(\{0\} \cup B \cup \{\tau\}\) are at most \(h_0\) apart Chapter9/BrokenJacobiIsFine; for \(\tau > 0\) one exists with the last point of \(\{0\} \cup B\) within \(h_0/2\) of \(\tau\) Chapter9/BrokenJacobiexists_isFine. Proof. (i) \(X = PX\) gives \(\|X'\|^2 \le \|\frac{DX}{dt}\|^2 + \|P'\|^2\|X\|^2\), so the integrand of [V8.15, §6.3] is \(\ge \|X'\|^2 - C\|X\|^2\) Chapter9/IndexFormintegrand_ge; and \(\|X(t)\|^2 \le L_s^t(X)^2 \le h_0E_0^1(X)\) by [V8.5, §6.1], so \(\int\|X\|^2 \le h_0\int\|X'\|^2\) Chapter9/IndexFormintegral_norm_sq_le. Combine, as \(h_0(C + 1) = 1\). (ii) \(\mathbf 1_{[a, b]}J \in T\Omega_\gamma\) has \(E_{**} = 0\) by [V9.15, §6.5], so vanishes by (i), and \(J = 0\) by [V9.2, §6.4]; onto by dimension. \(\square\)

Definitions (broken Jacobi fields) [V9.17]. Fix \(0 < \tau \le 1\) and \(B\) fine for \([0, \tau]\). The fields along \(\gamma|[0, \tau]\) are the \(X \in T\Omega_\gamma\) vanishing off \([0, \tau]\) Chapter9/BrokenJacobifieldsUpTo; they vanish at \(\tau\). \(X\) is a broken Jacobi field if on each piece of \(\{0\} \cup B \cup \{\tau\}\) it agrees with an element of \(\mathcal J\) Chapter9/BrokenJacobiIsBrokenJacobi; those along \(\gamma|[0, \tau]\) form \(\mathcal B_\tau\) Chapter9/BrokenJacobibrokenSpace, and the fields along \(\gamma|[0, \tau]\) vanishing on \(B\) form \(T'_\tau\) Chapter9/BrokenJacobinodeZero. A broken Jacobi field is determined by its values at \(0\), \(\tau\) and on \(B\), which may be any tangent vectors Chapter9/BrokenJacobiIsBrokenJacobi.eqOn_zero Chapter9/BrokenJacobiexists_isBrokenJacobi, piece by piece by [V9.16, §6.5] (ii). So \(X \mapsto (X(b))_{b \in B}\) is an isomorphism of \(\mathcal B_\tau\) onto \(\Sigma = \bigoplus_{b \in B}T_{\gamma(b)}N\) Chapter9/IndexReductionnodeEval_bijective.

Lemma 15.3 [V9.18]. The fields along \(\gamma|[0, \tau]\) are \(\mathcal B_\tau \oplus T'_\tau\) Chapter9/IndexReductionisCompl_broken_nodeZero; \(E_{**}(X, Y) = -2\sum_{b \in B}\langle Y(b), P\Delta_bX\rangle\) for \(X \in \mathcal B_\tau\) and \(Y\) along \(\gamma|[0, \tau]\) Chapter9/BrokenJacobienergyHessian_broken_eq, so \(E_{**}(\mathcal B_\tau, T'_\tau) = 0\); and \(E_{**}\) is positive definite on \(T'_\tau\) Chapter9/BrokenJacobienergyHessian_nodeZero_pos. Proof. \(X = W + (X - W)\), \(W\) the broken field with \(W = X\) on \(B\); the formula is [V9.15, §6.5]; positivity is [V9.16, §6.5] (i), a field of \(T'_\tau\) vanishing at the start of each piece. \(\square\)

Milnor proves this, the fineness of subdivisions and Assertion (2) by minimal geodesics; [V9.16, §6.5] (i) replaces them.

Definition (\(\lambda(\tau)\)) [V9.20]. \(\lambda(\tau)\) is the index of \(E_{**}\) on the fields along \(\gamma|[0, \tau]\) Chapter9/IndexReductionindexUpTo. Then \(\lambda(1) = \operatorname{index}E_{**}\) Chapter9/IndexReductionindexUpTo_one; \(\lambda\) is nondecreasing (Assertion (1)); and \(\lambda(\tau) = 0\) for \(0 < \tau \le h_0\) (Assertion (2): [V9.16, §6.5] (i) with the zero at \(0\)) Chapter9/IndexReductionindexUpTo_mono Chapter9/IndexReductionindexUpTo_eq_zero.

Lemma 15.4 [V9.19]. \(\lambda(\tau)\) is the index of \(E_{**}\) on \(\mathcal B_\tau\) Chapter9/IndexReductionlemma_15_4, so \(\lambda(\tau) \le \dim\mathcal B_\tau < \infty\) Chapter9/IndexReductionindexUpTo_lt_top; and the nullity of \(E_{**}\) on \(\mathcal B_\tau\) is \(\nu(\tau)\) Chapter9/IndexReductionfinrank_ker_broken. Proof. [V9.14, §6.5] (3) with Lemma 15.3. For the nullity, \(J \mapsto \mathbf 1_{[0, \tau]}J\) maps the \(J \in \mathcal J\) vanishing at \(0, \tau\) injectively onto the null space: its image is null by the jump formula; and a null \(X\), tested against the broken field with values \(P\Delta_bX\), has no tangential jumps, hence is one Jacobi field on \([0, \tau]\) by [V9.2, §6.4] Chapter9/IndexReductioneq_jacobi_of_jumps_zero. \(\square\)

Lemma 15.C [V9.21]. Fix \(B\); \(\tau\) is valid if \(0 < \tau \le 1\) and \(B\) is fine for \([0, \tau]\) Chapter9/IndexContinuityvalidFor. For valid \(\tau\) let \(H_\tau(x, y) = E_{**}(W^\tau_x, W^\tau_y)\) on \(\Sigma\), with \(W^\tau_x \in \mathcal B_\tau\) equal to \(x\) on \(B\) (\(H_\tau = 0\) otherwise) Chapter9/IndexContinuityHform. \(H_\tau\) is symmetric, with index \(\lambda(\tau)\) and nullity \(\nu(\tau)\) Chapter9/IndexContinuityformIndex_Hform Chapter9/IndexContinuityfinrank_ker_Hform, and \(\tau \mapsto H_\tau(x, y)\) is continuous on the valid \(\tau\) Chapter9/IndexContinuitycontinuousWithinAt_Hform. If \(B\) is fine for \([0, \tau]\) with last point \(m\) of \(\{0\} \cup B\) within \(h_0/2\) of \(\tau\), every \(\tau' \in (m, \tau + h_0/2)\), \(\tau' \le 1\), is valid Chapter9/IndexContinuitymem_validFor_of_near. Proof. Index and nullity by Lemma 15.4 and [V9.17, §6.5]. For continuity, \(W^\tau_x\) does not depend on \(\tau\) on \([0, \max B]\), so only the projected right derivative \(z(\tau)\) at \(m = \max B\) varies; it solves \(L(\tau)z(\tau) = c(\tau)\), with \(L(\tau)z\) the first component at \(\tau\) of \(\mathrm{jac}_m(0, z)\) and \(c\) likewise continuous Chapter9/JacobiODEcontinuous_linFlow. \(L(\tau_0)\) is injective by [V9.16, §6.5] (ii), as \(\tau_0 - m \le h_0\), and the solution of a linear system with injective limit is continuous Chapter9/IndexContinuitycontinuousWithinAt_of_injective. \(\square\)

Assertion (3) [V9.22]. For \(0 < \tau \le 1\), \(\lambda(\tau') = \lambda(\tau)\) for \(\tau' < \tau\) near \(\tau\) Chapter9/IndexAssertionsassertion_3. Proof. With \(B\) as in [V9.16, §6.5] (iii), \(\lambda(\tau)\) is attained on some \(S \subseteq \Sigma\) for \(H_\tau\), which stays negative definite for \(H_{\tau'}\), \(\tau' < \tau\) near \(\tau\), by [V9.14, §6.5] (2) and [V9.21, §6.5]; so \(\lambda(\tau') \ge \lambda(\tau)\); and Assertion (1). \(\square\)

Assertion (4) [V9.23]. For \(0 < \tau < 1\), \(\lambda(\tau') = \lambda(\tau) + \nu(\tau)\) for \(\tau' > \tau\) near \(\tau\) Chapter9/IndexAssertionsassertion_4. Proof. “\(\le\)” Chapter9/IndexAssertionsassertion_4_le: \(H_\tau\) is positive definite on some \(P \subseteq \Sigma\) of dimension \(\dim\Sigma - \lambda(\tau) - \nu(\tau)\), so is \(H_{\tau'}\) for \(\tau' > \tau\) near \(\tau\), and [V9.14, §6.5] (1) applies. “\(\ge\)”, for all \(\tau' \in (\tau, 1]\) Chapter9/IndexAssertionsassertion_4_ge: let \(U\) span a negative definite space of dimension \(k = \lambda(\tau)\) along \(\gamma|[0, \tau]\), and \(J_1, \dots, J_\nu\) be a basis of \(\{J \in \mathcal J : J(0) = J(\tau) = 0\}\). By [V9.15, §6.5], \(E_{**}(\mathbf 1_{[0, \tau]}J, Z) = 2\langle Z(\tau), \frac{DJ}{dt}(\tau)\rangle\) Chapter9/IndexAssertionsenergyHessian_cut. The \(d_h = \frac{DJ_h}{dt}(\tau)\) are independent [V9.2, §6.4]; take tangent \(x_k\) with \(\langle d_h, x_k\rangle = \delta_{hk}\) and \(X_k = \varphi Px_k\), \(\varphi\) a bump with \(\varphi(\tau) = 1\) supported in \((0, \tau')\). [V9.14, §6.5] (4) with \(Jb = \sum b_h\mathbf 1_{[0, \tau]}J_h\), \(Yb = \sum b_kX_k\) gives \(\lambda(\tau') \ge k + \nu\), as \(U\) vanishes at \(\tau\). \(\square\)

Theorem 15.1 (the Morse index theorem) [V9.24]. Let \(\gamma \in \Omega(N; p, q)\) be an unbroken geodesic. Finitely many \(t \in (0, 1)\) are conjugate to \(0\) along \(\gamma\), and \[\operatorname{index}E_{**} = \sum_{0 < t < 1}\nu(t)\] Chapter9/IndexTheoremtheorem_15_1. For any smooth curve \(\gamma\) in \(N\) the same holds with \(\lambda(1)\) on the left Chapter9/IndexTheoremindexUpTo_one_eq. Proof. Let \(\ell, \nu : \mathbb R \to \mathbb N\) and \(h_0 > 0\), with \(\ell\) nondecreasing on \((0, 1]\), \(\ell = 0\) on \((0, h_0]\), \(\ell(\tau') = \ell(\tau)\) for \(\tau' < \tau\) near \(\tau\) (\(0 < \tau \le 1\)) and \(\ell(\tau') = \ell(\tau) + \nu(\tau)\) for \(\tau' > \tau\) near \(\tau\) (\(0 < \tau < 1\)). Then \(\nu \ne 0\) at finitely many \(t \in (0, 1)\) and \(\ell(1) = \sum_{0 < t < 1}\nu(t)\) Chapter9/IndexTheoremeq_finsum_of_jumps: a finite \(F \subseteq (0, \tau)\) has \(\sum_F\nu \le \ell(\tau)\) (induction on \(\max F\)), which gives finiteness; \(\nu = 0\) below \(h_0\); and \(\ell(\tau) - \sum_{t < \tau}\nu(t)\) is locally constant on \((0, 1]\) and \(0\) near \(0\). Apply this to \(\ell = \lambda\), finite by Lemma 15.4, with Assertions (1)–(4); then \(\lambda(1) = \operatorname{index}E_{**}\) [V9.20, §6.5], and conjugacy is \(\nu(t) > 0\) [V9.4, §6.4]. \(\square\)

Milnor’s “clearly follows” hides this finiteness.

7. The path space and the fundamental theorem

This chapter proves Theorems 17.1 and 17.3 and builds the finite-dimensional model of Milnor’s §16, which Theorem 22.1 and Bott periodicity also use. Throughout, \(N \subseteq V\) is a slice submanifold, \(p, q \in V\), \(\rho\) the distance [V7.18, §5.7], \(\Omega = \Omega(N; p, q)\) [V8.1, §6.1], \(E = E_0^1\) the energy [V8.5, §6.1], \(\Omega^a = \{E \le a\}\), and a geodesic of \(\Omega\) is an unbroken geodesic [V8.10, §6.2], with the index and nullity of \(E_{**}\) [V8.14, §6.3; V9.13, §6.5]. Theorem 16.3, Corollaries 17.2, 17.4 and 17.5, the spheres, Milnor’s map \(h\), and Examples 2–3 and the Corollary of the Appendix are not needed.

7.1 Milnor’s metric

Paths are maps \(\mathbb R \to V\) of which only \([0, 1]\) matters; \(\dot s_\omega = \|\omega'\|\) is the speed.

Proposition (Milnor’s metric) [V10.1]. For \(\omega, \eta \in \Omega\), \[d(\omega, \eta) = \sup_{0 \le t \le 1}\rho(\omega(t), \eta(t)) + \Big(\int_0^1(\dot s_\omega - \dot s_\eta)^2\,dt\Big)^{1/2}\] is an extended pseudometric on \(\Omega\), and paths that agree on \([0, 1]\) are at distance \(0\). Chapter10/PathMetricPathSp.instPseudoEMetricSpace Chapter10/OmegaPathSp.edist_eq_zero_of_eqOn

Proof. The triangle inequality pointwise, resp. Minkowski’s (velocities are continuous on closed pieces); both terms see only \([0, 1]\). \(\square\)

From now on \(\Omega\) carries the topology of \(d\). It is not Hausdorff, but a map agreeing on \([0, 1]\) with a path of \(\Omega\) lies in \(\Omega\), and a map into \(\Omega\) at distance \(0\) from a continuous map is continuous Chapter10/DeformationPathSp.continuous_of_edist_eq_zero.

Lemma 16.A (the energy is continuous) [V10.2]. For \(0 \le a \le b \le 1\), \(|\sqrt{E_a^b(\omega)} - \sqrt{E_a^b(\eta)}| \le (\int_0^1(\dot s_\omega - \dot s_\eta)^2)^{1/2}\). So \(\sqrt{E_a^b}\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz for \(d\) and \(E_a^b\) is continuous on \(\Omega\). Chapter10/PathMetricPathSp.abs_sqrt_energy_sub_le Chapter10/PathMetricPathSp.continuous_energy

Proof. \(\sqrt{E_a^b} = \|\dot s\|_{L^2[a, b]}\): Minkowski on \([a, b]\), then enlarge \([a, b]\) to \([0, 1]\). \(\square\)

7.2 Broken geodesics

Definition (Milnor’s data) [V10.3]. Let \(c > 0\) and \(S = \{x \in N : \rho(p, x) \le \sqrt c\}\). Milnor’s data are \(p, q \in N\); \(c\) with \(S\) compact; \(\delta > 0\) such that any \(y, z \in S\) with \(\rho(y, z) < \delta\) are joined as in Corollary 10.8 [V7.20, §5.7] at the scale \(\delta\) (a unique \(v \in T_yN\) with \(\|v\| < \delta\), \(\exp_yv = z\); then \(\|v\| = \rho(y, z)\), and \(v\) depends smoothly on \((y, z)\)), and \(\delta\) is at most a normal radius [V7.9, §5.4] at each point of \(S\); and a subdivision \(0 = t_0 < \dots < t_{m+1} = 1\) with \(c\,\ell_i < \delta^2\), \(\ell_i = t_{i+1} - t_i\). \(B\) is the set of \(\omega \in \Omega\) with \(E(\omega) < c\) that are geodesics on each \((t_i, t_{i+1})\), and \(B^a = B \cap \Omega^a\). Chapter10/BrokenBrokenSetup Chapter10/BrokenPathsBrokenSetup.brokenPaths

Lemma (Milnor’s choices) [V10.3]. (i) If \(E(\omega) \le c\), then \(\omega([0, 1]) \subseteq S\). (ii) If \(N\) is closed in \(V\), \(S\) is compact. (iii) For compact \(K \subseteq N\) some \(\delta > 0\) joins points of \(K\) at distance \(< \delta\) as in Corollary 10.8 at the scale \(\delta\) and is at most a normal radius on \(K\). (iv) If \(p, q \in N\) and \(S\) is compact, there is \(\eta > 0\) such that every subdivision with all \(\ell_i < \eta\) is part of Milnor’s data; some uniform one is. Chapter10/BrokenisCompact_closedRiemBall_of_isClosed Chapter10/Brokencorollary_10_8' Chapter10/Brokenexists_brokenSetup_uniform

Proof. (i) \(\rho(p, \omega(t))^2 \le (L_0^t)^2 \le tE_0^t \le c\) [V8.5, §6.1]. (ii) \(S\) is closed and \(\|x - p\| \le \rho(p, x)\) [V7.21, §5.7]. (iii) Cover \(K\) by finitely many neighbourhoods of the local Corollary 10.8 and Lemma 10.3; take the least scale. (iv) \(\eta = \delta^2/c\). \(\square\)

Fix Milnor’s data. For \(y \in V^m\) put \(x_0 = p\), \(x_j = y_j\), \(x_{m+1} = q\), \(\rho_i = \rho(x_i, x_{i+1})\), \[E'(y) = \sum_{i=0}^m\frac{\rho_i^2}{\ell_i}, \qquad U = \{y \in N^m : \text{all } \rho_i < \infty,\ E'(y) < c\},\] and let \(v(x, x')\) be the vector of Corollary 10.8 from \(x\) to \(x'\) (\(0\) if there is none).

Lemma 16.1 [V10.4]. (i) \(U = N^m \cap O\) for an open \(O \subseteq V^m\); for every open \(O\), \(N^m \cap O\) is a slice submanifold of \(V^m\) modelled on \(Z^m\), with tangent space \(\prod_jT_{y_j}N\) at \(y\). (ii) For \(y \in U\) the broken geodesic \(\omega_y\), equal on \([t_i, t_{i+1}]\) to \(\tau \mapsto \exp_{x_i}(\frac{\tau - t_i}{\ell_i}v(x_i, x_{i+1}))\), lies in \(B\), has break points \((\omega_y(t_1), \dots, \omega_y(t_m)) = y\), and \(E(\omega_y) = E'(y)\). (iii) For \(\omega \in B\) the break points \(y\) of \(\omega\) lie in \(U\), and \(\omega_y = \omega\) on \([0, 1]\). Chapter10/BrokenPathsBrokenSetup.lemma_16_1 Chapter10/BrokenEnergyBrokenSetup.exists_isOpen_nodes Chapter10/ProducttangentSubspace_pi_inter

Proof. (ii) For \(y \in U\), \(\rho_i^2 \le \ell_iE'(y) < c\,\ell_i < \delta^2\), and by Cauchy–Schwarz \(\rho(p, x_k)^2 \le (\sum_i\rho_i)^2 \le (\sum_i\ell_i)E'(y) < c\): the vertices lie in \(S\) and consecutive ones are joined. Each segment is a geodesic of constant speed \(\rho_i/\ell_i\), whence the energy. (iii) A piecewise smooth path that is a geodesic on \((t_i, t_{i+1})\) is smooth on \([t_i, t_{i+1}]\), hence the radial geodesic \(\exp_{\omega(t_i)}(\frac{\tau - t_i}{\ell_i}w)\) of its initial velocity [V9.9, §6.4], with \(\|w\|^2 = \ell_iE_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}}(\omega) < \delta^2\) and \(\rho_i \le \|w\|\) Chapter10/BrokenPathsBrokenSetup.exists_segVec; uniqueness in Corollary 10.8 gives \(w = v(\omega(t_i), \omega(t_{i+1}))\), and \(E' \le E(\omega) < c\). (i) The gaps \((\rho_i)_i \in [0, \infty]^{m+1}\) are continuous on \(N^m\) [V7.21, §5.7]; products of slice charts, restricted to open sets, are slice charts. \(\square\)

7.3 The energy on the manifold of break points

Write \(U^a = \{y \in U : E'(y) \le a\}\).

Theorem 16.2: smoothness and compactness [V10.6]. (i) Every \(y_0 \in U\) has an open neighbourhood \(O \subseteq V^m\) and a function smooth on \(O\) equal to \(E'\) on \(U \cap O\); so \(E'\) is continuous on \(U\). (ii) For \(a < c\), \(U^a\) is compact. Chapter10/BrokenEnergyBrokenSetup.exists_smooth_energy' Chapter10/BrokenEnergyBrokenSetup.isCompact_sublevel

Proof. (i) \(\rho\) is not smooth on the diagonal, but \(\rho_i^2 = \|v(x_i, x_{i+1})\|^2\) and, near \(y_0\), uniqueness identifies \(v\) with the smooth map of Corollary 10.8. (ii) \(U^a \subseteq S^m\). If \(\rho(p, q) = \infty\), \(U = \emptyset\); otherwise the gaps are finite on \(S^m\), \(E'\) is continuous there, and \(U^a = S^m \cap \{E' \le a\}\). \(\square\)

Theorem 16.2: critical points [V10.9]. Let \(O \subseteq V^m\) be open with \(N^m \cap O \subseteq U\), and \(F : V^m \to \mathbb R\) smooth with \(F = E'\) on \(N^m \cap O\). For \(y \in N^m \cap O\) and \(w \in \prod_jT_{y_j}N\), \(dF_y(w) = -2\sum_j\langle w_j, \Delta_{t_j}\omega_y'\rangle\); and \(y\) is a critical point of \(F|(N^m \cap O)\) [V1.4, §1.2] if and only if \(\omega_y\) is a geodesic. Every geodesic \(\gamma \in \Omega\) with \(E(\gamma) < c\) has its break points \(y\) in \(U\), with \(\omega_y = \gamma\) on \([0, 1]\), \(\omega_y\) a geodesic and \(E'(y) = E(\gamma)\). Chapter10/BrokenVariationBrokenSetup.fderiv_eq_jumps Chapter10/BrokenVariationBrokenSetup.isCriticalPointM_iff Chapter10/FiniteBrokenSetup.eqOn_path_nodeVal_of_isUnbrokenGeodesic

Proof. Take a smooth curve \(y(u)\) in \(N^m \cap O\) with velocity \(w\). Then \(u \mapsto \omega_{y(u)}\) is a variation [V8.2, §6.1], smooth on each strip since a geodesic segment depends smoothly on its initial data over the whole segment [V9.9, §6.4], with variation field \(y'(0)_j\) at \(t_j\) Chapter10/BrokenVariationBrokenSetup.exists_variation_path. The acceleration vanishes on the segments, so the first variation [V8.7, §6.2] at \(\omega_y\) is \(-\sum_j\langle X(t_j), \Delta_{t_j}\omega_y'\rangle\), and \(F(y(u)) = E(\omega_{y(u)})\) gives the formula. At a critical point test with the tangent vector \(w = (\Delta_{t_j}\omega_y')_j\): all jumps vanish, and Corollary 12.3 [V8.11, §6.2] applies; conversely a geodesic has no jumps. A geodesic is broken for every subdivision; apply Lemma 16.1 (iii). \(\square\)

Lemma 15.4 for the subdivision of §16 [V10.10]. Let \(y \in U\) with \(\gamma = \omega_y\) a geodesic. (i) If \(J\) is a Jacobi field along \(\gamma\) and \(0 \le a\), \(0 < h\), \(a + h \le 1\), then \(s \mapsto J(hs + a)\) is a Jacobi field along \(s \mapsto \gamma(hs + a)\). (ii) \(t_i\) and \(t_{i+1}\) are not conjugate along \(\gamma\) [V9.4, §6.4]. (iii) \(W \mapsto (W(t_j))_j\) is a linear bijection from the broken Jacobi fields along \(\gamma\) with break points \(t_1, \dots, t_m\) [V9.17, §6.5] onto \(\prod_jT_{y_j}N\). (iv) \(E'(\omega(t_1), \dots, \omega(t_m)) \le E(\omega)\) for all \(\omega \in \Omega\); hence \(E_{**}(W, W) \ge 0\) for \(W \in T\Omega_\gamma\) vanishing at the \(t_j\), and \(> 0\) if moreover \(W \ne 0\) vanishes off \([0, 1]\). (v) Among the fields vanishing off \([0, 1]\), the broken Jacobi fields and those vanishing at the \(t_j\) are complementary; the index of \(E_{**}\) is that of its restriction to the broken Jacobi fields, whose null space has dimension the nullity of \(E_{**}\). Chapter10/BrokenSplittingBrokenSetup.brokenNodeMap_bijective Chapter10/BrokenSplittingBrokenSetup.formIndex_brokenSpace Chapter10/BrokenSplittingBrokenSetup.finrank_ker_brokenSpace

Proof. (i) The second covariant derivative and the curvature term scale by \(h^2\). (ii) The rescaled segment is \(s \mapsto \exp_{x_i}(sv_i)\) with \(\|v_i\| < \delta \le\) a normal radius; Remark 14.5 [V9.11, §6.4] and uniqueness for the Jacobi equation. (iii) Injective by (ii); surjective since by (ii) each segment carries a Jacobi field with given end values, and these glue. (iv) On each segment \(\rho(\omega(t_i), \omega(t_{i+1}))^2 \le \ell_iE_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}}(\omega)\). So along \(u \mapsto \exp_{\gamma(t)}(uW(t))\), which fixes the break points, the energy is \(\ge E'(y) = E(\gamma)\); its second derivative at \(0\), \(E_{**}(W, W)\) by Remark 13.5 [V8.17, §6.3], is \(\ge 0\) Chapter10/BrokenSplittingnonneg_of_isLocalMin_of_hasDerivAt. By the second variation formula broken Jacobi fields are \(E_{**}\)-orthogonal to fields vanishing at the \(t_j\); so if \(E_{**}(W, W) = 0\), Cauchy–Schwarz for the semidefinite form makes \(W\) a null vector, a Jacobi field [V9.5, §6.4] vanishing at \(t_0\) and \(t_1\), hence \(0\) by (ii). (v) \(X = X_b + (X - X_b)\), \(X_b\) the broken Jacobi field matching \(X\) at the \(t_j\); the abstract Lemma 15.B [V9.14, §6.5] gives the index. A null vector of the restriction has no projected jumps (test it against the broken Jacobi field with values \(P\Delta_{t_j}X'\)), so it is a Jacobi field vanishing at \(0\) and \(1\), and conversely; these form a space of dimension the nullity [V9.6, §6.4]. \(\square\)

Hidden hypothesis. Milnor quotes Lemma 15.4 [V9.19, §6.5], proved for subdivisions fine in the sense of §15, which the subdivision of §16 need not be; (iv)–(v) use the normal radius and the minimality of broken geodesics instead.

Theorem 16.2: index and nullity [V10.11]. With \(O\), \(F\) as in [V10.9, §7.3] and \(y \in N^m \cap O\) such that \(\omega_y\) is a geodesic, the index and the nullity of \(F|(N^m \cap O)\) at \(y\) are those of \(E_{**}\) at \(\omega_y\); in particular this index is finite. Chapter10/BrokenIndexBrokenSetup.theorem_16_2_index

Proof. Let \(x\) be the parametrization of the product slice chart at \(y = x(z_0)\), and \(\Lambda z\) the broken Jacobi field with values \(dx_{z_0}(z)_j\) at the \(t_j\), an isomorphism by [V10.10, §7.3] Chapter10/BrokenIndexBrokenSetup.chartBrokenEquiv. Along \(y(u) = x(z_0 + uz)\), \(F(y(u)) = E(\omega_{y(u)})\); the second derivative at \(0\) is on the left the Hessian of \(F \circ x\) at \((z, z)\), on the right \(E_{**}(W, W)\) for the variation field \(W\) [V8.17, §6.3]. On each segment \(W\) is a Jacobi field along the rescaled segment (Lemma 14.3 [V9.8, §6.4]) with the end values of \(\Lambda z\), so \(W = \Lambda z\) Chapter10/BrokenIndexBrokenSetup.hessian_eq_energyHessian. Polarize, compute index and nullity in the chart [V1.4, §1.2], and apply [V10.10, §7.3] (v). \(\square\)

Lemma (smooth extension of \(E'\)) [V10.12]. (i) If \(K \subseteq S'\) are subsets of a finite-dimensional normed space, \(K\) compact, and near each point of \(K\) the function \(f\) agrees on \(S'\) with a function smooth on an open set, then a smooth function agrees with \(f\) on \(K\). (ii) For \(b < c\) some smooth \(F\) on \(V^m\) equals \(E'\) on \(U^b\). Chapter10/SublevelCWexists_contDiff_eq_of_locally Chapter10/FiniteBrokenSetup.exists_contDiff_eq_energy'

Proof. (i) Glue finitely many local functions with a smooth partition of unity. (ii) (i) and [V10.6, §7.3]. \(\square\)

For \(y \in U\), \(\operatorname{ind}(y) \in \mathbb N\) is the index of \(E_{**}\) at \(\omega_y\) (\(0\) if infinite) Chapter10/FiniteBrokenSetup.geodIndex.

The Remark on p. 92 [V10.14]. Every \(\omega \in \Omega\) with \(E(\omega) < c\) has its break points in \(U\), with \(E'\) of them \(\le E(\omega)\). If some \(\omega_0 \in \Omega\) has \(E(\omega_0) < c\), there is \(y \in U\) with \(\omega_y\) a geodesic and \(E(\omega_y) \le E(\omega)\) for all \(\omega \in \Omega\).
