7.4 The deformation of \(\Omega^a\) onto \(B^a\)

Lemma 16.C (Milnor’s deformation \(r_u\)) [V10.7]. For \(\omega \in \Omega\) with \(E(\omega) < c\), \(y\) its break points, and \(t_i \le u \le t_{i+1}\), let \(r_u(\omega)\) be \(\omega_y\) on \([0, t_i]\), the short geodesic \(\tau \mapsto \exp_{\omega(t_i)}(\frac{\tau - t_i}{u - t_i}v(\omega(t_i), \omega(u)))\) on \([t_i, u]\), and \(\omega\) on \([u, 1]\); the formulas of neighbouring segments agree at \(u = t_i\). On \([0, 1]\): \(r_u(\omega) \in \Omega\), \(E(r_u\omega) \le E(\omega)\), \(r_0\omega = \omega\), \(r_1\omega = \omega_y\), and \(r_u\omega = \omega\) if \(\omega \in B\). Let \(\bar r_u\omega\) be \(r_u\omega\) on \([0, 1]\) and \(\omega\) off it, and \(\bar r_u\omega = \omega\) if \(u \notin [0, 1]\) or \(E(\omega) \ge c\). Then \((u, \omega) \mapsto \bar r_u\omega\), \(\mathbb R \times \Omega \to \Omega\), is continuous on \([0, 1] \times \{E < c\}\). Chapter10/RetractionBrokenSetup.retr Chapter10/DeformationBrokenSetup.continuousOn_deform

Proof. \(\rho(\omega(t_i), \omega(u))^2 \le (u - t_i)E(\omega) < \delta^2\), so the short geodesic exists; Schwarz’s inequality on each segment bounds the energy; a sub-arc of a short geodesic is the short geodesic between its ends, so \(r_u\) fixes \(B\). For continuity let \(u_j \to u\) in one segment, \(\omega_j \to \omega\) (any filter); the segments glue by the agreement at the \(t_i\). Uniform part: paths of energy \(\le c\) satisfy \(\rho(\omega(s), \omega(\tau)) \le (c|\tau - s|)^{1/2}\), so pointwise convergence, from the continuity of short geodesics in their ends [V7.20, §5.7; V7.23, §5.8], is uniform. \(L^2\) part: on \([0, t_i]\) the speeds \(\rho_k/\ell_k\) converge; beyond \(\max(u_j, u)\) they are those of \(\omega_j\), \(\omega\); in between, a short geodesic over a short interval may be fast, but its energy \(\rho(\omega_j(t_i), \omega_j(u_j))^2/(u_j - t_i) \le E_{t_i}^{u_j}(\omega_j)\) is small by Lemma 16.B: if \(\omega_j \to \omega\), for every \(\varepsilon > 0\) there is \(\eta > 0\) with eventually \(E_a^b(\omega_j) < \varepsilon\) whenever \(b - a < \eta\) (Lemma 16.A and a bound on the speed of \(\omega\)) Chapter10/RetractionContPathSp.eventually_energy_lt Chapter10/RetractionConvBrokenSetup.tendsto_retrSeg. \(\square\)

Theorem 16.2: deformation retraction [V10.8]. \(\bar r_0 = \mathrm{id}\); \(E(\bar r_u\omega) \le E(\omega)\); \(\bar r_1\omega \in B\) if \(E(\omega) < c\); \(\bar r_u\omega = \omega\) for \(\omega \in B\), \(u \in [0, 1]\). So for \(a < c\), \(B^a\) is a strong deformation retract of \(\Omega^a\), and \(\bar r_1 : \Omega^a \to B^a\) and the inclusion are inverse homotopy equivalences. Chapter10/DeformationBrokenSetup.deform_one_mem_brokenPaths Chapter10/DeformationBrokenSetup.homotopyEquivBroken

Proof. [V10.7, §7.4] and Lemma 16.1 (ii). \(\square\)

Proposition (\(B^a\) and \(U^a\)) [V10.5]. \(y \mapsto \omega_y\) is continuous from \(U\) to \(\Omega\), \(\omega \mapsto (\omega(t_j))_j\) from \(\Omega\) to \(V^m\), and for every \(a\) they restrict to inverse homotopy equivalences between \(B^a\) and \(U^a\). Chapter10/OmegaBrokenSetup.continuous_pathP Chapter10/OmegaBrokenSetup.homotopyEquivNodes

Proof. The uniform part as in [V10.7, §7.4]; the speeds \(\rho_k(y)/\ell_k\) are continuous on \(U\); \(\|x - y\| \le \rho(x, y)\). One composite is the identity (Lemma 16.1 (ii)); the other agrees with the identity on \([0, 1]\) (Lemma 16.1 (iii)), so the homotopy equal to it for \(t < 1\) and to the identity at \(t = 1\) is at distance \(0\) from a projection, hence continuous. \(\square\)

7.5 Telescopes (Milnor’s Appendix)

Spaces are arbitrary; \(X_0 \subseteq X_1 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq X\).

Fact (homotopy equivalences) [VA.1] (standard). \(f\) is a homotopy equivalence if \(gf \simeq \mathrm{id}\), \(fg \simeq \mathrm{id}\) for some \(g\). Composites, maps homotopic to one, homotopy inverses, and maps with a left and a right homotopy inverse (the Assertion of p. 22 [V2.14, §2.7]) are homotopy equivalences. Appendix/TelescopeIsHomotopyEquiv Appendix/TelescopeIsHomotopyEquiv.of_leftInv_rightInv

Fact (telescopes) [VA.2, VA.3] (standard). \(X_\Sigma = \bigcup_nX_n \times [n, n + 1] \subseteq X \times \mathbb R\), and \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit of \(\{X_n\}\) if \(p(x, \tau) = x\) is a homotopy equivalence \(X_\Sigma \to X\). \((x, \tau) \in X_\Sigma\) iff \(x \in X_n\) for an integer \(n \le \tau\). If the \(X_n\) are closed, a function on \(P \times X_\Sigma\) continuous on each \(P \times X_n \times [n, n + 1]\) is continuous. Appendix/TelescopeIsHomotopyDirectLimit Appendix/Telescopecontinuous_of_stripMap

Fact (maps of telescopes; truncations) [VA.4, VA.5] (standard). If \(f\) maps each \(X_n\) into \(Y_n\), \(f_\Sigma(x, \tau) = (f(x), \tau)\) satisfies \(pf_\Sigma = fp\); between homotopy direct limits, \(f\) is a homotopy equivalence if \(f_\Sigma\) is. The truncations \(X^n_\Sigma = \{\tau \le n\}\) are closed, and \(x \mapsto (x, n)\) is a homotopy equivalence \(X_n \to X^n_\Sigma\). Appendix/TelescopeIsHomotopyEquiv.of_telescopeMap Appendix/TelescopeisHomotopyEquiv_truncIncl

Fact (a criterion; Example 1) [VA.6, VA.7] (standard). (i) If \(f : X \to \mathbb R\) is continuous, \(f \ge 0\), and \(f \ge n + 1\) off \(X_n\), then \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit of \(\{X_n\}\): \((x, (1 - s)f(x) + s\tau)\) deforms \(X_\Sigma\) onto the graph of \(f\). So \(X_\Sigma\) is that of its truncations (\(f = \tau + 1\)). (ii) If \(X\) is paracompact Hausdorff and each point lies in the interior of some \(X_n\), take \(f = \sum_nn\varphi_n\), \((\varphi_n)\) a partition of unity. (iii) If \(E : X \to \mathbb R\) is continuous and \(a_n \uparrow \infty\), \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit of \(\{E \le a_n\}\), for any \(X\): take \(f = \sum_j\min(1, \max(0, E - a_j + 1))\). Appendix/Examplesexample1 Appendix/ExamplesisHomotopyDirectLimit_sublevel

Fact (Theorem A, Milnor’s proof) [VA.9, VA.12] (standard). Let \(X\), \(Y\) be the homotopy direct limits of increasing \(\{X_n\}\), \(\{Y_n\}\), the \(Y_n\) closed, and let \(f : X \to Y\) map each \(X_n\) into \(Y_n\) by a homotopy equivalence. Then \(f\) is a homotopy equivalence. Appendix/TheoremAtheoremA

Proof idea. Case 1 [VA.10]: for closed \(X_n\) and \(\varphi|X_n \simeq \mathrm{id}\), Milnor’s homotopy \(h_u\) (its third line is \(h^{n+1}_{(4t-3)u}\), misprinted \((4 - 3t)u\)) deforms \(\varphi_\Sigma\) to a map \(\psi\) with \(\psi(x, n + t) = (x, n + 2t)\) for \(t \le \frac12\) and level \(n + 1\) for \(t \ge \frac12\), and every such \(\psi\) is a homotopy equivalence Appendix/TheoremAisHomotopyEquiv_of_milnorMap. Case 2 [VA.11]: Milnor’s \(G\), pasted on the strips of the \(Y_n\) (this needs them closed), makes \(Gf_\Sigma\) and \(f_\Sigma G\) preserve the closed truncations and restrict to maps homotopic to the identity at integer levels; Case 1 on the truncations, [VA.6, §7.5] and the Assertion make \(f_\Sigma\) a homotopy equivalence Appendix/TheoremAtheoremA_telescope; then [VA.4, §7.5]. \(\square\)

Fact (mapping telescopes) [VA.13, VA.14] (standard). For maps \(K_0 \xrightarrow{c_0} K_1 \to \cdots\), \(\operatorname{Tel}(K) = \bigsqcup_nK_n \times [0, 1]/(k, 1)_n \sim (c_nk, 0)_{n+1}\). Maps out of it (and homotopies) are given block by block with no closedness; it is the homotopy direct limit of its closed truncations \(\{\text{level} \le n\}\), and \(k \mapsto [k, 0]_n\) is a homotopy equivalence from \(K_n\) to the \(n\)-th one. The mapping telescope \(T_X\) of the inclusions \(X_n \subseteq X_{n+1}\) maps to \(X_\Sigma\) by a homotopy equivalence, and to \(X\) by one if \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit. Appendix/MappingTelescopeMappingTelescope.isHomotopyEquiv_levelIncl Appendix/MonotoneUnionisHomotopyEquiv_telescopeProj'

Fact (Theorem A) [VA.15] (standard). Theorem A holds for arbitrary increasing \(X_n\), \(Y_n\): run Milnor’s proof on \(T_X \to T_Y\), whose truncations are closed, and compare by [VA.14, §7.5]. Appendix/MonotoneUniontheoremA_general

Fact (comparison with a sequence) [VA.16] (standard). If \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit of increasing \(\{X_n\}\), \(K_0 \xrightarrow{c_0} K_1 \to \cdots\) are maps, and \(g_n : X_n \to K_n\) homotopy equivalences with \(c_ng_n \simeq g_{n+1}\) on \(X_n\), then \(X \simeq \operatorname{Tel}(K)\): Milnor’s \(G\), built from homotopy inverses of the \(g_n\), is continuous from \(\operatorname{Tel}(K)\) to \(X_\Sigma\) and a homotopy equivalence by [VA.12, §7.5] on truncations. Appendix/MonotoneUnionisHomotopyEquiv_compareMap Appendix/MonotoneUnionnonempty_homotopyEquiv_mappingTelescope

Definition (countable cell complexes) [VA.18]. \(j : L \to K\) attaches cells \((\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k)\) if \(K\) arises from \(L\) by attaching a \(\lambda_1\)-cell [V1.2, §1.1] along an arbitrary map, then a \(\lambda_2\)-cell, and so on. A cell tower with cells \(\mathrm{cells}_0, \mathrm{cells}_1, \dots\) is \(K_0 \to K_1 \to \cdots\) with \(K_0\) an iterated adjunction space with cells \(\mathrm{cells}_0\) [V2.11, §2.7] and \(K_n \to K_{n+1}\) attaching \(\mathrm{cells}_{n+1}\). \(X\) has the homotopy type of the countable cell complex with these cells if \(X \simeq \operatorname{Tel}(K)\) for such a tower (the telescope stands for \(\bigcup_nK_n\)). Appendix/MonotoneUnionCellTower Appendix/MonotoneUnionIsCountableCellComplexType

Fact (towers) [VA.19] (standard). If \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit of increasing \(\{X_n\}\) and \(g_n : X_n \to K_n\) are homotopy equivalences to the stages of a cell tower with \(c_ng_n \simeq g_{n+1}\) on \(X_n\), then \(X\) has the homotopy type of the countable cell complex. (By [VA.16, §7.5].) Appendix/MonotoneUnionisCountableCellComplexType_of_tower

Definition (\(\Omega^*\)) [V10.15]. \(\Omega^*\) is the set of continuous \(\omega : [0, 1] \to V\) with values in \(N\), \(\omega(0) = p\), \(\omega(1) = q\), with the uniform distance \(d^*\) (the compact-open topology). \(i : \Omega \to \Omega^*\) restricts to \([0, 1]\); \(d^*(i\omega, i\eta) \le d(\omega, \eta)\) [V7.21, §5.7], so \(i\) is continuous. Chapter10/FullPathSpacePathSp.edist_toPathC_le Chapter10/FullPathTheorempathIncl

Lemma (convergence controls velocities) [V10.16]. (i) If \(\omega_j \to \omega\) in \(\Omega\) (any filter), then \(\int_0^1\|\omega_j' - \omega'\|^2 \to 0\). (ii) If \(\omega_j(s) \to \omega(s)\) for all \(s \in [0, 1]\) and \(\int_0^1\|\omega_j' - \omega'\|^2 \to 0\), then \(\omega_j \to \omega\). (iii) If \(\Phi\) is \(C^1\) on an open set containing \(F_0([a, b])\), \(F_j \to F_0\) uniformly on \([a, b]\), all differentiable off finite sets, \(\int_a^b\|F_j'\|^2 \le C\) eventually and \(\int_a^b\|F_j' - F_0'\|^2 \to 0\), then \(\int_a^b\|(\Phi \circ F_j)' - (\Phi \circ F_0)'\|^2 \to 0\). Chapter10/FullPathSpacePathSp.tendsto_integral_norm_deriv_sub_sq Chapter10/FullPathSpacePathSp.tendsto_of_tendsto_apply_of_integral Chapter10/FullPathOmegatendsto_integral_deriv_comp_sub_sq

Proof. (i) Expand the square: energies converge [V10.2, §7.1], and \(\int\langle\omega_j', \omega'\rangle \to E(\omega)\) by integration by parts on the pieces of \(\omega\). (ii) Bounded energies make the paths uniformly \(\frac12\)-Hölder, so convergence is uniform; and \(|\|a\| - \|b\|| \le \|a - b\|\). (iii) Write the difference as \((D\Phi(F_j) - D\Phi(F_0))F_j' + D\Phi(F_0)(F_j' - F_0')\); \(D\Phi\) is bounded and uniformly continuous near \(F_0([a, b])\). \(\square\)

Lemma 17.B (good balls) [V10.17]. For \(y, z \in V\) let \(v(y, z)\) be the minimal join vector: the unique \(v \in T_yN\) with \(\exp_yv = z\) and \(\rho(y, z) = \|v\|\) for which Corollary 10.8 holds at some scale \(> \|v\|\) (\(0\) if none); let \(\sigma_{yz}(s) = \exp_y(s\,v(y, z))\). An open \(O \subseteq V\) is a good ball if, for one \(\delta\), any two points of \(N \cap O\) are at distance \(< \delta\) and joined as in Corollary 10.8 at the scale \(\delta\), and \(\sigma_{yz}([0, 1]) \subseteq N \cap O\) for \(y, z \in N \cap O\). (i) For \(x \in N\), the balls \(\{\|y - x\| < r\}\) are good for all small \(r\). (ii) Near each pair of points of a good ball, \((y, z, s) \mapsto \sigma_{yz}(s)\) is the restriction of a map smooth on an open set times \((-\varepsilon, 1 + \varepsilon)\). (iii) The balls \(O = \{\|y - x\| < r\}\), \(x \in N\), whose concentric balls of radius \(\le 2r\) are good and with \(N \cap \bar O\) compact, form with \(\sigma\) a join system: open sets, convex for \(\sigma\), with \(\sigma_{yz}(0) = y\), \(\sigma_{yz}(1) = z\), \(\sigma_{yy} = y\), one smooth map on a neighbourhood of \((N \cap O)^2 \times (-\varepsilon, 1 + \varepsilon)\) equal to \(\sigma\), and Lebesgue numbers for compact subsets of \(N\). Chapter10/GoodBallsexists_isGoodBall_ball Chapter10/GoodBallsIsGoodBall.exists_smooth_minGeo Chapter10/GoodJoingoodJoin

Proof. (i) Uniform joins: Lemma 10.3 read with \(\rho\) [V7.20, §5.7]. Convexity from the ambient distance: along a geodesic \((\|\gamma - x\|^2)'' = 2\|\gamma'\|^2 + 2\langle\gamma - x, \mathrm{II}(\gamma', \gamma')\rangle \ge 0\) while \(\gamma\) stays where \(R\|\mathrm{II}(v, v)\| \le \|v\|^2\), so a short geodesic between points of a small ball stays in it. (ii) Geodesics depend smoothly on initial data over compact intervals [V11.1, §6.4]; feed in the smooth vector of Corollary 10.8. (iii) Glue the local maps of (ii) over the compact \((N \cap \bar O)^2\) by a partition of unity Chapter10/GoodJoinexists_smooth_glue. \(\square\)

Lemma 17.C [V10.18]. Fix a join system. Let \(Y_k \subseteq \Omega^*\) consist of the paths each of whose dyadic pieces \(\omega([j2^{-k}, (j + 1)2^{-k}])\) lies in \(N \cap O\) for a good set \(O\), and \(X_k = i^{-1}(Y_k)\). (i) The \(Y_k\) are open, increasing, and cover \(\Omega^*\). (ii) Let \(b(\omega)(s) = \sigma_{\omega(j2^{-k})\,\omega((j+1)2^{-k})}(2^ks - j)\) on the \(j\)-th piece and \(H(\omega, u)(s) = \sigma_{\omega(s)\,b(\omega)(s)}(u)\). Then \(H\) is continuous \(Y_k \times [0, 1] \to Y_k\) for \(d^*\) and \(X_k \times [0, 1] \to X_k\) for \(d\), and \(b\) is continuous from \((Y_k, d^*)\) to \((X_k, d)\). (iii) \(i : X_k \to Y_k\) is a homotopy equivalence with homotopy inverse \(b\). Chapter10/FullPathDeformJoinSystem.YSet Chapter10/FullPathOmegaJoinSystem.continuous_interpΩ Chapter10/FullPathOmegaJoinSystem.isHomotopyEquiv_toY

Proof. (i) Compact-open topology; a Lebesgue number and uniform continuity. (ii) By convexity \(b(\omega)(s)\) and \(H(\omega, u)(s)\) stay in \(N \cap O\) on the \(j\)-th piece, where \(b(\omega)(s) = \Phi((\omega(j2^{-k}), \omega((j+1)2^{-k})), 2^ks - j)\) and \(H(\omega, u)(s) = \Phi((\omega(s), b(\omega)(s)), u)\) for the smooth \(\Phi\) of \(O\), also for nearby paths Chapter10/FullPathDeformJoinSystem.continuous_interp_star. For \(d\), [V10.16, §7.6] (ii) reduces continuity to pointwise convergence and \(L^2\) convergence of velocities, which [V10.16, §7.6] (iii) and (i) give on each piece. (iii) \(b \circ i \simeq \mathrm{id}\) through \(H(\omega, 1 - t)\), replaced at \(t = 1\) by \(\omega\) (distance \(0\)); \(i \circ b \simeq \mathrm{id}\) through \(H\). \(\square\)

Theorem 17.1 [V10.19]. For every slice submanifold \(N\) of \(V\), complete or not, and all \(p, q \in V\), the inclusion \(i : \Omega(N; p, q) \to \Omega^*(N; p, q)\), with Milnor’s metric on \(\Omega\) and the compact-open topology on \(\Omega^*\), is a homotopy equivalence. Chapter10/FullPathTheoremtheorem_17_1

Proof. Milnor’s map \(h\) is not continuous for \(d\); the formal proof replaces his variable subdivision by fixed dyadic ones on the open sets \(Y_k\) of the join system of [V10.17, §7.6] Chapter10/FullPathTheoremJoinSystem.isHomotopyEquiv_toPathC. \(\Omega^*\) is metric, hence paracompact Hausdorff, and the open \(Y_k\) exhaust it: it is their homotopy direct limit [VA.7, §7.5]. \(\Omega\) is not Hausdorff, but if \(Y\) is paracompact Hausdorff, every point of \(Y\) is interior to some \(B_n\) (increasing), and \(g : X \to Y\) is continuous, then \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit of the \(g^{-1}(B_n)\): pull the function of [VA.7, §7.5] (ii) back along \(g\) and apply [VA.6, §7.5] Chapter10/FullPathSpaceisHomotopyDirectLimit_preimage. So \(\Omega\) is the homotopy direct limit of the \(X_k\). Each \(i|X_k \to Y_k\) is a homotopy equivalence [V10.18, §7.6]; Theorem A for open pieces [VA.15, §7.5] concludes. \(\square\)

7.7 Theorem 17.3

Relative cell complexes [V10.20]. A map \(\iota : A \to X\) is, up to homotopy, the inclusion of \(A\) with cells \((\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k)\) attached if some \(j : A \to K\) attaches these cells [VA.18, §7.5] and some homotopy equivalence \(e : X \to K\) has \(e\iota \simeq j\). (i) If \(j : L \to K\) attaches cells and \(e : L \to L'\) is a homotopy equivalence, some \(j' : L' \to K'\) attaches the same cells, with a homotopy equivalence \(E : K \to K'\), \(Ej = j'e\). (ii) If \(\iota' : A' \to X'\) has the property and \(\alpha : A \to A'\), \(\beta : X \to X'\) are homotopy equivalences with \(\beta\iota \simeq \iota'\alpha\), then \(\iota\) has it, with the same cells. (iii) Let \(A_0 \subseteq A\) in a Hausdorff space \(M\), \(A\) closed, \(A_0 \to A\) with cells \(c\), and \(\chi_i : \mathbb R^{k_i} \to M\) continuous and injective on the unit ball \(D^{k_i}\), with disjoint images, \(\chi_i(z) \in A\) iff \(\|z\| = 1\) (\(z \in D^{k_i}\)). Then \(A_0 \to A \cup \bigcup_i\chi_i(D^{k_i})\) has cells \(c\) followed by the \(k_i\). (iv) (the relative Theorem 3.5) Let \(f = F|N\), \(F : V \to \mathbb R\) smooth, \(N^{a_0}\) compact, every critical point in \(N^{a_0}\) non-degenerate, and \(b \le a_0\), neither a critical value. Listing the critical points in \(f^{-1}(b, a_0)\) without repetition by non-decreasing value as \(p_1, \dots, p_j\), \(N^b \to N^{a_0}\) is, up to homotopy, the inclusion with cells \(\operatorname{index}(p_1), \dots, \operatorname{index}(p_j)\). (v) If \(X\) is the homotopy direct limit of increasing \(X_n\) (e.g. \(\{E \le a_n\}\), \(E\) continuous, \(a_n \uparrow \infty\)), \(X_0\) has the homotopy type of an iterated adjunction space with cells \(\mathrm{cells}_0\), and each \(X_n \to X_{n+1}\) is, up to homotopy, the inclusion with cells \(\mathrm{cells}_{n+1}\), then \(X\) has the homotopy type of the countable cell complex with cells \(\mathrm{cells}_0, \mathrm{cells}_1, \dots\). Chapter10/RelativeCellsIsRelCellComplexType Chapter10/RelativeCellsIsRelCellComplexType.of_square Chapter10/RelativeCellsisRelCellComplexType_sublevel_of_isCompact Chapter10/RelativeCellsisCountableCellComplexType_of_relSublevel

Proof. (i) Extend over one cell at a time by Lemma 3.7 [V2.14, §2.7]. (ii) Transport the attachment of \(\iota'\) along a homotopy inverse of \(\alpha\) by (i), and compose. (iii) Induction; one cell is attached by [V2.7, §2.4]. (iv) The critical points in \(N^{a_0}\) are finitely many [V1.11, §1.7]; induct on their number in \((b, a)\): with \(c\) the top critical value below a regular \(a\), Remark 3.3 [V2.9, §2.6] attaches the cells of the level \(c\), Theorem 3.1 [V2.3, §2.3] gives strong deformation retractions [V2.1, §2.1] across the slabs between, and (iii) adds the cells. (v) Inductively transport the attachment of \(X_n \to X_{n+1}\) along \(g_n : X_n \to K_n\) by (i), getting \(K_n \to K_{n+1}\) and \(g_{n+1}\) with \(c_ng_n \simeq g_{n+1}\) on \(X_n\): only homotopy-commutative squares, so no nested subdivisions are needed Chapter10/RelativeCellsisCountableCellComplexType_of_rel; then [VA.19, §7.5] and [VA.7, §7.5] (iii). \(\square\)

The step from \(\Omega^a\) to \(\Omega^b\) [V10.21]. Fix Milnor’s data and \(a \le b < c\) such that \(E'(y) \notin \{a, b\}\) whenever \(y \in U\) and \(\omega_y\) is a geodesic, and such that each such \(\omega_y\) with \(E'(y) \le b\) has nullity \(0\). (i) The \(y \in U\) with \(\omega_y\) a geodesic and \(a < E'(y) < b\) form a list \(y^{(1)}, \dots, y^{(k)}\) without repetition, by non-decreasing \(E'\), and the inclusion \(\Omega^a \to \Omega^b\) of sublevel sets of the continuous \(E : \Omega \to \mathbb R\) is, up to homotopy, the inclusion with cells \(\operatorname{ind}(y^{(1)}), \dots, \operatorname{ind}(y^{(k)})\). (ii) The \(y \in U\) with \(\omega_y\) a geodesic and \(E'(y) \le b\) are finitely many; if \(N\) is closed in \(V\), \(p, q \in N\) and all geodesics in \(\Omega\) have nullity \(0\), the energies \(\le b\) of geodesics in \(\Omega\) are finitely many, for every \(b\). (iii) For \(\gamma \in \Omega\) let \(\operatorname{ind}(\gamma) \in \mathbb N\) be the index of \(E_{**}\) at \(\gamma\) (\(0\) were it infinite); then \(\operatorname{ind}(\omega_y) = \operatorname{ind}(y)\). Proof. (i) Let \(c_1 = (b + c)/2\), \(F\) smooth with \(F = E'\) on \(U^{c_1}\) [V10.12, §7.3], and \(S = \{y \in U : E'(y) < c_1\} = N^m \cap O\), a slice submanifold [V10.4, §7.2]. For \(t \le b\) the sublevel set of \(F|S\) is \(U^t\), compact [V10.6, §7.3]; its critical points are the \(y\) with \(\omega_y\) a geodesic [V10.9, §7.3], with the index and nullity of \(E_{**}\) [V10.11, §7.3], so non-degenerate below \(b\). [V10.20, §7.7] (iv) gives the cells of \(U^a \to U^b\) Chapter10/FundamentalTheoremBrokenSetup.isRelCellComplexType_nodes. The homotopy equivalences \(\Omega^t \to U^t\), \(t < c\), of [V10.8, §7.4] and [V10.5, §7.4] are all \(\omega \mapsto ((\bar r_1\omega)(t_j))_j\) Chapter10/FundamentalTheoremBrokenSetup.omegaEquivNodes, so they commute with the inclusions, and [V10.20, §7.7] (ii) transports the cells. (ii) The critical points of \(F|S\) in the compact \(U^b\) are non-degenerate, hence isolated. For the energies take data with \(c = \max(b, 0) + 1\) [V10.3, §7.2] and use [V10.9, §7.3]. \(\square\)

Theorem 17.3 [V10.22]. Let \(N\) be closed in \(V\), \(p, q \in N\), and let \(E_{**}\) have nullity \(0\) at every geodesic of \(\Omega\) (Milnor’s non-conjugacy hypothesis implies this by Theorem 14.1 [V9.6, §6.4]). Then there are finite lists \(G_0, G_1, \dots\) of geodesics of \(\Omega\) such that every geodesic of \(\Omega\) agrees on \([0, 1]\) with an entry of some list; neither entries of different lists nor distinct entries of one list agree on \([0, 1]\); the energies increase strictly from a list to any later one and weakly along each list; and \(\Omega(N; p, q)\), with Milnor’s metric, has the homotopy type of the countable cell complex with cells \((\operatorname{ind}\gamma)_{\gamma \in G_0}, (\operatorname{ind}\gamma)_{\gamma \in G_1}, \dots\): one \(\lambda\)-cell for each geodesic from \(p\) to \(q\) of index \(\lambda\), counted by its values on \([0, 1]\), attached in order of energy. Chapter10/FundamentalTheoremtheorem_17_3

Proof. Let \(a_0 = -1\) and choose \(a_{n+1} \in (n, n + 1)\) that is not the energy of a geodesic, by [V10.21, §7.7] (ii). For each \(n\) take Milnor’s data with \(c_n = \max(a_{n+1}, 0) + 1\), which exist as \(S\) is compact [V10.3, §7.2]; [V10.21, §7.7] (i) on \([a_n, a_{n+1}]\) gives the cells of \(\Omega^{a_n} \to \Omega^{a_{n+1}}\), and \(G_{n+1}\) is the list of the corresponding broken geodesics, \(G_0 = \emptyset\) Chapter10/FundamentalTheoremtheorem_17_3_of_levels. \(\Omega^{a_0} = \emptyset\), and \(\Omega\) is the homotopy direct limit of the \(\Omega^{a_n}\), \(E\) being continuous [V10.2, §7.1]; [V10.20, §7.7] (v) concludes. A geodesic has energy in some \((a_k, a_{k+1})\) and agrees on \([0, 1]\) with the broken geodesic of its break points [V10.9, §7.3]; paths agreeing on \([0, 1]\) have equal energies, which separates the lists. \(\square\)

Hidden hypothesis. The levels must tend to \(\infty\), which Milnor does not require.

Lemma (the index sees only \([0, 1]\)) [V10.23]. Two geodesics \(\gamma, \gamma' \in \Omega\) that agree on \([0, 1]\) have the same index (needed only for Bott periodicity). Chapter10/SphereGeodesicsformIndex_energyHessian_congr

Proof. By the index theorem [V9.24, §6.5] both indices are sums over \(t \in (0, 1)\) of multiplicities of conjugate points, and Jacobi fields along curves that agree on \([0, 1]\) are the same. \(\square\)

8. Whole manifolds of minimal geodesics

This chapter proves Theorem 22.1: if every geodesic from \(p\) to \(q\) that is not of least energy has index \(\ge \lambda_0\), the space \(\Omega^d\) of minimal geodesics carries the homotopy groups of \(\Omega\) below \(\lambda_0 - 1\); and Corollary 22.2, \(\pi_i\Omega^d \cong \pi_{i+1}N\). Notation is that of Chapter 7. The corollaries and the variant for an open and closed set of paths serve Bott periodicity only. Corollary 22.3 (Freudenthal) and the sphere are not needed.

8.1 Homotopy groups and pushing maps

Fact (induced maps, compressions) (standard). A map \(f : X \to Y\) induces \(f_* : \pi_i(X, x) \to \pi_i(Y, f(x))\), \([\gamma] \mapsto [f \circ \gamma]\), functorially, a homomorphism for \(i \ge 1\). A map \(j : Y \to X\) compresses maps from \(P\) if every \(f : P \to X\) is homotopic, relative to \(f^{-1}(j(Y))\), to a map into \(j(Y)\). If an embedding \(j\) compresses maps from \(I^n\), then \(j_*\) is onto on \(\pi_n\) at every base point; if it compresses maps from \(I \times I^n\), \(j_*\) is one-to-one. Homotopy/BasichomotopyGroupMap Homotopy/BasicCompresses Homotopy/Basicsurjective_homotopyGroupMap_of_compresses Homotopy/Basicinjective_homotopyGroupMap_of_compresses

Proof idea. Compress a representative, resp. a homotopy between two images, relative to the boundary. \(\square\)

Fact (push-off) (standard). Let \(P\) be compact with a continuous injection into a real vector space of dimension \(< n\). (i) The inclusion \(Y \to Y \cup_\varphi e^n\) [V1.2, §1.1] compresses maps from \(P\). (ii) If \(M\) is Hausdorff, \(A \subseteq M\) closed, and \(\chi : \mathbb R^n \to M\) continuous and injective on \(D^n\) with \(\chi(z) \in A\) iff \(\|z\| = 1\) (\(z \in D^n\)), every map \(P \to A \cup \chi(D^n)\) is homotopic in \(A \cup \chi(D^n)\), relative to the preimage of \(A\), to a map into \(A\). Proof idea. Approximate the cell coordinate of the map on \(P\) by a smooth map from the lower-dimensional vector space (Stone–Weierstrass); it misses a point near the centre; translating that point to the centre frees a small ball, which is expanded radially over the cell. (ii) reduces to (i) by [V2.7, §2.4]. \(\square\)

Fact (base points) (standard). A path \(\omega\) from \(y_0\) to \(y_1\) induces a bijection \(\omega_\# : \pi_i(Y, y_0) \to \pi_i(Y, y_1)\); a homotopy \(H\) from \(f\) to \(g\) gives \(g_* = \omega_\# \circ f_*\) with \(\omega = H(\cdot, x_0)\). So homotopy equivalences and homeomorphisms induce bijections at every base point. For the loop space \(\Omega Y\) at \(y\), \(\pi_i(\Omega Y, \mathrm{const}) \cong \pi_{i+1}(Y, y)\), as groups for \(i \ge 1\). Definition (pushing maps) [V13.12]. For \(A, X \subseteq T\) and a space \(P\), \(A\) pushes maps from \(P\) out of \(X\) if every map \(h : P \to T\) with values in \(X\) is homotopic in \(T\), relative to \(h^{-1}(A)\), to a map into \(A\). It passes to subsets of \(X\); it is transitive (\(A \subseteq B\), \(A\) out of \(B\) and \(B\) out of \(X\) give \(A\) out of \(X\)); a strong deformation retract \(A\) of \(X\) pushes maps from every \(P\) out of \(X\). If \(T\) is Hausdorff, \(A\) closed, \(P\) compact with a continuous injection into a real vector space \(E\), and \(\chi_1, \dots, \chi_k\) are cells as in the push-off (ii), of dimensions \(> \dim E\), with disjoint images, then \(A\) pushes maps from \(P\) out of \(A \cup \bigcup_i\chi_i(D^{n_i})\). Chapter13/CompressionPushesInto Chapter13/CompressionpushesInto_of_isStrongDeformationRetract Chapter13/CompressionpushesInto_union_cells

Proof. Transitivity concatenates the two homotopies; the first fixes \(h^{-1}(B) \supseteq h^{-1}(A)\), so the second is relative to \(h^{-1}(A)\). Cells: the push-off (ii), by induction, the partial unions being closed. \(\square\)

Lemma D (passing levels of high index) [V13.13]. Let \(F : V \to \mathbb R\) be smooth, \(f = F|N\), \(N^{a_0}\) compact, \(a\) not a critical value, every critical point \(q\) with \(a < f(q) \le a_0\) non-degenerate of index \(\ge \lambda_0\), and \(P\) compact with a continuous injection into a real vector space of dimension \(< \lambda_0\). Then for \(a \le b < a_0\), \(N^a\) pushes maps from \(P\) out of \(N^b\). Chapter13/Compressionlemma_D

Proof. The critical points in \(f^{-1}[a, a_0]\) are finitely many [V1.11, §1.7]; induct on the number at levels \(\le b\). If there is none, \(N^a\) is a strong deformation retract of \(N^b\) (Theorem 3.1 [V2.3, §2.3], [V2.1, §2.1]). Otherwise let \(c\) be the top critical value \(\le b\), isolated Chapter13/Compressionexists_gap_of_finite; by Remark 3.3 [V2.9, §2.6] \(N^{c - \varepsilon}\) with cells of dimension \(\ge \lambda_0\) is a strong deformation retract of \(N^{c + \varepsilon}\); push from \(N^b\) into \(N^{c + \varepsilon}\), then into the cells, then off them into \(N^{c - \varepsilon}\), then by induction into \(N^a\). \(\square\)

8.2 Lemmas 22.4 and 22.5

Lemma 22.4 [V13.10]. Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, \(U \subseteq E\) open, \(K \subseteq U\) compact, \(f\) of class \(C^2\) on \(U\), and every critical point of \(f\) in \(K\), degenerate or not, of index \(\ge \lambda_0\). There is \(\varepsilon > 0\) such that every \(g : E \to \mathbb R\) with \(\|dg_x - df_x\| < \varepsilon\) and \(\|d^2g_x - d^2f_x\| < \varepsilon\) at each \(x \in K\) has all its critical points in \(K\) of index \(\ge \lambda_0\); likewise for \(g = f + h\), \(h\) of class \(C^2\) on \(U\) with first and second derivatives of norm \(< \varepsilon\) on \(K\). Chapter13/Perturbationlemma_22_4 Chapter13/Perturbationlemma_22_4_add

Proof. The index is the largest dimension of a subspace \(W\) on which the Hessian is negative definite [V1.3, §1.2]; compactness of the unit sphere of \(W\) gives \(H(v, v) \le -\mu\|v\|^2\) there, and every form within \(\mu\) of \(H\) is negative definite on \(W\) Chapter13/Perturbationexists_negDef_margin Chapter13/Perturbationle_index_of_norm_sub_lt. So near a critical \(x \in K\), \(g\) close to \(f\) has index \(\ge \lambda_0\); near a non-critical \(x\), \(\|df_x\| > 0\) keeps \(g\) non-critical. Compactness of \(K\) gives one \(\varepsilon\). \(\square\)

Lemma 22.4 on a submanifold [V13.11]. Let \(F : V \to \mathbb R\) be smooth, \(K \subseteq N\) compact, and every critical point of \(F|N\) in \(K\) of index \(\ge \lambda_0\). There is \(\delta > 0\) such that for every linear \(a : V \to \mathbb R\) with \(\|a\| < \delta\), every critical point of \((F + a)|N\) in \(K\) has index \(\ge \lambda_0\). Chapter13/Perturbationlemma_22_4_submanifold

Proof. In a slice chart with parametrization \(\phi\) [V1.6, §1.4], critical points and indices of \(F|N\) are those of \(F \circ \phi\), and on a closed ball the first two derivatives of \(a \circ \phi\) are at most \(C\|a\|\); apply Lemma 22.4 to \(F \circ \phi + a \circ \phi\), and cover \(K\) by finitely many charts Chapter13/Perturbationexists_perturb_slice. \(\square\)

Lemma 22.5 [V13.14]. Let \(F : V \to \mathbb R\) be smooth, \(f = F|N \ge d\), \(N^{a_0}\) compact, every critical point \(q\) with \(d < f(q) < a_0\) of index \(\ge \lambda_0\), and \(P\) compact with a continuous injection into a real vector space of dimension \(< \lambda_0\). Suppose \(M^0 = N^d\) has an open neighbourhood \(U\) in \(N\) out of which it pushes maps from \(P\). Then \(M^0\) pushes maps from \(P\) out of \(N^b\) for every \(b < a_0\). Chapter13/ManifoldOfMinimalemma_22_5_sublevel

Proof. Let \(b \ge d\). On the compact \(N^{a_0} \setminus U\), \(f \ge m_1 > d\); put \(\delta = \min(\frac{m_1 - d}4, \frac{a_0 - b}5)\). Lemma 22.4 [V13.11, §8.2] on \(K = f^{-1}[d + \delta, b + 4\delta]\) bounds \(\|\ell\|\); choose \(\ell\) linear, that small, with \((F + \ell)|N\) a Morse function (Corollary 6.8 [V4.22, §3.3]), and a bump function \(\beta\) equal to \(1\) on a ball containing \(N^{a_0}\) with \(|\beta\ell| < \delta\); let \(g = (F + \beta\ell)|N\). Below \(a_1 = b + 3\delta\), \(g\) has compact sublevel sets, and its critical points and Hessians are those of \((F + \ell)|N\) Chapter13/ManifoldOfMinimacriticalPoint_hessianM_congr: non-degenerate, of index \(\ge \lambda_0\) above \(d + \delta\). For a regular value \(\alpha \in (d + 2\delta, d + 3\delta)\) of \(g\), Lemma D [V13.13, §8.1] makes \(g^\alpha\) push out of \(g^{\max(b + \delta, \alpha)} \supseteq N^b\), and \(M^0 \subseteq g^\alpha \subseteq U\); use transitivity. \(\square\)

8.3 Theorem 22.1

Definition (\(\Omega^d\)) [V13.1]. \(\Omega^d\) is the set of \(\gamma \in \Omega\) with \(E(\gamma) \le E(\gamma')\) for all \(\gamma' \in \Omega\). A path of least energy is a geodesic: its energy has a minimum at \(0\) along every variation, so Corollary 12.3 [V8.11, §6.2] applies. Chapter13/Theorem22minPaths Chapter13/MinimalDeformisUnbrokenGeodesic_of_minimal

Lemma (a neighbourhood of the minima) [V13.15]. Fix Milnor’s data [V10.3, §7.2], \(O \subseteq V^m\) open with \(N^m \cap O \subseteq U\), and \(d < c\). Suppose \(\{E \le d\}\) is a retract of an open \(O_r \subseteq \Omega\) containing it, by a map \(R\) continuous on \(O_r\). Then \(M^0 = \{y \in N^m \cap O : E'(y) \le d\}\) has an open neighbourhood in \(N^m \cap O\) out of which it pushes maps from every \(P\). Chapter13/MinimalDeformBrokenSetup.exists_pushesInto_nodes

Proof. Where \(\omega_y \in O_r\), let \(s(y)\) be the break points of \(R(\omega_y)\): continuous [V10.5, §7.4], with \(E'(s(y)) \le d\) [V10.14, §7.3], and \(s = \mathrm{id}\) on \(M^0\). Where every \(\rho(y_i, s(y)_i) < \delta\), the break points lying in \(S\) Chapter13/MinimalDeformBrokenSetup.mem_ball_of_mem_nodes, \(D(y, \theta)_i = \exp_{y_i}(\theta\,v(y_i, s(y)_i))\) is continuous [V7.23, §5.8], runs from \(y\) to \(s(y)\), and fixes \(M^0\) since \(v(x, x) = 0\) Chapter13/MinimalDeformBrokenSetup.joinVec_self. By the tube lemma its tracks stay in \(O\) near \(M^0\), and a deformation into \(M^0\) fixing \(M^0\) pushes maps Chapter13/ManifoldOfMinimapushesInto_of_deformation. \(\square\)

Theorem 22.1 [V13.2]. Let \(p, q \in N\), all closed balls \(\{x \in N : \rho(p, x) \le r\}\) compact, and \(\lambda_0 \in \mathbb N\) such that every geodesic \(\gamma \in \Omega\) with \(E(\gamma) > E(\gamma')\) for some \(\gamma' \in \Omega\) has index \(\ge \lambda_0\). Suppose \(\Omega^d\) is a retract of an open neighbourhood: there are an open \(O \supseteq \Omega^d\) and \(R : \Omega \to \Omega\), continuous on \(O\), with \(R(O) \subseteq \Omega^d\) and \(R = \mathrm{id}\) on \(\Omega^d\). Let \(P\) be compact with a continuous injection into a real vector space of dimension \(< \lambda_0\). Then every map \(h : P \to \Omega\) is homotopic, relative to \(h^{-1}(\Omega^d)\), to a map into \(\Omega^d\); that is, the inclusion \(\Omega^d \to \Omega\) compresses maps from \(P\). Chapter13/Theorem22theorem_22_1 Chapter13/Theorem22compresses_minPaths

Proof. (1) \(E \circ h \le c_0\) on \(P\) [V10.2, §7.1]; take Milnor’s data with \(c = c_0 + 3\) [V10.3, §7.2]. (2) By [V10.14, §7.3] some path has least energy \(d \le c_0\), so \(\Omega^d = \{E \le d\}\), and its paths are geodesics [V13.1, §8.3], hence in \(B\). (3) \(K_1(t, x) = \bar r_t(h(x))\) [V10.8, §7.4] lowers energy, ends in \(B\) and fixes \(B \supseteq \Omega^d\). (4) Let \(S = \{y \in U : E'(y) < c_0 + 2\} = N^m \cap O'\) and \(f = F|S\), \(F\) smooth with \(F = E'\) there [V10.12, §7.3]; \(f \ge d\) and \(\{f \le c_0 + 1\}\) is compact [V10.6, §7.3]. A critical point \(y\) of \(f\) with \(f(y) > d\) gives a geodesic \(\omega_y\) not of least energy [V10.9, §7.3], so of index \(\ge \lambda_0\), which is its index for \(f\) [V10.11, §7.3]. With the neighbourhood of [V13.15, §8.3], Lemma 22.5 [V13.14, §8.2] pushes \(h_2(x)\), the break points of \(K_1(1, x)\), into \(\{f \le d\}\) by a homotopy \(G_2\) relative to \(h_2^{-1}\{f \le d\}\). (5) \(K_2(t, x) = \omega_{G_2(t, x)}\) agrees with \(K_1(1, x)\) only on \([0, 1]\) (Lemma 16.1 [V10.4, §7.2]); replacing it by \(K_1(1, x)\) when \(t = 0\) or \(h(x) \in \Omega^d\) moves it by distance \(0\) and keeps it continuous. \(K_1\) followed by the modified \(K_2\) is the homotopy. \(\square\)

Hidden hypothesis. Milnor’s hypothesis that \(\Omega^d\) is a topological manifold enters his proof only through Hanner’s theorem, as a neighbourhood retraction, which is assumed here; his completeness of \(M\) is the compactness of the balls.

Corollary (homotopy groups) [V13.3]. Under the hypotheses of Theorem 22.1, for every \(\gamma \in \Omega^d\) and \(i \le \lambda_0 - 2\), \(\pi_0\) included, the inclusion induces a bijection \(\pi_i(\Omega^d, \gamma) \to \pi_i(\Omega, \gamma)\). Chapter13/Theorem22theorem_22_1_bijective

Proof. \(I^i\) and \(I \times I^i\) embed in \(\mathbb R^i\) and \(\mathbb R^{i+1}\), of dimension \(< \lambda_0\); apply the compression criteria. \(\square\)

Theorem 22.1 for an open and closed set of paths [V13.16]. Needed only for Bott periodicity for the orthogonal group. Keep the hypotheses of Theorem 22.1, but let \(\Omega' \subseteq \Omega\) be open and closed and require the index bound only for the geodesics in \(\Omega'\) that are not of least energy (in \(\Omega\)). Then every \(h : P \to \Omega'\) is homotopic, relative to \(h^{-1}(\Omega^d)\), to a map into \(\Omega^d \cap \Omega'\); so the inclusion \(\Omega^d \cap \Omega' \to \Omega'\) compresses maps from \(P\), and \(\Omega^d \to \Omega\) induces bijections on \(\pi_i\), \(1 \le i \le \lambda_0 - 2\), at every \(\gamma \in \Omega^d \cap \Omega'\). Proof. As for Theorem 22.1, with \(S\) cut down to the open set of \(y\) with \(\omega_y \in \Omega'\) [V10.5, §7.4]; it contains the break points of \(K_1(1, x)\), since open sets of \(\Omega\) are saturated for \(d\) Chapter13/ComponentwisePathSp.mem_of_edist_eq_zero; compactness uses that \(\Omega'\) is closed, and homotopies starting in \(\Omega'\) stay there. For \(i \ge 1\) the inclusion of an open and closed set containing the base point is bijective on \(\pi_i\) Homotopy/BundlesUnitarybijective_homotopyGroupMap_clopen, for \(\Omega^d \cap \Omega' \subseteq \Omega^d\) and \(\Omega' \subseteq \Omega\). \(\square\)

8.4 Corollary 22.2

Corollary 22.2 [V13.4]. Under the hypotheses of Theorem 22.1, for \(\gamma \in \Omega^d\) and \(i + 2 \le \lambda_0\) there is a bijection \(\pi_i(\Omega^d, \gamma) \cong \pi_{i+1}(N, p)\). Chapter13/Corollariescorollary_22_2

Proof. Compose six bijections: [V13.3, §8.3]; \(\Omega \to \Omega^*\), a homotopy equivalence by Theorem 17.1 [V10.19, §7.6]; the homeomorphism of \(\Omega^*\) with the space of paths from \(p\) to \(q\) in \(N\) Chapter13/CorollariespathCHomeomorph; \(\delta \mapsto \delta \cdot x^{-1}\), \(x\) the path \(\gamma\), a homotopy equivalence onto the loops at \(p\) sending \(x\) to \(x \cdot x^{-1}\); the change of base point along \(s \mapsto x|_{[0, s]} \cdot x|_{[0, s]}^{-1}\) to the constant loop Chapter13/CorollariescontractPath; and \(\pi_i(\Omega N) \cong \pi_{i+1}N\). \(\square\)

Milnor’s “\(\pi_i\Omega \cong \pi_{i+1}M\)” hides this change of base point; \(N\) need not be connected.

Corollary 22.2 as groups [V13.5]. (i) For a path \(\omega\) from \(y_0\) to \(y_1\) and \(i \ge 1\), \(\omega_\#\) is a group isomorphism \(\pi_i(Y, y_0) \to \pi_i(Y, y_1)\). (ii) If \(p, q \in N\), then \(\pi_{j+1}(\Omega, \gamma) \cong \pi_{j+2}(N, p)\) as groups, for every \(\gamma \in \Omega\) and \(j \ge 0\). (iii) Under the hypotheses of Theorem 22.1, \(\pi_i(\Omega^d, \gamma) \cong \pi_{i+1}(N, p)\) as groups for \(\gamma \in \Omega^d\), \(1 \le i \le \lambda_0 - 2\). Proof. (i) On the free path space \(C(I, Y)\), \((s, \omega) \mapsto \omega(s)\) is a homotopy from \(\mathrm{ev}_0\) to \(\mathrm{ev}_1\), so \((\mathrm{ev}_1)_* = \omega_\# \circ (\mathrm{ev}_0)_*\) at the base point \(\omega\). \(\mathrm{ev}_0\) is a homotopy equivalence Homotopy/ChangeOfBaseGroupevalZeroHomotopyEquiv, so \((\mathrm{ev}_0)_*\) is onto, and both are homomorphisms; hence \(\omega_\#(ab) = \omega_\#(a)\omega_\#(b)\) Homotopy/ChangeOfBaseGroupchangeBaseMap_mul. (ii), (iii) The other steps of [V13.4, §8.4] are induced by maps or are group isomorphisms. \(\square\)

9. Bott periodicity for the unitary group

This chapter proves the main theorems on the unitary group: \(\pi_i(U(n), I) \cong \pi_{i+2}(U(n'), I)\) for \(i < 2n\), \(i + 2 < 2n'\), and \(\pi_{2k+1}(U(m), I) \cong \mathbb Z\) as groups for \(2k + 2 \le 2m\) (Theorem 23.5). The route is Milnor’s §23: in \(SU(2m)\) the minimal geodesics from \(I\) to \(-I\) form the Grassmannian \(G_m(\mathbb C^{2m})\) and the others have index \(\ge 2m + 2\), so Corollary 22.2 [V13.4, §8.4] gives Theorem 23.3; three bundles then give periodicity. Matrix groups, bundles and stability are stated for \(\mathbb K = \mathbb R\) and \(\mathbb C\), for Chapter 10. Not needed: the abstract Lie-algebra model of §21, Corollaries 21.4–21.6, Theorem 21.7, Lemma 21.1, Milnor’s eigenvectors of \(K_A\), the case of \(U(n)\), the even groups \(\pi_{2k}U(m)\), and the Grassmannian as a space of subspaces.

Matrices are indexed by a finite set \(\iota\), \(n = |\iota|\); bijections of index sets (“reindexing”) induce homeomorphisms of all the spaces below. \(U_{\mathbb K}(n)\) is \(O(n)\) or \(U(n)\), \(\mathfrak u_{\mathbb K}(n)\) the skew-Hermitian matrices, and \(d = \dim_{\mathbb R}\mathbb K\). Between homotopy groups, \(\cong\) is a bijection, not claimed to respect base points, or an isomorphism where “as groups” is said.

9.1 Matrix groups

Theorem (matrix groups) [V12.14]. Give \(M_n(\mathbb K)\) the inner product \(\langle A, B\rangle = \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A^*B)\) Chapter12/MatrixInnerMatrixInner.innerProductSpace. (i) Multiplication on either side by a unitary matrix preserves it; Hermitian and skew-Hermitian matrices are orthogonal; \(\exp\) is smooth, with unitary values on \(\mathfrak u_{\mathbb K}(n)\). (ii) A matrix group is a slice submanifold \(G \subseteq M_n(\mathbb K)\) modelled on \(Z\) with a real Lie subalgebra \(\mathfrak g \subseteq \mathfrak u_{\mathbb K}(n)\) such that \(G\) consists of unitary matrices, is closed under products and \(g \mapsto g^*\), \(g\mathfrak gg^* \subseteq \mathfrak g\) for \(g \in G\), \(\exp\mathfrak g \subseteq G\), and \(\dim Z = \dim\mathfrak g\) Chapter12/MatrixGroupsIsMatrixGroup. Then \(T_gG = g\mathfrak g\) Chapter12/MatrixGroupsIsMatrixGroup.tangentSubspace_eq.

Proof. (i) Cycle traces; if \(A^* = A\), \(B^* = -B\), then \(\overline{\operatorname{tr}(AB)} = \operatorname{tr}(B^*A^*) = -\operatorname{tr}(AB)\); \((\exp X)^*\exp X = \exp(-X)\exp X\). (ii) \(t \mapsto g\exp(tX)\) lies in \(G\) with velocity \(gX\), so \(g\mathfrak g \subseteq T_gG\), of the same dimension. \(\square\)

Lemma 21.2 (for matrix groups) [V12.15]. For \(g \in G\) and \(X \in \mathfrak g\), \(t \mapsto g\exp(tX)\) is a geodesic [V7.1, §5.3] of \(G\) on \(\mathbb R\). A geodesic \(\gamma\) of \(G\) on a preconnected open \(s \ni t_0\) is \(\gamma(t) = \gamma(t_0)\exp((t - t_0)X)\) on \(s\), with \(X = \gamma(t_0)^*\gamma'(t_0) \in \mathfrak g\). So \(\exp_g(gX) = g\exp X\), and \(G\) is geodesically complete [V7.22, §5.8]. Chapter12/GroupGeodesicsIsMatrixGroup.isGeodesicOn_mul_exp_smul Chapter12/GroupGeodesicsIsMatrixGroup.eqOn_mul_exp_smul

Proof. The acceleration \(\gamma(t)X^2\) is normal to \(T_{\gamma(t)}G = \gamma(t)\mathfrak g\), since \(X^2\) is Hermitian and \(A \mapsto \gamma(t)A\) is an isometry. Conversely, \(X \in \mathfrak g\) as \(\gamma'(t_0) \in \gamma(t_0)\mathfrak g\), and \(\gamma(t_0)\exp((t - t_0)X)\) is a geodesic with the value and velocity of \(\gamma\) at \(t_0\) [V7.5, §5.3]. \(\square\)

Theorem 21.3 (for matrix groups) [V12.17]. Let \(P_{\mathfrak g}\) be the orthogonal projection onto \(\mathfrak g\), \(g \in G\) and \(X, Y, Z \in \mathfrak g\). (a) The orthogonal projection onto \(T_gG\) is \(M \mapsto gP_{\mathfrak g}(g^*M)\). (b) \(\mathrm{II}_g(gX, gY) = \tfrac12g(XY + YX)\). (c) \(R(gX, gY)gZ = \tfrac14g[[X, Y], Z]\), with Milnor’s sign. Chapter12/GroupGeodesicsIsMatrixGroup.secondFundForm_mul Chapter12/GroupGeodesicsIsMatrixGroup.curvOp_mul

Proof. (a) \(gP_{\mathfrak g}(g^*M) \in g\mathfrak g\), and \(M - gP_{\mathfrak g}(g^*M) = g(g^*M - P_{\mathfrak g}(g^*M)) \perp g\mathfrak g\). (b) \(\gamma'' = \mathrm{II}(\gamma', \gamma')\) along \(g\exp(tX)\) [V7.3, §5.3] gives \(\mathrm{II}_g(gX, gX) = gX^2\); polarize. (c) Both sides are tangent; pair with \(gW\), \(W \in \mathfrak g\). The Gauss equation [V6.18, §5.1] and (b) give \(\tfrac14(\langle XZ + ZX, YW + WY\rangle - \langle XW + WX, YZ + ZY\rangle)\), which is \(\tfrac14\langle[[X, Y], Z], W\rangle\) by expanding and cycling traces Chapter12/GroupGeodesicsinner_gauss_identity. \(\square\)

Theorem 20.5 (along one-parameter subgroups) [V12.18]. Let \(A \in \mathfrak g\), \(\gamma(t) = \exp(tA)\), \(h(t) = \exp(tA/2)\) and \(K_A(U) = \tfrac14[[A, U], A]\). If \(U : \mathbb R \to \mathfrak g\) is smooth with \(U'' + K_A(U) = 0\), then \(hUh\) is a Jacobi field along \(\gamma\) [V9.2, §6.4], with covariant derivative \(U'(0)\) at \(0\). Chapter12/GroupJacobiIsMatrixGroup.isJacobiField_conj Chapter12/GroupJacobiIsMatrixGroup.covAlong_conj_zero

Proof. \(h\) is unitary, commutes with \(A\), and \(h^2 = \gamma\). So \((hUh)' = h(U' + \tfrac12(AU + UA))h\), whose tangential part [V8.7, §6.2] is, by (a), \(\gamma P_{\mathfrak g}(h^*U'h + \tfrac12h^*(AU + UA)h) = hU'h\), the second term being Hermitian. By (c), \(R(\gamma', hMh)\gamma' = \gamma K_A(h^*Mh) = hK_A(M)h\). So the Jacobi expression of \(hUh\) is \(h(U'' + K_AU)h = 0\). \(\square\)

Theorem (\(U(n)\), \(O(n)\) and \(SU(n)\)) [V14.13]. (i) \(U_{\mathbb K}(n) = \{A : A^*A = I\}\) is a compact slice submanifold of \(M_n(\mathbb K)\) modelled on \(\mathfrak u_{\mathbb K}(n)\), and a matrix group with it. (ii) \(d(\det)_A(AX) = \det A\operatorname{tr}X\), and \(\det\exp(tX) = 1\) if \(\operatorname{tr}X = 0\). (iii) For \(n \ge 1\), \(SU(n) = \{A \in U(n) : \det A = 1\}\) is a compact slice submanifold modelled on \(\mathfrak{su}(n)\), the traceless part of \(\mathfrak u(n)\), and a matrix group with it. Chapter12/MatrixGroupsisMatrixGroup_unitaryGroup Chapter12/MatrixGroupsisMatrixGroup_specialUnitaryGroup

Proof. (i) \(U_{\mathbb K}(n) = \Phi^{-1}(0)\), \(\Phi(A)\) the Hermitian part of \(A^*A - I\); at a unitary \(A\), \(d\Phi_A(\tfrac12AS) = S\) Chapter12/MatrixGroupsisRegularValue_unitaryMap, so the preimage theorem of the companion volume applies Milnor/Chapter2/LevelSetisSliceSubmanifold_preimage; \(\|A\|^2 = n\) on it. (ii) \(\det(I + sX) = 1 + s\operatorname{tr}X + O(s^2)\). (iii) \(SU(n)\) is not a regular level set of \((\Phi, \det - 1)\). As \(|\det| = 1\) on \(U(n)\), it is the open piece \(\operatorname{Re}\det > 0\) of \(\Psi^{-1}(0)\), \(\Psi = (\Phi, \operatorname{Im}\det)\); at \(\det A = \delta = \pm1\), (ii) shows \(d\Psi_A(A(\tfrac12S + \tfrac{c\delta}{n}iI)) = (S, c)\). \(\square\)

9.2 The index of a spectrum

Definition (the index of a spectrum) [V14.7, V14.8] [V12.13]. For \(e \in \mathbb R\) let \(\operatorname{cp}(e) = \{t \in (0, 1) : e > 0,\ t \in \pi\mathbb Z/\sqrt e\}\). For a finite family \(e = (e_q)\) let \(\mu_e(t) = \#\{q : t \in \operatorname{cp}(e_q)\}\) and \(\operatorname{ind}(e) = \sum_t\mu_e(t)\): Theorems 20.5 and 15.1 as a definition, justified for \(SU(n)\) in §9.3. Chapter14/IndexCountconjParams Chapter14/IndexCountspectralIndex Then \(\operatorname{cp}(e)\) is finite; for an integer \(d \ge 1\), \(\operatorname{cp}((\pi d)^2)\) consists of the \(d - 1\) numbers \(s/d\), \(0 < s < d\); \(\operatorname{ind}(e) = \sum_q\#\operatorname{cp}(e_q)\) (exchange two finite sums); and repeating every \(e_q\) twice doubles the index.

Lemma (odd squares) [V14.3]. For odd integers \(k_1, \dots, k_n\), \(\sum k_j^2 \ge n\), with equality iff every \(k_j = \pm1\). Chapter14/IndexCountsum_sq_eq_card_iff

Theorem (the index formula) [V14.9]. For \(k \in \mathbb Z^\iota\) let \(\lambda(k) = \sum_{k_i > k_j}(k_i - k_j - 2)\), over ordered pairs, and let \(\operatorname{sp}(k)\) be the family of the numbers \(\tfrac{\pi^2}4(k_i - k_j)^2\), \(k_i > k_j\), each counted twice. If all \(k_j\) are odd, \(\operatorname{ind}(\operatorname{sp}(k)) = \lambda(k)\). Chapter14/IndexCountspectralIndex_suSpectrum

Proof. For odd \(b < a\), \(\tfrac{\pi^2}4(a - b)^2 = (\pi d)^2\) with \(d = (a - b)/2 \ge 1\) an integer, and \(2(d - 1) = a - b - 2\). \(\square\)

Lemma (minimal \(k\)) [V14.10]. If every \(k_j = \pm1\), then \(\lambda(k) = 0\): each pair with \(k_i > k_j\) has \(k_i - k_j = 2\). Chapter14/IndexCountbottIndex_eq_zero_of_minimal

Lemma 23.2 (combinatorial form) [V14.11]. If \(k_1, \dots, k_{2m}\) are odd, \(\sum k_j = 0\) and not all \(k_j = \pm1\), then \(\lambda(k) \ge 2m + 2\). Chapter14/IndexCountbottIndex_ge

Proof. Let \(P, N\) count the positive and negative \(k_j\), and let \(S_+\), \(S_-\) be the sums of \(|k_j|\) over them: \(P + N = 2m\), \(S_+ = S_-\), \(S_+ \ge P\), \(S_- \ge N\). Distinct odd integers differ by at least \(2\), so the terms of \(\lambda\) are \(\ge 0\), and the pairs (positive, negative) give \(\lambda(k) \ge NS_+ + PS_- - 2PN\). Some \(|k_i| \ge 3\), so \(S_+ \ge P + 2\) or \(S_- \ge N + 2\). If \(P < N\): \(N - P \ge 2\), \(N \ge m + 1\), \(S_\pm \ge N\), and the bound is \(\ge N(N - P) \ge 2m + 2\); \(P > N\) is symmetric. If \(P = N = m\): \(S_\pm \ge m + 2\), and the bound is \(\ge 4m \ge 2m + 2\). \(\square\)

9.3 Geodesics from \(I\) to \(-I\) in \(SU(n)\)

Write \(D_a = \operatorname{diag}(ia_j)_j\) for \(a \in \mathbb R^\iota\), and \(D_k = D_{\pi k}\) for \(k \in \mathbb Z^\iota\).

Lemma (\(\exp D_a = -I\)) [V14.1]. \(e^{ia} = -1\) iff \(a = \pi k\) with \(k\) odd; so \(\exp D_a = -I\) iff every \(a_j\) is an odd multiple of \(\pi\). Chapter14/SUMatricesexp_diagonal_eq_neg_one_iff

Theorem 20.5 for \(SU(n)\) [V14.18]. Let \(T\) be unitary, \(A = TD_aT^* \in \mathfrak{su}(n)\), \(\gamma(t) = \exp(tA)\), \(s_b(t) = \sin(bt)/b\) (\(s_0(t) = t\)), and \(S(t) \odot W = (s_{(a_j - a_l)/2}(t)w_{jl})_{jl}\). (i) For \(C \in \mathfrak{su}(n)\), \(J_C = h\,T(S \odot T^*CT)T^*\,h\), \(h(t) = \exp(tA/2)\), is a Jacobi field along \(\gamma\) in \(SU(n)\) with \(J_C(0) = 0\) and \(\frac{DJ_C}{dt}(0) = C\); \(J_C(t) = 0\) iff \(S(t) \odot T^*CT = 0\). (ii) The multiplicity [V9.4, §6.4] of \(t_0 \in [0, 1]\) as a conjugate parameter is \(\dim\{W \in \mathfrak{su}(n) : S(t_0) \odot W = 0\}\). (iii) For \(a = \pi k\), \(k \in \mathbb Z^\iota\), and \(0 < t < 1\), this dimension is \(\mu_{\operatorname{sp}(k)}(t)\). Proof. (i) \(K_{D_a}\) multiplies the entry \((j, l)\) by \(((a_j - a_l)/2)^2\), and \(K_{TDT^*}(TMT^*) = TK_D(M)T^*\). As \(s_b'' = -b^2s_b\), \(s_b(0) = 0\), \(s_b'(0) = 1\), \(U = T(S \odot T^*CT)T^*\) solves \(U'' + K_A(U) = 0\), \(U(0) = 0\), \(U'(0) = C\), in \(\mathfrak{su}(n)\) (\(S(t)\) is real symmetric with diagonal \(t\)); apply [V12.18, §9.1]. (ii) \(J \mapsto \frac{DJ}{dt}(0)\) is injective on Jacobi fields vanishing at \(0\) and \(t_0\) [V9.3, §6.4], such a \(J\) is \(J_C\), \(C \in T_ISU(n) = \mathfrak{su}(n)\), and by (i) the image is \(\{C : S(t_0) \odot T^*CT = 0\}\). (iii) For \(k_l < k_j\), \(s_{\pi(k_j - k_l)/2}(t) = 0\) iff \(t \in \operatorname{cp}(\tfrac{\pi^2}4(k_j - k_l)^2)\); \(s_0(t) = t \ne 0\). So the real and imaginary parts of the \(w_{jl}\), \(k_j > k_l\), \(t\) such a parameter, are coordinates (inverse \(F \mapsto F - F^*\)), \(\mu_{\operatorname{sp}(k)}(t)\) in number. \(\square\)

Theorem (geodesics from \(I\) to \(-I\)) [V14.14]. (i) Every geodesic in \(\Omega(SU(n); I, q)\) [V8.10, §6.2] agrees on \([0, 1]\) with \(t \mapsto \exp(tA)\) for some \(A \in \mathfrak{su}(n)\). Proof. (i) [V12.15, §9.1] on \((0, 1)\), extended to \([0, 1]\) by continuity, with \(\gamma(0) = I\). (ii) The spectral theorem for \(iA\) Mathlib/Analysis/Matrix/SpectrumMatrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem, \(\exp(TDT^*) = T\exp(D)T^*\), [V14.1, §9.3] and [V14.2, §9.3]. \(\square\)

Theorem (distance and minimal geodesics) [V14.15]. For skew-Hermitian \(A\), \(t \mapsto \exp(tA)\) has length \(\|A\|\) on \([0, 1]\); and \(\|TD_kT^*\| = \pi(\sum k_j^2)^{1/2}\), which is \(\ge \pi\sqrt n\) for odd \(k\). Let \(|\iota| = 2m \ge 2\) and \(k^0 = (1, \dots, 1, -1, \dots, -1)\). In \(SU(2m)\) the distance [V7.18, §5.7] is \(\rho(I, -I) = \pi\sqrt{2m}\), and for \(A \in \mathfrak{su}(2m)\) with \(\exp A = -I\), \(t \mapsto \exp(tA)\) is a minimal geodesic [V7.24, §5.8] iff \(A^2 = -\pi^2I\), iff all \(k_j = \pm1\). Proof. The speed \(\|\exp(tA)A\| = \|A\|\) is constant; conjugation by \(T\) is an isometry; [V14.2, §9.3], [V14.3, §9.2]. “\(\le\)”: the geodesic of \(D_{k^0}\). “\(\ge\)”: \(SU(2m)\) is complete, so by Hopf–Rinow [V7.26, §5.8] some \(v \in \mathfrak{su}(2m)\) has \(\exp_Iv = \exp v = -I\) ([V12.15, §9.1]) and \(\|v\| = \rho(I, -I)\). Finally \((TD_kT^*)^2 = T\operatorname{diag}(-\pi^2k_j^2)T^*\); a minimal geodesic has \(\|A\| \le \pi\sqrt{2m}\), so all \(k_j = \pm1\) by [V14.3, §9.2]; conversely its length is then \(\rho(I, -I)\). \(\square\)

Lemma 23.1 [V14.16]. Let \(|\iota| = 2m\), \(\operatorname{minVel} = \{A \in \mathfrak{su}(2m) : A^2 = -\pi^2I\}\), and \(G_m(\mathbb C^{2m})\) the set of Hermitian projections (\(P^* = P = P^2\)) of trace \(m\). (i) \(\exp A = -I\) for \(A \in \operatorname{minVel}\). (ii) \(A \mapsto \tfrac12(I - \tfrac i\pi A)\) is a homeomorphism \(\operatorname{minVel} \to G_m(\mathbb C^{2m})\) with inverse \(P \mapsto i\pi(2P - I)\). Chapter12/SUMinimallemma_23_1

Proof. (i) The eigenvalues \(\lambda\) of \(iA\) have \(\lambda^2 = \pi^2\); [V14.1, §9.3]. (ii) \(P = \tfrac12(I - \tfrac i\pi A)\) is Hermitian, \(P^2 = \tfrac14(I - \tfrac{2i}\pi A - \pi^{-2}A^2) = P\), \(\operatorname{tr}P = m\); conversely \((i\pi(2P - I))^2 = -\pi^2(4P^2 - 4P + I) = -\pi^2I\), with trace \(i\pi(2m - 2m) = 0\). Both maps are affine. \(\square\)

Theorem (the index formula in \(SU(n)\)) [V14.19]. Let \(k \in \mathbb Z^\iota\) with \(\sum k_j = 0\), \(T\) unitary, \(A = TD_kT^*\), and \(\gamma(t) = \exp(tA)\) in \(\Omega(SU(n); I, -I)\). The index of \(E_{**}\) at \(\gamma\) [V8.14, §6.3] is \(\operatorname{ind}(\operatorname{sp}(k))\); so for \(A \in \mathfrak{su}(n)\) with \(\exp A = -I\) it is \(\lambda(k)\), \(k\) as in [V14.14, §9.3]. Proof. The index theorem [V9.24, §6.5] sums the multiplicities over \(0 < t < 1\); by [V14.18, §9.3] they are the \(\mu_{\operatorname{sp}(k)}(t)\), which vanish off \((0, 1)\). Then [V14.9, §9.2]. \(\square\)

Lemma 23.2 [V14.20]. Let \(|\iota| = 2m\). A geodesic \(t \mapsto \exp(tA)\) from \(I\) to \(-I\) in \(SU(2m)\), \(k\) as in [V14.19, §9.3], has index \(0\) if all \(k_j = \pm1\) and index \(\ge 2m + 2\) otherwise. For skew-Hermitian \(A\), \(E(\exp(\cdot A)) = \|A\|^2\). Every geodesic in \(\Omega(SU(2m); I, -I)\) that is not of least energy has index \(\ge 2m + 2\). Chapter12/SUIndexlemma_23_2_index Chapter13/SUInstancele_formIndex_of_not_minimal_su

Proof. [V14.19, §9.3] with [V14.10, §9.2] and [V14.11, §9.2]; constant speed [V8.5, §6.1]. For the last claim the geodesic is \(\exp(tA)\) on \([0, 1]\) ([V14.14, §9.3]), and the index depends only on \([0, 1]\) [V10.23, §7.7]. If all \(k_j = \pm1\), it is minimal ([V14.15, §9.3]), and \(E(\gamma) = L(\gamma)^2 \le L(\omega)^2 \le E(\omega)\) for every \(\omega\) [V8.5, §6.1]: it has least energy. \(\square\)

9.4 Homotopy groups and bundles

Fact (maps) (standard). A map induces \(f_* : \pi_i(X, x) \to \pi_i(Y, f(x))\), a homomorphism for \(i \ge 1\); a homotopy equivalence, in particular a homeomorphism, induces bijections at every base point. Contractible spaces have trivial \(\pi_i\), discrete spaces trivial \(\pi_i\) for \(i \ge 1\). Homotopy/ExactSequenceIsohomotopyGroupHom Homotopy/ChangeOfBasebijective_homotopyGroupMap_of_homotopyEquiv Idea: a free homotopy acts on \(\pi_i\) by change of basepoint.

Fact (fibrations) (standard). \(p : E \to B\) is locally trivial with fibre \(F\) if every \(b \in B\) has an open \(U \ni b\) and a homeomorphism \(p^{-1}(U) \cong U \times F\) over \(U\); every fibre is then homeomorphic to \(F\). A locally trivial map is a Serre fibration: a map \(I^n \times I \to B\) lifts to \(E\), extending any lift given on \(I^n \times 0 \cup \partial I^n \times I\). Homotopy/FibrationIsLocallyTrivial Homotopy/HomotopyLiftingIsLocallyTrivial.isSerreFibration Idea: lift box by box over trivializing sets, along a lower set of indices, so that each new box retracts onto its lifted faces.

Fact (the exact sequence) (standard). For a continuous Serre fibration \(p\), \(e_0 \in E\) and \(F = p^{-1}(p(e_0))\), the sequence \(\cdots \to \pi_{i+1}B \xrightarrow{\partial} \pi_iF \to \pi_iE \to \pi_iB \to \cdots \to \pi_0B\) is exact as pointed sets, \(\partial\) being a homomorphism for \(i \ge 1\) Homotopy/ExactSequenceexact_fiber. In every degree: (a) if \(\pi_iE = 0\) for \(i \le k\), \(\partial : \pi_{j+1}B \to \pi_jF\) is bijective for \(j + 1 \le k\); (b) if \(\pi_iB = 0\) for \(i \le k\), \(\pi_iF \to \pi_iE\) is bijective for \(i + 1 \le k\); (c) \(\pi_nF \to \pi_nE\) is bijective if \(\pi_nB = \pi_{n+1}B = 0\), and \(\partial\) on \(\pi_{n+1}B\) if \(\pi_nE = \pi_{n+1}E = 0\); (d) \(\pi_iE = 0\) if \(\pi_iF = 0\) and \(\pi_{i'}B = 0\) for \(i' \le i\); \(\pi_{j+1}B = 0\) if \(\pi_{j+1}E = \pi_jF = 0\). Homotopy/ExactSequenceIsoboundaryEquivPi Homotopy/ExactSequenceIsobijective_homotopyGroupMap_fiberIncl_of_le Idea: \(\partial\) takes the top face of a lift relative to the open box; injectivity, even in low degrees, comes from further lifting problems.

Fact (spheres) (standard). The unit sphere \(S^n\) of a real inner product space of dimension \(n + 1\) has \(\pi_i = 0\) for \(i < n\). Homotopy/Spheressubsingleton_pi_sphere_of_finrank Idea: \(S^n\) is a contractible hemisphere with an \(n\)-cell attached along its boundary sphere [V2.7, §2.4], and maps of cubes of dimension \(< n\) can be pushed off the cell.

Theorem (orbit sections; the Stiefel bundles) [V14.23]. (i) Let a topological group \(G\) act continuously on \(E\) and transitively on \(B\), let \(p : E \to B\) be continuous and equivariant, and let \(g \mapsto gb_0\) have a continuous section on an open \(U_0 \ni b_0\). Then \(p\) is locally trivial with fibre \(p^{-1}(b_0)\). Homotopy/Homogeneousexists_triv_of_orbitSection (ii) Let \(V_\kappa(\mathbb K^\iota) = \{F \in M_{\iota\times\kappa}(\mathbb K) : F^*F = I\}\), \(\iota = \iota_1 \sqcup \kappa\), \(F = \binom WC\) and \(F_0 = \binom 0I\). Where \(I + C\) is invertible,

\[s(F) = \begin{pmatrix} I - W(I + C^*)^{-1}W^* & W\\ -(I + C)(I + C^*)^{-1}W^* & C\end{pmatrix}\]

is unitary with \(s(F)F_0 = F\) Homotopy/StiefelsecMat_mem_unitaryGroup, and \(U_{\mathbb K}(\iota)\) acts transitively on \(V_\kappa(\mathbb K^\iota)\). (iii) Restriction to the last vectors, \(V_{\kappa_1\sqcup\kappa_2}(\mathbb K^{\iota_1\sqcup\kappa_2}) \to V_{\kappa_2}(\mathbb K^{\iota_1\sqcup\kappa_2})\), is locally trivial with fibre \(V_{\kappa_1}(\mathbb K^{\iota_1})\), and \(g \mapsto gF_0\), \(U_{\mathbb K}(\iota_1 \sqcup \kappa) \to V_\kappa(\mathbb K^{\iota_1\sqcup\kappa})\), with fibre \(U_{\mathbb K}(\iota_1)\), included as \(S \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(S, I)\). \(V_1(\mathbb K^\iota)\) is the unit sphere. Homotopy/StiefelstiefelRestrict_locallyTrivial Homotopy/StiefelunitaryOrbit_locallyTrivial

Proof. (i) \(x \mapsto (p(x), s(p(x))^{-1}x)\) trivializes over \(U_0\); translate by \(G\). (ii) Multiply out in blocks, using \(W^*W + C^*C = I\); for transitivity extend the columns of \(F\) to an orthonormal basis. (iii) Apply (i) with \(s\); a frame with last columns \(F_0\) is \(\operatorname{diag}(A, I)\) with \(A^*A = I\). \(\square\)

Theorem (the Grassmannian bundle) [V14.24]. Let \(G_k(\mathbb K^\iota)\) be the set of Hermitian projections of trace \(k\) (for \(\mathbb C\) and \(|\iota| = 2k\), the space of Lemma 23.1). (i) Hermitian projections with \(PQ = Q\) and \(\operatorname{tr}P = \operatorname{tr}Q\) are equal. (ii) Every \(P \in G_m(\mathbb K^\iota)\) is \(FF^*\) for some \(F \in V_m(\mathbb K^\iota)\). (iii) \(F \mapsto FF^*\), \(V_m(\mathbb K^{\iota_1 \sqcup m}) \to G_m(\mathbb K^{\iota_1\sqcup m})\), is locally trivial with fibre \(U_{\mathbb K}(m)\). Proof. (i) \(R = P - Q\) has \(R^*R = R\), so \(\operatorname{tr}R^*R = 0\). (ii) Take an orthonormal basis of the range as \(F\), and apply (i). (iii) [V14.23, §9.4] (i) for \(g\cdot P = gPg^*\), transitive by (ii). Near \(P_0 = F_0F_0^*\), Gram–Schmidt applied to the columns of \(PF_0\) gives a continuous frame \(\sigma(P)\) Homotopy/GrassmanniancontinuousAt_gsFrame, with \(\sigma\sigma^* = P\) by (i); \(s(\sigma(P))\) is the section. 9.5 Theorem 23.3

Theorem (Lemma 23.1 in the path space) [V14.17]. Let \(|\iota| = 2m\), \(\Omega = \Omega(SU(2m); I, -I)\) with Milnor’s metric [V10.1, §7.1], and \(\Omega^d\) its paths of least energy [V13.1, §8.3]. (i) \(E(\omega) \ge 2m\pi^2\) on \(\Omega\). (ii) For \(A \in \operatorname{minVel}\), \(\exp(A/2) = A/\pi\), and \(\epsilon_A : t \mapsto \exp(tA)\) lies in \(\Omega^d\). (iii) Every \(\gamma \in \Omega^d\) agrees on \([0, 1]\) with \(\epsilon_A\), \(A = \pi\gamma(\tfrac12) \in \operatorname{minVel}\). (iv) \(A \mapsto \epsilon_A\) is continuous, and a homotopy equivalence \(\operatorname{minVel} \simeq \Omega^d\) with homotopy inverse \(\gamma \mapsto \pi\gamma(\tfrac12)\) (a homeomorphism only up to paths at distance \(0\)). Chapter14/MinimalPathsexists_minVel_of_mem_minPaths Chapter14/MinimalPathsminPathsHomotopyEquiv

Proof. (i) \(E \ge L^2 \ge \rho(I, -I)^2\) [V8.5, §6.1], [V7.18, §5.7], [V14.15, §9.3]. (ii) In diagonal form \(e^{\pm i\pi/2} = \pm i\); \(E(\epsilon_A) = \|A\|^2 = 2m\pi^2\). (iii) \(\gamma\) is a geodesic [V13.1, §8.3], so \(\gamma = \epsilon_A\) on \([0, 1]\) with \(\exp A = -I\) ([V14.14, §9.3]), and \(\|A\|^2 = E(\gamma) \le 2m\pi^2\): \(\gamma\) is minimal, \(A^2 = -\pi^2I\) ([V14.15, §9.3]); then (ii). (iv) All speeds are \(\pi\sqrt{2m}\), so the \(L^2\) part of Milnor’s distance between \(\epsilon_A\), \(\epsilon_B\) vanishes, and the uniform part tends to \(0\) as \(B \to A\) by pointwise convergence at bounded energy [V7.30, §5.7]; \(\gamma \mapsto \gamma(\tfrac12)\) is continuous [V10.15, §7.6]. One composite is the identity; the other is at distance \(0\) from the identity, hence homotopic to it (switch at time \(1\)). \(\square\)

Theorem (the neighbourhood retraction; Corollary 22.2 for \(SU(2m)\)) [V14.21]. Let \(|\iota| = 2m\), \(Q(H)\) the spectral projection of a Hermitian \(H\) onto its eigenvalues \(> \tfrac12\), continuous in \(H\) where \(\tfrac12\) is not an eigenvalue, and \(H(\omega)\) the Hermitian part of \(\tfrac12(I - i\omega(\tfrac12))\). The set \(O\) of the \(\omega \in \Omega\) with \(\tfrac12 \notin \operatorname{spec}H(\omega)\) and \(|\operatorname{tr}Q(H(\omega)) - m| < \tfrac12\) is open and contains \(\Omega^d\), and the map equal to \(\omega \mapsto \epsilon_{i\pi(2Q(H(\omega)) - I)}\) on \(O \setminus \Omega^d\) and to the identity on \(\Omega^d\) is continuous on \(O\), with values in \(\Omega^d\) Chapter14/MinimalRetractexists_retraction_minPaths_su. Hence, for \(\gamma \in \Omega^d\), \(\pi_i(\Omega^d, \gamma) \cong \pi_{i+1}(SU(2m), I)\) for \(i \le 2m\), as groups for \(1 \le i \le 2m\). Proof. \(Q(H)\) is a Hermitian projection, equal to \(H\) if \(H\) is one, of natural-number trace. \(\det(\tfrac12 - H) \ne 0\) is open, so \(O\) is open, and \(Q(H(\omega)) \in G_m\) on \(O\); [V14.16, §9.3] and [V14.17, §9.5] give continuity and values in \(\Omega^d\). For \(\omega \in \Omega^d\), \(\omega(\tfrac12) = A/\pi\), so \(H(\omega) = \tfrac12(I - \tfrac i\pi A) \in G_m\): \(\omega \in O\), and the formula gives a path at distance \(0\) from \(\omega\), which keeps continuity. \(SU(2m)\) is compact and contains \(-I\), so Corollary 22.2 [V13.4, §8.4], [V13.5, §8.4], with this retraction in place of Hanner’s theorem, applies with \(\lambda_0 = 2m + 2\) ([V14.20, §9.3]). \(\square\)

Theorem 23.3 [V14.22]. Let \(|\iota| = 2m\), \(P \in G_m(\mathbb C^{2m})\) and \(i \le 2m\). Then \(\pi_i(G_m(\mathbb C^{2m}), P) \cong \pi_{i+1}(SU(2m), I)\), as groups for \(1 \le i \le 2m\). Chapter14/Periodicitytheorem_23_3 Chapter14/PeriodicityGroupstheorem_23_3_mulEquiv

10. Bott periodicity for the orthogonal group

This chapter proves Theorem 24.7 in the stable range: \(\pi_i(O(n), I) \cong \pi_{i+8}(O(n'), I)\), as sets, for \(n \ge i + 2\) and \(n' \ge i + 10\). Matrices are real, \(n \times n\); \(M_n(\mathbb R)\) has \(\langle A, B\rangle = \operatorname{tr}(AB^{\mathsf T})\) [V12.14, §9.1]; \(J_1, J_2, \dots\) is a fixed sequence of matrices. The route is Theorem 22.1 [V13.3, §8.3], [V13.16, §8.3], eight times at \(n = 16r\), with index bounds from Killing fields and the index theorem [V9.24, §6.5]. Not needed: Lemma 24.2 as a formula, the curvature of \(\Omega_k(n)\), the limit spaces, the odd steps of Lemma 24.6, vector fields on spheres, and the path components for \(k = 2, 6\).

10.1 Complex structures and the spaces \(\Omega_k(n)\)

Lemma (complex structures) [V15.1]. A complex structure is a \(J \in O(n)\) with \(J^2 = -I\) Chapter15/ComplexStructureIsComplexStructure; equivalently \(J^{\mathsf T} = -J\) and \(J^2 = -I\) Chapter15/ComplexStructureisComplexStructure_iff. If one exists, \(n\) is even Chapter15/ComplexStructureIsComplexStructure.even_card.

Proof. \(J^{\mathsf T} = J^{-1} = -J\); conversely \(JJ^{\mathsf T} = -J^2 = I\). And \(1 = (\det J)^2 = \det(-I) = (-1)^n\). \(\square\)

Lemma (parametrized slices) [V15.21]. Let \(S\) be a subset of a real normed space \(E\), \(Z, W\) finite-dimensional, and suppose near each \(x \in S\) a smooth \(\Phi : Z \times W \to E\) with \(\Phi(0) = x\) and invertible derivative at \(0\) satisfies, near \(0\): \(\Phi(z, 0) \in S\), and \(\Phi(q) \in S\) implies \(\Phi(q) = \Phi(g(q), 0)\) with \(g(q) \to 0\). Then \(S\) is a slice submanifold modelled on \(Z\) Chapter15/TotallyGeodesicisSliceSubmanifold_of_param. Proof: a local inverse of \(\Phi\) is a slice chart. \(\square\)

Definition. A slice submanifold \(N \subseteq M_n(\mathbb R)\) modelled on \(Z\) is totally geodesic for \(x \mapsto T_x\) if for \(x \in N\): \(x^{\mathsf T}x = I\), \(T_x\) is a space of skew matrices of dimension \(\dim Z\), and \(x\exp A \in N\), \(A \in T_{x\exp A}\) for \(A \in T_x\) Chapter15/TotallyGeodesicIsTotGeo.

Theorem [V15.21]. For such \(N\): (i) \(T_xN = xT_x\) Chapter15/TotallyGeodesicIsTotGeo.tangentSubspace_eq; (ii) for \(A \in T_x\), \(t \mapsto x\exp(tA)\) is a geodesic of \(N\) on \(\mathbb R\) Chapter15/TotallyGeodesicIsTotGeo.isGeodesicOn_mul_exp_smul; (iii) every unbroken geodesic in \(\Omega(N; p, q)\) agrees on \([0, 1]\) with \(s \mapsto p\exp(sV)\) for some \(V \in T_p\) Chapter15/TotallyGeodesicIsTotGeo.eqOn_of_isUnbrokenGeodesic; (iv) \(\exp_x(xA) = x\exp A\) for \(A \in T_x\), and \(N\) is geodesically complete Chapter15/TotallyGeodesicIsTotGeo.exp_eq Chapter15/TotallyGeodesicIsTotGeo.isGeodesicallyComplete.

Proof. (i) The curves \(x\exp(tA)\) lie in \(N\) with velocity \(xA\); the dimensions agree. (ii) The acceleration \(\gamma A^2\) of \(\gamma(t) = x\exp(tA)\) satisfies \(\langle\gamma A^2, \gamma B\rangle = \operatorname{tr}(A^2B^{\mathsf T}) = 0\) for skew \(B\), so it is normal to \(T_{\gamma(t)}N = \gamma(t)T_{\gamma(t)}\). (iii), (iv) Uniqueness of geodesics. \(\square\)

Assertions 1 and 2 [V15.22]. Let \(\mathcal T_x\) be the space of skew \(A\) commuting with \(J_\alpha\) (\(1 \le \alpha < k\)) and, if \(k \ne 0\), anticommuting with \(x\) Chapter15/OmegaManifoldmem_tanAlg; for \(k = 0\) it is \(\mathfrak o(n)\) for every \(x\) Chapter15/OmegaManifoldtanAlg_zero. (iii) Hence there is \(L\) with \(L(y) \to 0\) as \(y \to x\), and \(L(y) \in \mathcal T_x\), \(y = x\exp L(y)\) for \(y \in \Omega_k(n)\) near \(x\) Chapter15/OmegaManifoldexists_local_log.

Proof. (i) V15.6. (ii) \(\exp\) has derivative the identity at \(0\). Injectivity, three times: \(\exp(C^{\mathsf T}) = (\exp C)^{-1} = \exp(-C)\); \((x\exp C)^2 = -I\) gives \(\exp(x^{\mathsf T}Cx) = \exp(-C)\); \(J_\alpha\) anticommutes with \(x\) and \(x\exp C\), so \(\exp(J_\alpha CJ_\alpha^{\mathsf T}) = \exp C\). (The norm is invariant under transposition and orthogonal conjugation.) (iii) \(L(y) = \log(x^{\mathsf T}y)\). \(\square\)

10.4 The minimal geodesics: Lemmas 24.1 and 24.4

Lemma 24.1 [V15.24]. Let \(V\) be skew with \(\exp V = -I\). If \(E \ne 0\) and \(V^2E = -\lambda E\), then \(\lambda \ge \pi^2\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalpi_sq_le_of_sq_mul. Hence \(\|V\|^2 \ge \pi^2n\), and \(\|V\|^2 \le \pi^2n\) implies \(V^2 = -\pi^2I\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalpi_sq_mul_card_le_norm_sq Chapter15/OmegaMinimalmul_self_eq_of_norm_sq_le.

Proof. \(\|VE\|^2 = \lambda\|E\|^2\); \(\lambda = 0\) would give \(E = \exp(V)E = -E\). For \(\mu = \sqrt\lambda > 0\), \(\exp(tV)E = \cos(\mu t)E + \mu^{-1}\sin(\mu t)VE\) (both solve \(c' = Vc\)); at \(t = 1\), pairing with \(E\) (\(\langle E, VE\rangle = 0\)) gives \(\cos\mu = -1\). Diagonalize \(V^{\mathsf T}V\) (spectral theorem): \(\|V\|^2 = \sum\lambda_i\) with all \(\lambda_i \ge \pi^2\). \(\square\)

Theorem (minimal geodesics) [V15.25]. Let \(J_1, \dots, J_k\) be an anticommuting family, \(p \in \Omega_k(n)\), \(N\) the stratum through \(p\), and \(\mathcal C_p = \{A \in \mathcal T_p : A^2 = -I\} \ne \emptyset\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalminVelO. Put \(\gamma_A(t) = p\exp(\pi tA)\). Then (i) \(-p \in N\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalneg_mem_omegaStratum; (ii) \(\rho_N(p, -p) = \pi\sqrt n\), and paths in \(\Omega(N; p, -p)\) have energy \(\ge \pi^2n\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalriemDist_omegaStratum Chapter15/OmegaMinimalpi_sq_card_le_energy; (iii) each \(\gamma_A\), \(A \in \mathcal C_p\), has least energy Chapter15/OmegaMinimalomegaPath_mem_minPaths, and \(\gamma_A(\frac12) = pA\) if \(A^2 = -I\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalomegaGeo_half; (iv) every path of least energy agrees on \([0, 1]\) with some \(\gamma_A\), \(A \in \mathcal C_p\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalexists_minVelO_of_mem_minPaths.

Proof. \(-p = p\exp(\pi A)\); \(\gamma_A\) has energy \(\|\pi A\|^2 = \pi^2n\). \(N\) is closed, hence complete, and Hopf–Rinow [V7.26, §5.8] Chapter7/HopfRinowtheorem_10_9 gives \(V \in \mathcal T_p\) with \(\exp_p(pV) = p\exp V = -p\) and \(\rho = \|V\| \ge \pi\sqrt n\) (V15.24). (iv) A path of least energy is an unbroken geodesic [V13.1, §8.3], so \(p\exp(tV)\) on \([0, 1]\) (V15.21), \(\exp V = -I\), \(\|V\|^2 \le \pi^2n\); so \(V^2 = -\pi^2I\). \(\square\)

Lemma 24.4 (iii) [V15.26]. Let \(J_1, \dots, J_k\) be an anticommuting family with base point \(J_k\) (\(J_0 = I\)). (i) \(A \in \mathcal C_{J_k}\) iff \(J_kA \in \Omega_{k+1}(n)\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalmem_minVelO_iff; \(A \mapsto J_kA\) is a homeomorphism \(\mathcal C_{J_k} \to \Omega_{k+1}(n)\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalminVelOHomeomorph; and \(\gamma_A(t) = \cos(\pi t)J_k + \sin(\pi t)J'\) for \(A = J_k^{\mathsf T}J'\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalomegaGeo_eq_semicircle. (ii) In the setting of V15.25, \(A \mapsto \gamma_A\) is a homotopy equivalence \(\mathcal C_p \simeq \Omega^d(N; p, -p)\) Chapter15/OmegaMinimalomegaMinPathsHomotopyEquiv. (iii) If \(J_1, \dots, J_{k+1}\) is an anticommuting family and \(N\) the stratum through \(J_k\), \(\varphi(J')(t) = \cos(\pi t)J_k + \sin(\pi t)J'\) defines a continuous \(\varphi : \Omega_{k+1}(n) \to \Omega(N; J_k, -J_k)\) Chapter15/FiniteStageomegaPhi, the inclusion \(\Omega^d \to \Omega\) composed with a homotopy equivalence Chapter15/FiniteStageisHomotopyEquiv_omegaPhi_minPaths.

Proof. (i) For \(k = 0\), \(\mathcal T_I = \mathfrak o(n)\) and V15.1; for \(k \ge 1\), V15.7 both ways. (ii) The \(\gamma_A\) have constant speed, so \(A \mapsto \gamma_A\) is continuous [V10.1, §7.1]. The midpoint map \(\omega \mapsto p^{\mathsf T}\omega(\frac12)\) is a continuous left inverse on \(\Omega^d\); the other composite is at distance \(0\) from the identity, hence homotopic to it, a map at distance \(0\) from a continuous one being continuous Chapter10/DeformationPathSp.continuous_of_edist_eq_zero. \(\square\)

Theorem (the retraction) [V15.27]. In the setting of V15.25, let \(Y_1\) be the orthogonal projection of \(p^{\mathsf T}Y\) onto \(\mathcal T_p\); if \(\det(Y_1^{\mathsf T}Y_1) \ne 0\), \(Y_1(Y_1^{\mathsf T}Y_1)^{-1/2} \in \mathcal C_p\) Chapter15/OmegaRetractpolarDir_mem. The paths \(\omega\) with \(\det(Y_1^{\mathsf T}Y_1) \ne 0\) for \(Y = \omega(\frac12)\) form an open \(O \supseteq \Omega^d\) Chapter15/OmegaRetractisOpen_omegaNbhd, and some \(\rho\), continuous on \(O\), maps \(O\) into \(\Omega^d\) and is the identity on \(\Omega^d\) Chapter15/OmegaRetractexists_retraction_minPaths_omega.

Proof. \(S = Y_1^{\mathsf T}Y_1 = -Y_1^2\) commutes with \(Y_1\), \(p\) and the \(J_\alpha\), hence so does \(S^{-1/2}\) (functional calculus); so \(Y_1S^{-1/2} \in \mathcal T_p\), of square \(-I\). On \(\Omega^d\), \(Y_1 = A\). Put \(\rho(\omega) = \gamma_{Y_1S^{-1/2}}\) off \(\Omega^d\), \(\rho = \mathrm{id}\) on \(\Omega^d\): it is at distance \(0\) from a continuous map. \(\square\)

10.5 Index bounds from Killing fields

Theorem (Killing fields) [V15.28]. Let \(J_1, \dots, J_k\) be an anticommuting family, \(p \in \Omega_k(n)\), \(N\) the stratum through \(p\), \(V \in \mathcal T_p\), and \(\mathfrak i_p\) the space of skew \(X\) commuting with \(p\) and the \(J_\alpha\), \(\alpha < k\) Chapter15/OmegaKillingisoAlg. (i) For \(X \in \mathfrak i_p\), \(K(t) = X\gamma(t) - \gamma(t)X\) is a Jacobi field along \(\gamma(t) = p\exp(tV)\) in \(N\) Chapter15/OmegaKillingisJacobiField_killing. (ii) Let \(\gamma \in \Omega(N; p, q)\) be an unbroken geodesic equal to \(p\exp(tV)\) on \([0, 1]\), \(\tau \in [0, 1]\), and \(\mathcal X \subseteq \mathfrak i_p\) a subspace whose elements commute with \(\exp(\tau V)\) and whose non-zero elements do not commute with \(V\). Then \(\gamma(\tau)\) is conjugate to \(\gamma(0)\) with multiplicity \(\ge \dim\mathcal X\) Chapter15/OmegaKillingfinrank_le_conjMultiplicity. (iii) For finite \(T \subseteq (0, 1)\) and such \(\mathcal X_\tau\) (\(\tau \in T\)), the index of \(\gamma\) is \(\ge \sum_{\tau \in T}\dim\mathcal X_\tau\) Chapter15/OmegaKillingsum_finrank_le_formIndex.

Proof. (i) With \(g = \exp(uX)\), \(g\,p\exp(tV)g^{-1} = p\exp(t\,gVg^{-1})\), \(gVg^{-1} \in \mathcal T_p\): a variation through geodesics; Lemma 14.3 [V9.8, §6.4] Chapter9/JacobiVariationlemma_14_3. (ii) \(K(0) = 0 = K(\tau)\), and \(K \equiv 0\) forces \(K'(0) = p(XV - VX) = 0\): \(X \mapsto K\) is injective. (iii) The index theorem [V9.24, §6.5] Chapter9/IndexTheoremtheorem_15_1. \(\square\)

Lemma (the splitting) [V15.29]. On a finite-dimensional real inner product space \(E\): (i) if each member of \(\mathcal G\) is self- or skew-adjoint Chapter15/InvariantSplittingIsStarSigned, every invariant \(U\) is spanned by pairwise orthogonal minimal invariant Chapter15/InvariantSplittingIsMinInvar subspaces of \(U\), of total dimension \(\dim U\) Chapter15/InvariantSplittingexists_minInvar_decomp; a self-adjoint operator commuting with \(\mathcal G\) and preserving a minimal invariant \(M\) is scalar on \(M\) Chapter15/InvariantSplittingIsMinInvar.exists_scalar. (ii) Let \(A\) be skew-adjoint, \(J, J_1, \dots, J_{k-1}\) skew-adjoint, pairwise anticommuting, of square \(-1\), with \(AJ = -JA\), \(AJ_\alpha = J_\alpha A\) (for \(k = 0\): \(J = 1\), no \(J_\alpha\)) Chapter15/SplittingCliffordIsOmegaOps, and \(\mathcal G = \{A, J, J_\alpha\}\). On a minimal invariant \(M\), \(A^2 = -c\) Chapter15/SplittingCliffordIsOmegaOps.exists_sq_eq; if \(s^2c = 1\), the restrictions of \(J_1, \dots, J_{k-1}, J, sJA\) satisfy the relations of \(C_{k+1}\) and \(M\) is minimal for them Chapter15/SplittingCliffordIsOmegaOps.isClifford_cliffFam Chapter15/SplittingCliffordIsOmegaOps.isMinimal_cliffFam. For a skew matrix \(A\) with \(\exp(\pi A) = -I\) and \(A^2 = -c\) on a non-zero subspace, \(c \ge 1\) Chapter15/IndexBoundone_le_of_minInvar. (iii) If \(k \le 7\), \(k \not\equiv 2 \pmod 4\), and \(A^2 = -a_0^2\), \(-b^2\) on minimal invariant \(M_0\), \(M_1\) (\(a_0, b > 0\)), some linear isomorphism \(T : M_0 \to M_1\) commutes with \(J\), \(J_\alpha\) and carries \(a_0^{-1}JA\) to \(-b^{-1}JA\) Chapter15/SplittingDataIsOmegaOps.exists_inter. (iv) If moreover \(c \ge 1\) on every minimal invariant subspace and \(A^2 \ne -1\), some piece of a splitting has \(c > 1\) Chapter15/SplittingDataIsOmegaOps.exists_piece_gt; and for \(r_0 = 1\) (or \(2\) if \(k = 0\)) there are \(s\) with \((s + 1)m_{k+1} = \dim E\), \(a_0 > 1\), \(b_1, \dots, b_s \ge 1\), operators \(D_{j,l}\) (\(l < r_0\)) commuting with \(J\), \(J_\alpha\) and intertwining \((A; a_0, b_j)\): \(b_jDA = -a_0AD\), \(A^2D = -b_j^2D\), \(DA^2 = -a_0^2D\); and operators \(R\), \(Q_j\) with \(D_{j,l}R = D_{j,l}\), \(D_{j,l}^*R = 0\), \(Q_jAD_{i,l} = \delta_{ij}AD_{i,l}\), the \(AD_{j,l}\) (\(l < r_0\)) independent Chapter15/SplittingDataIsOmegaOps.exists_omegaPieceData.

Proof. (i) Complements of invariant subspaces are invariant; induct on the dimension. Eigenspaces of \(S\) in \(M\) are invariant. (ii) \(-A^2\) is self-adjoint and commutes with \(\mathcal G\); \((JA)^2 = A^2\); and \(A = -s^{-1}J(sJA)\). For \(c \ge 1\), the matrix whose columns are all an eigenvector has \((\pi A)^2E = -\pi^2cE\): V15.24. (iii) By (ii) with \(s = a_0^{-1}\), resp. \(-b^{-1}\), and Lemma 24.8. (iv) Otherwise \(A^2 = -1\) on the span \(E\) of the pieces. Take \(M_0\) with \(c_0 = a_0^2 > 1\), \(T_j : M_0 \to M_j\) from (iii), \(R\), \(Q_j\) the projections onto \(M_0\), \(M_j\), \(D_{j,l} = \iota_jT_j\pi_0A^l\); pieces have dimension \(m_{k+1}\) (Lemma 24.8). \(\square\)

Theorem (the index, \(k \not\equiv 2 \pmod 4\)) [V15.30]. If \(D\) intertwines \((A; a, b)\) Chapter15/OmegaIntertwinersIsInterRel, \(a, b > 0\) and \(s(a + b) = 2\pi\), then \(D\) commutes with \(\exp(sA)\) Chapter15/OmegaIntertwinersIsInterRel.commute_exp. For skew \(A\) and \(a_0\), \(b_j\), \(D_{j,l}\), \(R\), \(Q_j\) as in V15.29 (iv) with \(D_{j,l} - D_{j,l}^{\mathsf T} \in \mathfrak i_p\), there are \(\mathcal X_\tau\) as in V15.28 (iii) for \(V = \pi A\), of total dimension \(r_0s\) Chapter15/OmegaIntertwinersexists_killing_spaces Chapter15/IndexBoundexists_killing_spaces_omega. Now let \(J_1, \dots, J_k\) be an anticommuting family with \(\mathcal C_{J_k} \ne \emptyset\), \(k \le 7\), \(k \not\equiv 2 \pmod 4\), \(N\) the stratum through \(J_k\). Every unbroken geodesic in \(\Omega(N; J_k, -J_k)\) not of least energy has index \(\ge r_0s\), where \((s + 1)m_{k+1} = n\) Chapter15/IndexBoundle_formIndex_of_not_minimal_omega; for an anticommuting family \(J_1, \dots, J_{k+1}\), index \(\ge r_0(n/m_{k+1} - 1)\) Chapter15/FiniteStageomega_hidx.

Proof. \(D\exp(sA) = \cos(as)D + a^{-1}\sin(as)DA = \cos(as)D - b^{-1}\sin(as)AD\), which is \(\exp(sA)D\) when \(as = 2\pi - bs\). Count: \(X_{j,l} = D_{j,l} - D_{j,l}^{\mathsf T}\) commutes with \(\exp(\tau_j\pi A)\), \(\tau_j = 2/(a_0 + b_j) \in (0, 1)\), as \(D^{\mathsf T}\) intertwines backwards. Right multiplication by \(R\) kills the \(D^{\mathsf T}\)-terms of \([A, X_{j,l}]\), leaving a non-zero multiple of \(AD_{j,l}\), and \(Q_j\) isolates \(j\): the \([A, X_{j,l}]\) are independent. Bound: the geodesic is \(J_k\exp(tV)\) on \([0, 1]\), \(V \in \mathcal T_{J_k}\), \(\exp V = -I\); \(A = V/\pi\) has \(A^2 \ne -I\), as otherwise the energy \(\|V\|^2 = \pi^2n\) is least. Apply V15.29 to the operators \(A\), \(J_k\), \(J_\alpha\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), the count and V15.28. \(\square\)

Let \(J_1, \dots, J_{k+1}\) be an anticommuting family, \(k \le 7\), \(k \not\equiv 2 \pmod 4\), \(N\) the stratum of \(\Omega_k(n)\) through \(J_k\), \(r_0 = 1\) (or \(2\) if \(k = 0\)), \(i + 2 \le r_0(n/m_{k+1} - 1)\).
