Theorem 24.3 [V15.32]. Let \(J_1\) be a complex structure on \(\mathbb R^n\), \(i + 4 \le n\), \(N\) the stratum of \(I\) in \(O(n)\). For every \(J' \in \Omega_1(n)\), \(\varphi : \Omega_1(n) \to \Omega(N; I, -I)\), \(\varphi(J)(t) = \cos(\pi t)I + \sin(\pi t)J\), is bijective on \(\pi_i\) at \(J'\), and \(\pi_i(\Omega_1(n), J') \cong \pi_{i+1}(O(n), I)\) Chapter15/FiniteStagetheorem_24_3. 10.7 The case \(k = 2, 6\)

Angles [V15.33]. Let \(F : \mathbb E \to \mathbb C\) (\(\mathbb E\) Euclidean) and \(\omega : \mathbb R \to \mathbb E\). A continuous \(\theta : [0, 1] \to \mathbb R\) is the angle of \(F \circ \omega\) if \(\theta(0) = 0\) and \(F\omega(t) = e^{i\theta(t)}\) on \([0, 1]\) Chapter15/WindingIsAngleLift; it is unique Chapter15/WindingIsAngleLift.unique. If \(F\omega\), \(F\omega'\) are continuous of modulus \(1\) on \([0, 1]\), \(|F\omega' - F\omega| < 1\), \(F\omega'(0) = F\omega(0)\) and \(\theta\) is the angle of \(F\omega\), then \(F\omega'\) has an angle, ending at \(\theta(1)\) if \(F\omega'(1) = F\omega(1)\) Chapter15/WindingIsAngleLift.perturb. Let \(\Omega_w \subseteq \Omega(N; p, q)\) be the paths whose angle ends at \(w\) Chapter15/WindingwindSet. If \(F\) is continuous and \(|F| = 1\) on a compact \(K \supseteq N\), every \(\Omega_w\) is open and closed Chapter15/WindingisClopen_windSet.

Proof. \(\mathbb R \to S^1\) is a covering Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex/CircleCircle.isCoveringMap_exp. \(\theta' = \theta + \arg(F\omega'/F\omega)\), the quotient having positive real part. Paths close for Milnor’s metric are uniformly close [V10.1, §7.1], and \(F\) is uniformly continuous on \(K\); so a path near \(\omega\) lies in \(\Omega_w\) iff \(\omega\) does. \(\square\)

\(\det_{\mathbb C}\) [V15.34]. Proof. \(P_\pm\) are complementary idempotents commuting with \(N_{\mathbb C}\); \(\overline{\det_{\mathbb C}M} = \det_{\mathbb C}M^{\mathsf T}\); \(\exp(tV)_{\mathbb C}P_+ + P_- = \exp(tV_{\mathbb C}P_+)\), Jacobi’s formula, and \(\operatorname{tr}(V_{\mathbb C}P_+) = \frac12(\operatorname{tr}V - \sqrt{-1}\operatorname{tr}(V\mathbf i))\). \(\square\)

Proof. \(D\exp(sA) = \cos(as)D + \sin(as)D\mathbf i\), \(\exp(sA)D = \cos(bs)D + \sin(bs)\mathbf iD\); multiply by \(\mathbf i\). If \(a_0 = a_{h_0} \ge 3\): for each piece with \(a_j < 0\), V15.37 (iv) gives \(D_j\), and \(X_j = D_j\mathbf i - (D_j\mathbf i)^{\mathsf T} \in \mathfrak i_{J_k}\) commutes with \(\exp(\tau\pi A)\) at the \((a_0 - a_j)/2 - 1\) values \(\tau = 2l/(a_0 - a_j) \in (0, 1)\); the \([X_j, A]\) are independent Chapter15/KillingTwoexists_killing_spaces_two. As \((a_0 - a_j)/2 - 1 \ge (|a_j| + 1)/2\) and \(2\sum_{a_j < 0}|a_j| = \sum|a_h| - c \ge \nu - c\), the count is \(\ge (\nu - c)/4\) Chapter15/SplittingTwoDataexists_twoPieceData_of_decomp. If \(a_{h_0} \le -3\), use \(-A\), \(-c\). Then V15.28 (iii). \(\square\)

Theorem 24.5 at a finite stage, \(k = 2, 6\) [V15.39]. Let \(J_1, \dots, J_{k+1}\) be an anticommuting family. For \(k = 2, 6\), \(\mathbf i = J_1\cdots J_{k-1}\) is central Chapter15/FiniteStageTwoisCentralI_iWordM. If \(\mathbf i\) is central, \(\varphi(J') \in \Omega_w\), \(w = -\pi\operatorname{tr}(J_k^{\mathsf T}J'\mathbf i)/2\) Chapter15/FiniteStageTwoomegaPhi_mem_omegaComp. If moreover \(1 \le k \le 7\), \(k \not\equiv 3 \pmod 4\), \(j + 3 \le \lfloor(n/m_{k+1} - |c|)/4\rfloor\) and \(\varphi(J') \in \Omega^{(c)}\), then \(\varphi\) is bijective on \(\pi_{j+1}\) at \(J'\) Chapter15/FiniteStageTwoomegaPhi_bijective_two and \(\pi_{j+1}(\Omega_{k+1}(n), J') \cong \pi_{j+2}(\Omega_k(n), J_k)\) Chapter15/FiniteStageTwoomega_pi_equiv_two.

Proof. \(\varphi(J') = J_k\exp(t\pi J_k^{\mathsf T}J')\) (V15.26) and V15.35. \(\varphi = (\Omega^d \to \Omega) \circ e\), \(e\) a homotopy equivalence, \(e(J') \in \Omega^{(c)}\); with V15.35 and V15.38, \(\Omega^d \to \Omega\) is bijective on \(\pi_{j+1}\) at \(e(J')\) [V13.16, §8.3] Chapter13/Componentwisetheorem_22_1_clopen_bijective_minPathsIncl. Then \(\pi_{j+1}(\Omega(N; p, q), \omega) \cong \pi_{j+2}(N, p)\) [V13.5, §8.4] Chapter13/CorollaryGroupsnonempty_mulEquiv_pathSp, and V15.31 for \(N\). \(\square\)

10.8 \(\Omega_8(16r) \cong O(r)\) and Theorem 24.7

The structures on \(\mathbb R^{16r} = \mathbb R^{16} \otimes \mathbb R^r\) [V15.41]. \(J_\alpha = J'_\alpha \oplus \dots \oplus J'_\alpha\) Chapter15/BottChainbottJ form an anticommuting family of eight Chapter15/BottChainisAnticommFamily_bottJ, and \(\varphi(J_{k+1}) \in \Omega^{(0)}\) for \(k = 2, 6\) Chapter15/BottChainomegaPhi_bottJ_mem_omegaComp. Proof: by V15.39 it suffices that \(\operatorname{tr}(J_k^{\mathsf T}J_{k+1}\mathbf i) = r\operatorname{tr}(J'^{\mathsf T}_kJ'_{k+1}\mathbf i') = 0\); this Kronecker word has a traceless letter in some slot Chapter15/BottChaintrace_bott16_six. \(\square\)

Lemma 24.6 (8) [V15.42]. (i) A \(16 \times 16\) matrix commuting with \(J'_1, \dots, J'_7\) is \(bI + cW\), \(W = 1 \otimes 1 \otimes 1 \otimes \tau\) Chapter15/EightCommutanteq_of_commute_bott16. (ii) With \(P_\pm = \frac12(1 \pm W)\), every matrix commuting with \(J_1, \dots, J_7\) is \(q(U, V) = P_+ \otimes U + P_- \otimes V\) for some \(U, V \in M_r(\mathbb R)\) Chapter15/OmegaEighteq_qOf_of_commute. (iii) \(J \mapsto U\), where \(-J_8J = q(U, U^{\mathsf T})\), is a homeomorphism \(\Omega_8(16r) \to O(r)\) with inverse \(U \mapsto J_8q(U, U^{\mathsf T})\) Chapter15/OmegaEightomegaEightHomeomorph, sending \(J_8\) to \(I\) Chapter15/OmegaEightomegaEightHomeomorph_basePt.

Proof. (i) The \(256\) Kronecker words in \(1, \sigma, \tau, \kappa\) form an orthogonal basis; \(X = -J'_\alpha XJ'_\alpha\) kills the coefficients of words anticommuting with \(J'_\alpha\), and a finite check leaves \(1\) and \(W\) Chapter15/EightCommutanteq_of_not_wanti. (ii) Block by block. (iii) \(Q = -J_8J\) commutes with \(J_1, \dots, J_7\), so \(Q = q(U, V)\), \(U, V\) orthogonal. \(J_8q(U, V) = q(V, U)J_8\) Chapter15/OmegaEighteight_qOf, so \(J^2 = -I\) reads \(q(VU, UV) = I\): \(V = U^{\mathsf T}\). Conversely \(J_8q(U, U^{\mathsf T}) \in \Omega_8(16r)\). \(\square\)

Bott’s chain [V15.43]. For \(2i + 7 \le r\): \(\pi_i(\Omega_8(16r), J_8) \cong \pi_{i+8}(O(16r), I)\) Chapter15/StablePeriodicitybott_chain_of_le and \(\pi_i(O(r), I) \cong \pi_{i+8}(O(16r), I)\) Chapter15/StablePeriodicitybott_periodicity_finite_of_le.

Proof. \(n/m_{k+1}\) is \(r\) for \(k = 7\), \(2r\) for \(3 \le k \le 6\), \(4r\) for \(k = 1, 2\). Steps at the base points, with their ranges: \(k = 7\) (V15.31), \(\pi_i\Omega_8 \cong \pi_{i+1}\Omega_7\), \(i + 2 \le r - 1\); \(k = 6\) (V15.39 with \(c = 0\), V15.41), \(\pi_{i+1}\Omega_7 \cong \pi_{i+2}\Omega_6\), \(i + 3 \le \lfloor r/2\rfloor\); \(k = 5, 4, 3\) (V15.31), \(i + 6 \le 2r - 1\); \(k = 2\) (V15.39), \(\pi_{i+5}\Omega_3 \cong \pi_{i+6}\Omega_2\), \(i + 7 \le r\); \(k = 1\), \(i + 8 \le 4r - 1\); \(k = 0\) (V15.32), \(\pi_{i+7}\Omega_1 \cong \pi_{i+8}O(16r)\), \(i + 11 \le 16r\). Then V15.42. \(\square\)

Theorem 24.7 [V15.45]. For every \(i \ge 0\), \(n \ge i + 2\), \(n' \ge i + 10\), there is a bijection \(\pi_i(O(n), I) \cong \pi_{i+8}(O(n'), I)\) Chapter15/StablePeriodicitytheorem_24_7.

Proof. With \(r = 2i + 7\): \(\pi_iO(n) \cong \pi_iO(r)\) by stability [V15.44, §9.6]; \(\cong \pi_{i+8}O(16r)\) (V15.43, after renaming coordinates Chapter15/StablePeriodicityHomotopy.piUnitaryCongr); \(\cong \pi_{i+8}O(n')\) by [V15.44, §9.6], as \(i + 10 \le 16r, n'\). \(\square\)

Appendix B. What is left out

The results of the verified edition that no main theorem uses: none of their declarations is on the path. They are true and machine-checked, and many are interesting, but the main theorems do not need them. Grouped by the chapter of the verified edition (the Milnor sections in brackets).
